expr2tc &expr);\n88\t  int get_total_instrument() const;\n89\t  int get_total_assert_instance() const;\n90\t  std::set<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> get_total_cond_assert() const;\n91\t  std::string get_filename_from_path(std::string path);\n92\t  void set_target(const std::string &_tgt);\n93\t  bool is_target_func(const irep_idt &f, const std::string &tgt_name) const;\n94\t  bool\n95\t  filter(const irep_idt &func_name, const goto_programt &goto_program) const;\n96\t\n97\t  // total numbers of instrumentation\n98\t  static size_t total_assert;\n99\t  static size_t total_assert_ins;\n100\t  static std::set<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> total_cond;\n101\t  static size_t total_branch;\n102\t  static size_t total_func_branch;\n103\t  static size_t total_kpath;\n104\t  // |spanning_set| under Marré-Bertolino subsumption (issue #4335 PR1).\n105\t  // Equals total_kpath when no goal is subsumed by another. Used as the\n106\t  // denominator of the k-path coverage percentage to drop the lower\n107\t  // bound contribution of redundant subsumed goals.\n108\t  static size_t total_kpath_spanning;\n109\t  // (msg, loc) pairs whose every emission is non-maximal. JSON report\n110\t  // marks these as \"spanning-set-redundant\" and they are excluded from\n111\t  // the spanning-set denominator.\n112\t  static std::set<std::pair<std::string, std::string>>\n113\t    k_path_spanning_redundant;\n114\t  // all instrumented claims (condition, location) for JSON report.\n115\t  // For branch coverage this is the *static universe* (every in-scope\n116\t  // decision edge, built with NO covered-set skip applied) so the\n117\t  // denominator never shrinks when edges are skipped (Item 2c).\n118\t  static std::set<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> all_claims;\n119\t\n120\t  // Cross-run persisted covered-set (Item 2). covered_set holds the\n121\t  // (guard_str, location.as_string()) edge keys loaded from the JSON at\n122\t  // branch_coverage() entry; an edge present here is NOT re-instrumented\n123\t  // this run (its assert pair is skipped) but still counted in the\n124\t  // denominator via all_claims. covered_set_outpath, when non-empty, is\n125\t  // where bmc.cpp merge-writes the accumulated set at run end. Static so\n126\t  // the run-end report path (bmc.cpp) can read them like total_branch /\n127\t  // all_claims.\n128\t  static std::set<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> covered_set;\n129\t  static std::string covered_set_outpath;\n130\t\n131\t  // ---- Complete-path coverage: CONTENT-ADDRESSED cross-run path keys ----\n132\t  //\n133\t  // Branch coverage keys an edge by (condition text, location) — content\n134\t  // addressed already. Complete-path coverage used to key a path by its ordinal\n135\t  // `enc`, which is a position in one particular enumeration. That is unsafe\n136\t  // across runs: the decision set has changed three times (short-circuit\n137\t  // operands, the ABI non-payable gate, internal-call expansion), and each\n138\t  // change RENUMBERS every path. A key witnessed under one numbering then\n139\t  // silently designates a DIFFERENT path under the next, so a path can be\n140\t  // skipped as \"already covered\" when nothing has covered it — no crash, no\n141\t  // warning, coverage simply reads low. An ordinal key cannot be made safe;\n142\t  // it has to be replaced.\n143\t  //\n144\t  // The stable key is the decision SEQUENCE itself:\n145\t  //     unit signature, then per decision (site, polarity, occurrence index)\n146\t  // where `site` is the decision's SOURCE LOCATION (plus its operand index, for\n147\t  // several folded short-circuit operands sharing one location) rather than any\n148\t  // serial number. Enumeration order, added decisions elsewhere, and a changed\n149\t  // unit set then leave a path's key untouched: an old key either matches\n150\t  // exactly or does not match at all — it can never designate a different path.\n151\t  //\n152\t  // `path_covered_ids` holds the ids loaded from the previous run;\n153\t  // `path_stable_id` maps this run's claim key -> its stable id so the run-end\n154\t  // write-back can record exactly the paths that were witnessed.\n155\t  static std::set<std::string> path_covered_ids;\n156\t  static std::map<std::pair<std::string, std::string>, std::string>\n157\t    path_stable_id;\n158\t  static std::string path_covered_outpath;\n159\t\n160\t  // Fail-closed guard for the file above. The stable key protects against\n161\t  // RE-NUMBERING; it cannot protect against a change that alters what a path IS\n162\t  // (different source, a decision kind added to the set, a different loop or\n163\t  // recursion bound). This fingerprint covers exactly those, and a mismatch\n164\t  // DISCARDS the cache and recomputes — deliberately with no migration path,\n165\t  // because migration logic is where this class of silent error hides.\n166\t  static std::string path_cov_fingerprint;\n167\t\n168\t  // Serialise the complete-path covered set + its fingerprint (atomic publish,\n169\t  // same .tmp-then-rename discipline as write_covered_set_atomic). No-op when\n170\t  // no --coverage-covered-set was given.\n171\t  static void write_path_covered_set_atomic();\n172\t\n173\t  // Was this claim's path already witnessed in an EARLIER round?\n174\t  //\n175\t  // Complete-path coverage does NOT use `covered_set` — that is the branch\n176\t  // metric's (condition, location) pair set, and solidity_path_coverage()\n177\t  // deliberately leaves it empty because an ordinal-keyed pair cannot survive a\n178\t  // re-numbering. The cross-run identity here is the content-addressed stable\n179\t  // id, so the test has to go through path_stable_id -> path_covered_ids.\n180\t  //\n181\t  // Getting this wrong is not cosmetic: a path skipped because a previous round\n182\t  // already witnessed it has NO verdict this run, so reading `covered_set`\n183\t  // (always empty) reports it as U — a path with a counterexample in hand,\n184\t  // filed under \"we could not decide\". Measured: with --coverage-covered-set\n185\t  // the file was never even written, so the whole cross-run mechanism was dead\n186\t  // in both directions.\n187\t  static bool\n188\t  path_witnessed_earlier(const std::pair<std::string, std::string> &claim_key);\n189\t\n190\t  // ---- U REASON TOKEN: why is this path not witnessed? ----\n191\t  //\n192\t  // U is a FIRST-CLASS DELIVERABLE, not an internal diagnostic. The claim being\n193\t  // made is \"every uncovered path carries a named reason; there is no\n194\t  // unexplained remainder\". A U cell that can also absorb an implementation\n195\t  // defect makes that claim false — and it has absorbed one three times already\n196\t  // (ordinal-key mismatch, the RETURN exit, `rawBalances`). Each time the broken\n197\t  // case was indistinguishable from an honest solver timeout, because \"we do not\n198\t  // know\" is a legitimate, expected outcome.\n199\t  //\n200\t  // So every U must be classifiable, and a U that is not is a HARD FAILURE\n201\t  // rather than a quiet residue. The tokens:\n202\t  //\n203\t  //   named-obstacle      the unit is disqualified (the model admits an\n204\t  //                       execution the chain does not have). Not an unknown at\n205\t  //                       all — a declared exclusion that no verdict can change.\n206\t  //   bounded-holds       the solver proved no witness AT THIS EXPLORATION.\n207\t  //                       Honest and precise: it is not \"unreachable\", it is\n208\t  //                       \"no witness within the declared tx/unwind bound from\n209\t  //                       the post-constructor entry state\".\n210\t  //   solver-unknown      the solver returned UNKNOWN/error, or an inductive\n211\t  //                       step could not prove it. The genuine \"we do not know\".\n212\t  //   not-solved-this-run the claim was instrumented but never reached the\n213\t  //                       solver. The entry-liveness audit catches the case\n214\t  //                       where a WHOLE unit is in this state; this token is\n215\t  //                       exactly the per-claim residue it cannot see.\n216\t  //   unit-not-entered    the harness never entered this path's unit, so no\n217\t  //                       classification of the path itself means anything.\n218\t  //\n219\t  // ORDER MATTERS, and `unit-not-entered` must sit SECOND — directly under\n220\t  // named-obstacle and ABOVE the two tokens that would otherwise swallow it:\n221\t  //\n222\t  //   * a unit that is entered but whose claims hold vacuously gets verdict 'P'\n223\t  //     and would be filed `bounded-holds` — \"no witness within the bound\",\n224\t  //     which is a statement about the path when the truth is that nothing ran;\n225\t  //   * a unit whose claims were never generated at all (measured on a real\n226\t  //     benchmark: 120166 instrumented paths, ZERO verification conditions) has\n227\t  //     no verdict and would be filed `not-solved-this-run`.\n228\t  //\n229\t  // Both are strictly less informative than the real reason, so putting them\n230\t  // first loses the one fact worth having. The ordering rule is the same one\n231\t  // that puts named-obstacle at the top: when the unit is disqualified, or was\n232\t  // never entered, every finer classification of its paths is meaningless.\n233\t  //\n234\t  // This is NOT a reserved slot — it fires today. With --focus-function the\n235\t  // audit deliberately does not abort for the units the narrowing excluded, so\n236\t  // their paths reach the report; measured before the ordering was fixed, they\n237\t  // were all reported `not-solved-this-run` on a run whose own log line one\n238\t  // line earlier said the unit had not been entered.\n239\t  //\n240\t  // This is an INVARIANT ASSERTION, not a detector: the live tokens partition\n241\t  // the possible states by construction (a claim's verdict is one of\n242\t  // {none, P, U, F}, and F means witnessed, hence not U). It therefore needs no\n243\t  // fault injection — its value is as a tripwire for a future change that\n244\t  // introduces a U with no reason. THE PARTITION ARGUMENT ONLY HOLDS WHILE THE\n245\t  // CLASSIFICATION HAS NO CATCH-ALL: the implementation's `default` arm returns\n246\t  // \"\" so the caller aborts. Mapping `default` to any token instead would make\n247\t  // the abort dead code while everything still looked fine — do not add one when\n248\t  // a fifth verdict value appears; add an explicit case for it.\n249\t  //\n250\t  // Returns the token, or \"\" when the path is not a U (which callers treat as\n251\t  // the hard failure above).\n252\t  static std::string\n253\t  path_u_reason_token(const std::pair<std::string, std::string> &claim_key);\n254\t\n255\t  // The token names, in report order. Printed in full every time, zeros\n256\t  // included, so a category that stops occurring is visible rather than absent.\n257\t  static const std::vector<std::string> &path_u_reason_tokens();\n258\t\n259\t  // ENTRY-LIVENESS AUDIT — hard-fails when a unit's results are vacuous.\n260\t  //\n261\t  // Measured on a real benchmark (St1inch): 120166 paths were instrumented and\n262\t  // symex generated ZERO verification conditions — the harness never called any\n263\t  // unit. Every path was then reported \"U\", which is indistinguishable from an\n264\t  // honest solver timeout, so a completely empty run looked like a merely hard\n265\t  // one. Nothing crashed and nothing warned; the defect was found by a human\n266\t  // reading a log line.\n267\t  //\n268\t  // Two levels of the same failure, deliberately sharing ONE channel so that\n269\t  // implementing half of it cannot leave the other half silent:\n270\t  //   * a unit whose claims never reached the solver was never entered;\n271\t  //   * zero verification conditions overall is the extreme case of that, where\n272\t  //     EVERY unit was never entered.\n273\t  //\n274\t  // The witness is positive: a claim that produced a solver verdict proves the\n275\t  // unit was executed. Absence of a verdict is not read as \"undecided\" — for a\n276\t  // whole unit it is read as \"this run says nothing about this unit\", which is\n277\t  // a tool failure, not a result. Claims deliberately skipped via the cross-run\n278\t  // covered set are excluded, since not instrumenting them is intentional.\n279\t  //\n280\t  // This is also what currently makes it safe to keep `I` disabled: if\n281\t  // unreachability were ever emitted, a never-entered unit would have every one\n282\t  // of its `assert(tr != enc)` hold vacuously and be reported as PROVEN\n283\t  // INFEASIBLE — the most damaging wrong answer this pass could give. The audit\n284\t  // is the precondition for ever enabling it.\n285\t  // `focus_function` is --focus-function's value, empty when unset. With it set\n286\t  // the dispatcher deliberately calls only that entry, so every OTHER unit is\n287\t  // legitimately never entered and must not be treated as a defect — measured:\n288\t  // the first real use of this audit aborted on exactly that. The premise\n289\t  // (\"a unit with instrumented claims should be entered\") only holds for the\n290\t  // focused unit, so the check is narrowed to where it holds rather than\n291\t  // weakened everywhere.\n292\t  static void audit_entry_liveness(const std::string &focus_function);\n293\t\n294\t  // Units the audit found had claims instrumented but NONE decided, i.e. the\n295\t  // harness never entered them — mapped to WHY, because the two causes are\n296\t  // opposite in nature and must not be collapsed:\n297\t  //\n298\t  //   \"excluded by --focus-function\"  INTENDED and declared. The narrowing says\n299\t  //                                   this unit is not supposed to be entered\n300\t  //                                   in this run; its paths are meant to be\n301\t  //                                   witnessed by the run that focuses on them\n302\t  //                                   and unioned via the covered set. Normal\n303\t  //                                   output, labelled `unit-not-entered`.\n304\t  //   \"harness never entered it\"      A DEFECT. Measured on a real benchmark:\n305\t  //                                   120166 instrumented paths, zero\n306\t  //                                   verification conditions. Hard failure.\n307\t  //\n308\t  // Keeping the reason (rather than a bare set) is what makes this usable BEYOND\n309\t  // token selection. The planned entry-liveness WITNESS — an `assert(false)` at\n310\t  // each unit's body head that must be refuted — has the rule \"not refuted =>\n311\t  // hard failure\", and applying that rule uniformly would abort the moment\n312\t  // anyone passes --focus-function. It must consult this same distinction:\n313\t  // SKIP the check for focus-excluded units, REQUIRE refutation for the rest.\n314\t  // Recording only \"not entered\" would force that layer to rediscover the split.\n315\t  //\n316\t  // Filled by audit_entry_liveness (which runs before any figure is printed).\n317\t  // Today the defect entries never survive to a reader — the audit aborts on\n318\t  // them — but both are recorded so the shape is right when that changes.\n319\t  static std::map<std::string, std::string> units_not_entered;\n320\t\n321\t  // ---- Solidity complete-path coverage: tri-state (F/I/U) reporting ----\n322\t  //\n323\t  // `reached_claims` alone cannot distinguish \"proven unreachable\" from\n324\t  // \"could not decide\": both are simply absent from it. The tri-state\n325\t  // report needs the per-claim solver verdict, so multi_property_check\n326\t  // records it here as it solves (keyed by claim_sig == \"msg\\tloc\"):\n327\t  //   'F' — refuted (P_SATISFIABLE): the path is feasible and a\n328\t  //         counterexample (concrete input) is in hand.\n329\t  //   'P' — proven (P_UNSATISFIABLE) AT THE CURRENT EXPLORATION. This is a\n330\t  //         CANDIDATE for I and nothing more: it means \"no witness within this\n331\t  //         tx/unwind bound, from this entry state\", NOT unreachability.\n332\t  //         NOTHING currently upgrades it. In particular --solidity-max-tx 0\n333\t  //         does NOT: coverage rewrites the dispatcher back-edge to a SKIP, so\n334\t  //         that flag explores ONE transaction — fewer than\n335\t  //         --solidity-max-tx 2. Every 'P' is therefore reported as U with\n336\t  //         `bounded_holds: true`. See path_cov_can_prove_unreachable() in\n337\t  //         bmc.cpp, which is the single place to change if a havoc'd-entry or\n338\t  //         loop-live exploration mode is ever added.\n339\t  //   'U' — undecided: solver UNKNOWN/error, or the inductive step could\n340\t  //         not prove it.\n341\t  // Written under a mutex (--parallel-solving runs jobs on threads).\n342\t  static std::map<std::string, char> claim_outcome;\n343\t  static std::mutex claim_outcome_mutex;\n344\t\n345\t  // Complete paths whose exit is a detected custom-error revert\n346\t  // (`revert E()` reaching a `#sol_error` call). Keyed like all_claims, so\n347\t  // the report can label each path's exit_kind normal|revert. Filled by\n348\t  // solidity_path_coverage() at instrumentation time.\n349\t  static std::set<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> revert_paths;\n350\t\n351\t  // Complete paths that exit through a ROLLBACK revert: `require(cond)` /\n352\t  // `require(cond,\"msg\")` / `revert(\"msg\")` lower to a block that restores the\n353\t  // entry snapshot (`*this = _sol_save_this`) and jumps to END_FUNCTION. These\n354\t  // reach END_FUNCTION like a normal exit, so without this set they would be\n355\t  // reported `exit_kind: \"normal\"` — actively wrong, since the transaction\n356\t  // reverts. Unlike `revert_paths` (custom errors) the rollback IS modelled,\n357\t  // so their post-state is the correctly restored one and needs no warning.\n358\t  static std::set<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> rollback_revert_paths;\n359\t\n360\t  // Paths whose exit shape cannot be classified: they reach END_FUNCTION while\n361\t  // skipping the epilogue and carry no rollback restore. A `require` failing\n362\t  // before any state write and a plain early `return` both compile to exactly\n363\t  // this, with nothing on the edge to separate them. Reported as\n364\t  // `exit_kind: \"undetermined\"` — labelling them \"normal\" would assert that a\n365\t  // reverted transaction succeeded.\n366\t  static std::set<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> undetermined_exit_paths;\n367\t\n368\t  // Complete paths POSITIVELY confirmed to exit normally. The three sets above\n369\t  // say what went wrong; this one says nothing did, and it exists so that no\n370\t  // consumer has to infer normality from absence.\n371\t  //\n372\t  // That inference is not merely inelegant, it is wrong across coverage modes:\n373\t  // a branch-coverage claim appears in none of these sets either, so \"in\n374\t  // all_claims and in no failure set\" calls every branch claim normal. Measured\n375\t  // — it turned three branch-coverage regressions red on the first attempt.\n376\t  //\n377\t  // Only complete-path coverage fills this. Its consumer is the Foundry\n378\t  // emitter, which drops the revert-tolerant try/catch and emits the call bare\n379\t  // when the exit is confirmed normal, so a revert at run time fails the test.\n380\t  // That makes this set the single fact authorising a generated test to assert\n381\t  // anything at all, which is why it is recorded rather than derived.\n382\t  static std::set<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> normal_exit_paths;\n383\t\n384\t  // Paths along which the MODEL AND THE EVM DISAGREE, keyed like all_claims,\n385\t  // with the value naming the obstacle.\n386\t  //\n387\t  // These are not imprecision — they are paths where a counterexample would\n388\t  // describe an execution that does not exist on-chain, so a test built from\n389\t  // one is red when run while being labelled certified. That is the single\n390\t  // failure mode this pipeline must never produce, and it is why the marking is\n391\t  // not merely reported: a marked path must be excluded from the sibling set\n392\t  // used for the stage-3 subtraction AND must not be turned into a test.\n393\t  // Marking without excluding would be worthless.\n394\t  //\n395\t  // Counted and reported as an ABSOLUTE number, never folded into a coverage\n396\t  // ratio: an obstacle is not partial credit.\n397\t  //\n398\t  // Marking is PER PATH, not per unit — a path of the same unit that never\n399\t  // walks the offending site is unaffected and stays fully usable. The rule is\n400\t  // conservative: any path whose decision sequence passes through the site is\n401\t  // marked.\n402\t  static std::map<std::pair<std::string, std::string>, std::string>\n403\t    named_obstacle_paths;\n404\t\n405\t  // Paths whose certified region is NARROWER than it would otherwise be,\n406\t  // because their unit lost paths to the goal cap. Keyed like all_claims.\n407\t  //\n408\t  // This is deliberately NOT named_obstacle_paths, and the reason is mechanical.\n409\t  // Certification is a query — `assume(L <= x <= U); assert(tr == pi)` — and the\n410\t  // goal cap limits only how many EXIT ASSERTS are emitted. Phase-1 accounting\n411\t  // still updates `tr`/`cnt` on every decision of every path, dropped ones\n412\t  // included, so an input that walks a dropped path carries that path's number\n413\t  // at the exit, the query fails on it, and the candidate interval is rejected\n414\t  // and shrunk. The query never needed the dropped path to have been enumerated.\n415\t  //\n416\t  // A `require` lowered to a control-flow-free assume is the opposite case and\n417\t  // stays an obstacle: there the reverting execution does not exist in the model\n418\t  // at all, so no query can see it and no interval can be shrunk away from it.\n419\t  // Existing-but-unenumerated and non-existent are different failures, and only\n420\t  // the second can ship a test that is red on the unmodified contract.\n421\t  static std::map<std::pair<std::string, std::string>, std::string>\n422\t    truncation_weakened;\n423\t\n424\t  // ---- DEGRADATION: which call points a unit gave up to fit its budget ----\n425\t  //\n426\t  // Degradation and TRUNCATION are two different mechanisms with two different\n427\t  // soundness stories, so they get two separate reports and are never merged:\n428\t  //\n429\t  //   * DEGRADATION withdraws call points BEFORE enumeration. The callee stays\n430\t  //     a call, so symex still executes it; it simply stops contributing\n431\t  //     decisions to the caller's path identity. The path classes get COARSER\n432\t  //     but still partition the input space (two different decision sequences\n433\t  //     still differ in polarity at their first differing index; execution is\n434\t  //     still deterministic), so the enumeration stays sound. What is lost is\n435\t  //     assertion STRENGTH, and it is lost at named, reported places rather\n436\t  //     than everywhere.\n437\t  //   * TRUNCATION drops enumerated paths at the goal cap. Those paths exist\n438\t  //     and symex will execute them; they are simply missing from the sibling\n439\t  //     set.\n440\t  //\n441\t  // The order is fixed: degradation fires FIRST, truncation is the last-resort\n442\t  // backstop. In the intended steady state truncation never fires at all — so\n443\t  // if it does fire, that is a result in its own right (the degradation policy\n444\t  // was not aggressive enough for that unit) and is reported as such, never\n445\t  // folded into the degradation report.\n446\t  //\n447\t  // Keyed by unit id; the value names each withdrawn call point (callee plus\n448\t  // the source location of the call), because \"this unit was degraded\" is not\n449\t  // actionable while \"this unit stopped recording the decisions of THIS call\"\n450\t  // is.\n451\t  static std::map<std::string, std::vector<std::string>> degraded_call_sites;\n452\t\n453\t  // The CE payload of a witnessed (F) path: the concrete values that make the\n454\t  // path execute, harvested from the solver model while it is still live.\n455\t  // This is the half of the report a downstream generaliser actually consumes\n456\t  // — a path id alone says \"reachable\", these values say \"with WHAT\".\n457\t  //   inputs      — first nondeterministically-sourced value per symbol\n458\t  //                 (the harness's chosen call arguments / environment)\n459\t  //   final_state — LAST value written to each contract state variable\n460\t  //                 (`this->x`) on this path, i.e. the post-state\n461\t  // Both are recorded ONLY from concrete model values; a symbolic or missing\n462\t  // value is dropped rather than guessed.\n463\t  //\n464\t  // `sliced`/`compact_trace`/`payload_symbols_protected` record HOW the trace\n465\t  // was produced, because all three affect what can be harvested: the symex\n466\t  // slicer keeps only steps the CLAIM depends on, and a path claim's guard\n467\t  // mentions only the ghost accumulators, so state-variable writes would be\n468\t  // sliced away — unless the payload symbols were exempted from slicing\n469\t  // (protect_ce_symbols, which --cov-report-json turns on) or slicing was\n470\t  // switched off entirely. Without these flags an empty final_state would be\n471\t  // ambiguous between \"this path writes no state\" and \"the writes were sliced\n472\t  // away\".\n473\t  struct path_ce_t\n474\t  {\n475\t    // Solidity call arguments only: a nondet-sourced write to a symbol whose\n476\t    // mangled id has the `sol:@C@<C>@F@<f>@<name>` shape. Harness plumbing\n477\t    // (allocator tables, dispatcher choice bits, temporaries) is NOT an input\n478\t    // and is counted in `dropped_internal` instead of polluting this list.\n479\t    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> inputs;\n480\t    // EVM environment the path was witnessed under (msg.*/tx.*/block.*),\n481\t    // kept separate because it is context, not an argument.\n482\t    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> env;\n483\t    // How many nondet values were classified as harness-internal and dropped.\n484\t    // Reported so the omission is visible rather than silent.\n485\t    size_t dropped_internal = 0;\n486\t    // What the external calls on this path RETURNED. Under --unbound the\n487\t    // frontend models an external call as a nondet return plus a nondet\n488\t    // re-entry, so this value is chosen by the model, not by the caller —\n489\t    // keeping it out of `inputs` is the difference between a replayable test\n490\t    // and one that tries to pass an unpassable argument.\n491\t    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> extcall_returns;\n492\t    // Contract state at the moment this path's function was ENTERED. A path\n493\t    // guarded by state that an earlier transaction established is only\n494\t    // reproducible if the entry state is known too.\n495\t    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> entry_storage;\n496\t    // False when the entry marker was not seen in the trace (e.g. the entry\n497\t    // assignment was sliced, or the path was witnessed in an earlier round), so\n498\t    // an empty entry_storage is never read as \"the contract started empty\".\n499\t    bool entry_storage_known = false;\n500\t    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> final_state;\n501\t    // State variables this path provably WROTE but whose value could not be\n502\t    // rendered as a constant (mappings / dynamic arrays lower to infinite-array\n503\t    // globals whose model value is the whole store). Listed by name so the\n504\t    // reader knows the variable changed: omitting them entirely would let a\n505\t    // consumer infer \"unchanged\", which is a silent wrong conclusion.\n506\t    std::vector<std::string> state_written_unrendered;\n507\t    bool sliced = true;\n508\t    bool compact_trace = true;\n509\t    // The symbols this payload is built from (contract objects, contract-scope\n510\t    // mapping/array stores, msg./tx./block.) were registered as no-slice names,\n511\t    // so `sliced == true` here does NOT mean the payload was cut down. This is\n512\t    // what makes an empty `final_state` readable as \"this path writes no state\"\n513\t    // rather than \"the writes were sliced away\".\n514\t    bool payload_symbols_protected = false;\n515\t    // The harvest stopped at this path's own violated assert, so values from\n516\t    // any LATER transaction in a multi-tx harness cannot leak in. False means\n517\t    // the assert was not found in the trace and the whole trace was scanned —\n518\t    // the post-state may then belong to a later transaction.\n519\t    bool scoped_to_claim = false;\n520\t    // This path exits through a custom-error `revert E()`, which the Solidity\n521\t    // frontend lowers to a `#sol_error` callee containing only ASSUME(false)\n522\t    // — with NO state rollback (unlike require/revert(\"msg\"), which restore\n523\t    // `*this` from an entry snapshot). So the harvested post-state is the\n524\t    // state AT THE REVERT POINT, not the EVM post-state (on-chain every write\n525\t    // in the reverted transaction is undone). Reported, never silently used.\n526\t    bool revert_pre_rollback = false;\n527\t  };\n528\t  static std::map<std::string, path_ce_t> path_ce;\n529\t\n530\t  // Each enumerated path's DECISION DEPTH, keyed like all_claims.\n531\t  //\n532\t  // Reported because the next stage cannot be driven without it: every stage-2\n533\t  // query identifies a path by `tr == enc && cnt == depth`, and `enc` alone does\n534\t  // not identify it — the `cnt` conjunct is what stops a longer path whose\n535\t  // 64-bit `tr` wrapped from firing a shorter path's claim. A driver reading\n536\t  // only the report had to be told the depth by hand, which is exactly the kind\n537\t  // of out-of-band knowledge that makes an interface not one.\n538\t  static std::map<std::pair<std::string, std::string>, uint64_t>\n539\t    path_decision_depth;\n540\t\n541\t  // ---- THE ORDERED DECISION SEQUENCE BEHIND A PATH ----\n542\t  //\n543\t  // `path_id` is `enc`, and `enc` is a pure bit accumulator: the k-th decision's\n544\t  // ARM is `(enc >> (depth-k)) & 1` arithmetically, but nothing about the source\n545\t  // location is mixed into it. Which SITE each bit came from is path-dependent\n546\t  // (bit 3 of one path and bit 3 of a sibling come from different instructions\n547\t  // once their prefixes diverge), so no external consumer can recover it from\n548\t  // the report. The information exists only here, during enumeration.\n549\t  //\n550\t  // It is needed for the one comparison this pass has never been able to make:\n551\t  // projecting the witnessed (F) path set onto the DECISIONS those paths walk,\n552\t  // which is the only common denominator with --branch-coverage. Without it the\n553\t  // two metrics cannot be put on one scale at all.\n554\t  //\n555\t  // THE STORAGE IS INTERNED, and that is what makes it affordable. A unit can\n556\t  // enumerate 120166 paths; storing a location string per path per decision is\n557\t  // the reason the pre-existing (log-only) recorder is gated off by default.\n558\t  // Here the DESCRIPTORS live in a per-unit table whose size is the number of\n559\t  // distinct decision sites (tens), and the per-prefix map holds a 32-bit index.\n560\t  //\n561\t  // Keyed by the PREFIX `enc` value the decision produced, so a path's sequence\n562\t  // is read off by walking `enc >> (depth-1)`, `enc >> (depth-2)`, ..., `enc`.\n563\t  // Two paths sharing a prefix share those keys by construction, so one entry\n564\t  // serves every path through it and the map cannot be ambiguous. Polarity is\n565\t  // not stored: it is the key's own low bit.\n566\t  struct path_decisiont\n567\t  {\n568\t    // `location.as_string()`, i.e. exactly the string bmc.cpp's\n569\t    // parse_claim_location() already splits into file/line/column/function.\n570\t    // Deliberately not pre-split here: a second parser is a second thing that\n571\t    // can disagree with the first.\n572\t    std::string loc;\n573\t    // Each arm's claim text, built with the same from_expr/gen_not_expr the\n574\t    // branch metric uses.\n575\t    //\n576\t    // Both arms are published because the mapping is INVERTED and inverting it\n577\t    // in the consumer is a silent, plausible-looking error: a probe assert(P)\n578\t    // fails when P is false, so `assert(guard)` covers the FALL-THROUGH edge and\n579\t    // `assert(!guard)` the GOTO-TAKEN edge. Path polarity TRUE (taken) therefore\n580\t    // corresponds to the claim keyed on the NEGATED guard. Getting it backwards\n581\t    // still produces a number.\n582\t    //\n583\t    // ⚠ IT IS DIAGNOSTIC, NOT A JOIN KEY AGAINST --branch-coverage. MEASURED on\n584\t    // regression/esbmc-solidity/solidity_path_cov_exit_kinds, same contract,\n585\t    // same source line, the two modes report DIFFERENT text for the SAME\n586\t    // decision:\n587\t    //\n588\t    //     branch coverage       \"!(a != 0)\"   /  \"a != 0\"\n589\t    //     path coverage       \"!(!(a != 0))\"  /  \"!(a != 0)\"\n590\t    //\n591\t    // The guards are one `not` apart because --solidity-path-coverage turns on\n592\t    // the revert-observation gate, which lowers `require` to a different goto\n593\t    // shape. A plain `if` agrees exactly (verified on the same run: `v > 1` and\n594\t    // `!(v > 1)` match both sides verbatim), so a text join would work on part\n595\t    // of the corpus and quietly drop every `require` decision on the rest —\n596\t    // producing a lower number with no error.\n597\t    //\n598\t    // A projection onto branch coverage must therefore join on LOCATION, which\n599\t    // is also what the comparison's own metric is defined in terms of (unique\n600\t    // source lines reached, capped at the file's decision count).\n601\t    std::string cond_arm_true;  // polarity 1 (taken)  -> this branch claim\n602\t    std::string cond_arm_false; // polarity 0 (fall-through)\n603\t    // Operand index within the site, for several folded short-circuit operands\n604\t    // sharing one location.\n605\t    unsigned sub = 0;\n606\t    // The synthesised ABI non-payable gate (`msg_value == 0`). It is a decision\n607\t    // of the PATH metric with NO branch-coverage counterpart, and its location\n608\t    // is COPIED from the unit's first body instruction — so a consumer matching\n609\t    // on location alone would credit itself with a real decision sitting on that\n610\t    // line. Flagged at the source rather than left for the consumer to guess\n611\t    // from the condition text.\n612\t    bool synthetic_abi_gate = false;\n613\t  };\n614\t  // unit id -> that unit's interned decision descriptors.\n615\t  static std::map<std::string, std::vector<path_decisiont>> path_decision_table;\n616\t  // unit id -> (prefix enc -> index into the table above).\n617\t  static std::map<std::string, std::map<uint64_t, uint32_t>> path_decision_index;\n618\t\n619\t  // Item 2e: serialize covered_set to covered_set_outpath crash-safely\n620\t  // (write a .tmp then atomic rename). Called both incrementally as\n621\t  // each edge is witnessed P_SATISFIABLE (bmc.cpp) and once at run end,\n622\t  // so a mid-run kill still persists every edge proven so far and\n623\t  // bounded re-runs accumulate monotonically. No-op if outpath empty.\n624\t  static void write_covered_set_atomic();\n625\t\n626\t  // \"data even on UNKNOWN\": an external kill (SIGALRM from esbmc's own\n627\t  // --timeout, or SIGTERM/SIGINT from timeout(1)/CI/orchestrator) lands\n628\t  // mid-solve, so report_coverage (the stdout \"Branch Coverage:\" line,\n629\t  // only reached at a normal conclude/exhaustion point) never runs even\n630\t  // though the numerator is already known. The signal handler reads\n631\t  // this async-signal-safe snapshot and emits a SOUND LOWER BOUND\n632\t  // before _exit. It is EXACT once any report_coverage has run (every\n633\t  // such call re-syncs the active counter to its authoritative value);\n634\t  // between the first per-claim hook and the first report it is a\n635\t  // lower bound. Handler does only atomic loads + write(2); it never\n636\t  // touches the std::set (mid-mutation under SIGALRM).\n637\t  //   branch_cov_active   — set once branch-coverage mode is live\n638\t  //   total_branch_atomic — |all_claims| (denominator), set at\n639\t  //                          instrumentation, pre-solve; mirrors\n640\t  //                          total_branch\n641\t  //   covered_set_mode    — true iff --coverage-covered-set given; it\n642\t  //                          selects which numerator the handler reads\n643\t  //   live_reached        — DEFAULT mode numerator == reached_claims\n644\t  //                          .size() (the canonical bmc.cpp:901 count,\n645\t  //                          which intentionally includes non-universe\n646\t  //                          entries); updated under reached_claims_\n647\t  //                          mutex at the per-claim hook\n648\t  //   covered_run         — COVERED-SET mode numerator == count of\n649\t  //                          universe edges newly witnessed+persisted\n650\t  //                          THIS run (covered_set.emplace().second at\n651\t  //                          the Item 2e hook). A loaded prior set only\n652\t  //                          raises true coverage, so this is a sound\n653\t  //                          lower bound on the covered-set authoritative\n654\t  //                          |all_claims ∩ (covered_set ∪ reached)|.\n655\t  static std::atomic<bool> branch_cov_active;\n656\t  static std::atomic<size_t> total_branch_atomic;\n657\t  static std::atomic<bool> covered_set_mode;\n658\t  static std::atomic<size_t> live_reached;\n659\t  static std::atomic<size_t> covered_run;\n660\t\n661\t  std::string target_function = \"\";\n662\t  bool cov_assume_asserts = false;\n663\t\n664\t  // Context for creating+registering ghost snapshot symbols in\n665\t  // solidity_path_coverage(). namespacet only exposes a const context, so\n666\t  // the pass needs a mutable contextt& to move() new symbols in (pattern:\n667\t  // assign_params_as_non_det / symbol_generator). Set by the dispatch site\n668\t  // (esbmc_parseoptions.cpp) where `context` is available; nullptr => the\n669\t  // pass aborts with an actionable error rather than silently no-op.\n670\t  contextt *cov_context = nullptr;\n671\t  // Per-unit budget on enumerated complete paths (--path-cov-max-goals).\n672\t  // TWO mechanisms are keyed off it, in a fixed order (see\n673\t  // degraded_call_sites): degradation withdraws call points until the unit\n674\t  // fits, and only if that fails does the enumeration truncate at the cap. On\n675\t  // truncation the dropped count is always reported — never a silent cut.\n676\t  size_t path_cov_max_goals = 10000;\n677\t  // Loop bound for path enumeration: each back-edge is followed at most this\n678\t  // many times per path, so complete paths are enumerated up to this many\n679\t  // loop iterations. Set from --unwind by the dispatch (default 4). Must\n680\t  // match the symex unwind bound, or enumerated paths and solver-explored\n681\t  // paths disagree.\n682\t  size_t path_cov_unwind = 4;\n683\t  // When non-empty (set from --contract), branch_coverage() instruments\n684\t  // ONLY decisions whose lexically-declaring Solidity contract equals this\n685\t  // name (location's \"sol_decl_contract\", stamped by the frontend). This\n686\t  // makes per-contract branch coverage count C's own source decisions\n687\t  // only; inherited/library decisions are attributed to their own\n688\t  // declaring contract and excluded. Empty => no scoping (unchanged\n689\t  // whole-unit behaviour, e.g. C/C++/no --contract).\n690\t  std::string scope_contract = \"\";\n691\t\n692\t  // --cov-report-json: the report exists FOR the per-path counterexample\n693\t  // payload (call arguments / EVM environment / post-state). The symex slicer\n694\t  // keeps only what the CLAIM depends on, and a path claim's guard mentions\n695\t  // nothing but the ghost accumulators `tr`/`cnt` — so every contract-state\n696\t  // write and every environment read is sliced out and the payload comes back\n697\t  // empty. When this is set, solidity_path_coverage() registers exactly the\n698\t  // symbols the harvest reads (contract instance objects, contract-scope\n699\t  // mapping/dynamic-array stores, msg./tx./block.) in config.no_slice_names,\n700\t  // ESBMC's existing per-symbol slicing exemption. Slicing itself stays ON, so\n701\t  // the c2goto crypto/ABI tables and the rest of the harness plumbing are\n702\t  // still removed from the formula.\n703\t  bool protect_ce_symbols = false;\n704\t\n705\t  // Record the per-path decision sequence (see path_decision_table). Its own\n706\t  // flag rather than a reuse of protect_ce_symbols: both happen to be set by\n707\t  // --cov-report-json today, but they are different obligations, and keying a\n708\t  // recorder off an unrelated flag's value is how a mechanism ends up silently\n709\t  // disabled by a change to that other flag.\n710\t  bool emit_decision_sites = false;\n711\t\n712\t  // ---- STAGE 2: THE CERTIFICATION QUERY (--path-cov-certify <json>) ----\n713\t  //\n714\t  // Everything downstream of path enumeration rests on ONE query:\n715\t  //     assume(L <= x <= U);  assert(tr == pi)\n716\t  // \"every input in the box walks path pi\". It is what makes certification\n717\t  // immune to goal-cap truncation (the cap drops exit asserts, never the\n718\t  // Phase-1 `tr` accounting, so an input reaching a dropped path still carries\n719\t  // that path's number and the query rejects the box). Until now that argument\n720\t  // lived only in a comment — the query itself had no implementation at all,\n721\t  // which made it the one contributed mechanism no code had ever exercised.\n722\t  //\n723\t  // THE ASSERT GOES ON EVERY EXIT OF THE UNIT, not on pi's exit. An input in\n724\t  // the box that walks a DIFFERENT path leaves through a different exit; with\n725\t  // the assert only on pi's exit it would never be checked and the query would\n726\t  // hold vacuously — a permanently green check in the single place where being\n727\t  // green must mean something. On every exit, that same input hits\n728\t  // `tr == enc` at ITS exit, fails, and the counterexample IS the witness that\n729\t  // shrinks the box.\n730\t  //\n731\t  // Deliberately implemented as a branch at the END of solidity_path_coverage()\n732\t  // rather than a pass of its own: expansion, the ABI gate, Phase-1 accounting,\n733\t  // the `tr`-completeness invariant and both censuses must all still run. They\n734\t  // are the defences, and a certification mode that bypassed them would be\n735\t  // certifying against accounting nobody checked. It also matters that the query\n736\t  // uses the SAME `tr` the enumeration uses — if the two used different\n737\t  // accounting, the immunity-to-truncation argument would not hold.\n738\t  //\n739\t  // Empty => disabled, and the pass behaves exactly as before.\n740\t  std::string path_cov_certify_path = \"\";\n741\t  // Spec for the outer-box batch (see report_outer_boxes). Empty => disabled.\n742\t  std::string path_cov_outer_box_path = \"\";\n743\t\n744\t  // Set by solidity_path_coverage() when a certification query was emitted, so\n745\t  // the reporting side can behave differently WITHOUT re-reading the CLI.\n746\t  static bool path_cov_certify_mode;\n747\t  // The coordinate names the box bounds. Kept because the witness audit below\n748\t  // needs to know what a refutation is obliged to report.\n749\t  static std::vector<std::string> path_cov_certify_box_names;\n750\t  // The box being certified, and the path's own counterexample if the driver\n751\t  // supplied it. Kept so that a REFUTATION can be turned into the next box to\n752\t  // try instead of just a verdict: the witness is the input inside the box that\n753\t  // leaves the path, so the box has to be cut on the witness's side, and the\n754\t  // path's counterexample is what says which side that is. Without both, the\n755\t  // loop has to fall back to blind bisection, which is the search that was\n756\t  // withdrawn.\n757\t  static std::vector<std::array<std::string, 3>> path_cov_certify_box;\n758\t  static std::map<std::string, std::string> path_cov_certify_ce;\n759\t\n760\t  // ---- PUNCHED INTERVALS (Definition 5): R_c = [L, U] \\ H ----\n761\t  //\n762\t  // The values REMOVED from each coordinate's interval. A closed interval alone\n763\t  // cannot express `everything except v`, and that is not a cosmetic loss — it\n764\t  // makes the YIELD depend on an arbitrary solver choice. MEASURED, same\n765\t  // contract, same coordinate, same probes, changing only WHICH counterexample\n766\t  // the sibling happened to return (both legal members of its domain):\n767\t  //\n768\t  //     sibling CE = 2^160-1  ->  region `to in [256, 2^160-1]`  (~1.46e48)\n769\t  //     sibling CE = 0        ->  region `to in [0, 254]`        (255)\n770\t  //\n771\t  // Both are correct — each is a subset of the true domain\n772\t  // `[0,254] U [256, 2^160-1]` — and they differ by a factor of 5.7e45. The\n773\t  // subtraction can only keep the side that contains its own counterexample,\n774\t  // so the side it keeps is decided by a value nobody chose. With a hole, BOTH\n775\t  // cases produce `[0, 2^160-1] \\ {255}` and the counterexample stops mattering.\n776\t  //\n777\t  // A hole is legal under exactly the rule the side cuts already obey: it must\n778\t  // keep a KNOWN member of this path's domain (its own counterexample), and it\n779\t  // only ever makes the region SMALLER. What changes is the cost — removing one\n780\t  // value instead of a whole side.\n781\t  static std::map<std::string, std::vector<std::string>> path_cov_certify_holes;\n782\t\n783\t  // A REFUTATION WITHOUT A WITNESS IS WORTHLESS — hard-fail on one.\n784\t  //\n785\t  // The verdict and the witness fail INDEPENDENTLY, which is what makes this\n786\t  // worth an invariant rather than a comment. Measured: decorating the claim\n787\t  // comment with a `certify:` prefix left the report's `path_function` reading\n788\t  // `certify:sol:@C@Box@F@f#18`, the counterexample harvest builds the expected\n789\t  // argument scope from that string, every nondet failed the scope test and was\n790\t  // filed as harness-internal (dropped 19 -> 25) — and the run still printed a\n791\t  // perfectly correct FAILED verdict with an empty `inputs`.\n792\t  //\n793\t  // The damage is entirely downstream: the refuting INPUT is what the box gets\n794\t  // shrunk with, so a witness-less refutation leaves the generalisation loop\n795\t  // with nothing to do. Its symptom would be \"the loop does not converge\" or\n796\t  // \"the loop collapses to a point\", several hundred lines away from a string\n797\t  // prefix. Checking it here costs one comparison; finding it there costs hours.\n798\t  //\n799\t  // `ce_payload_requested` narrows the check to where its premise holds. The\n800\t  // counterexample payload is only harvested when the report asks for it; a run\n801\t  // that never asked has no witness to be missing, and demanding one there is\n802\t  // the audit accusing the tool of a defect it does not have. MEASURED on this\n803\t  // audit's very first real use — the same false positive the entry-liveness\n804\t  // audit produced on ITS first use (with --focus-function), and the same fix:\n805\t  // narrow to where the premise holds rather than weaken the check everywhere.\n806\t  static void audit_certify_witness(bool ce_payload_requested);\n807\t\n808\t  // ---- STAGE 2, step 1: THE OUTER BOX (--path-cov-outer-box <json>) ----\n809\t  //\n810\t  // The certification query answers \"is this box inside D_pi?\". It does not say\n811\t  // where to look, and the way NOT to find out is to widen from the CE point and\n812\t  // ask again each time — that is a search, it has no terminating condition, and\n813\t  // it sits exactly on the \"too coarse fails / too fine is expensive\" dilemma\n814\t  // that got the widening route withdrawn.\n815\t  //\n816\t  // Instead measure the OUTER box first: `assume(tr == pi); assert(temp_c <= U)`\n817\t  // says D_pi is CONTAINED in the box. Assumption fixed, assertions varied — so\n818\t  // an entire ladder of candidate bounds, for every coordinate and every path,\n819\t  // is judged in ONE run. Then the certified region is computed by SUBTRACTING\n820\t  // the siblings' outer boxes, which costs no query at all: path domains\n821\t  // partition the input space, so an input in nobody else's outer box must walk\n822\t  // this path.\n823\t  //\n824\t  // The ladder's SPAN comes from the sibling counterexamples — a sibling CE at\n825\t  // value v proves the boundary lies between this path's CE and v, so the probes\n826\t  // go there instead of across the whole 256-bit type. The tool does not compute\n827\t  // that span: the driver passes it in, keeping the method abstract and the tool\n828\t  // free of any dependence on its own report format.\n829\t  //\n830\t  // Resolution is stated honestly rather than implied: K non-adaptive probes in\n831\t  // one batch give resolution (hi-lo)/(K+1), NOT log(hi-lo) — that would need K\n832\t  // adaptive rounds. Refining is the driver's job, and each round is one more\n833\t  // batch.\n834\t  struct outer_box_probet\n835\t  {\n836\t    uint64_t enc = 0;\n837\t    std::string coord;\n838\t    bool upper = false; // true: `temp_c <= value`; false: `temp_c >= value`\n839\t    std::string value;\n840\t    std::pair<std::string, std::string> key; // claim key, to read the verdict\n841\t  };\n842\t  static bool path_cov_outer_box_mode;\n843\t  static std::vector<outer_box_probet> path_cov_outer_box_probes;\n844\t  // Every path enumerated for the target unit, as (enc, depth). Needed because\n845\t  // the subtraction is over SIBLINGS, so a path that got no probes still has to\n846\t  // be visible as \"unmeasured\" rather than silently treated as absent.\n847\t  static std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>> path_cov_outer_box_paths;\n848\t  // (enc, coordinate) -> that path's counterexample value on it. Supplied by the\n849\t  // driver from the enumeration run. Needed because a subtraction cut is legal\n850\t  // only if it keeps a KNOWN member of the path's domain; without one there is\n851\t  // nothing to stop the greedy cut from carving away the real region.\n852\t  static std::map<std::pair<uint64_t, std::string>, std::string>\n853\t    path_cov_outer_box_ce;\n854\t  // Each coordinate's own TYPE range, as decimal strings. Returning the\n547\t// parent aggregate instead would hand the caller a coordinate it did not ask\n548\t// for, and on the certify side that is a bound on the wrong quantity -- the one\n549\t// outcome that query exists to prevent.\n550\tstatic bool\n551\twalk_fields(const namespacet &ns, expr2tc &e, const std::string &path)\n552\t{\n553\t  size_t p = 0;\n554\t  while (p <= path.size())\n555\t  {\n556\t    const size_t q = path.find('.', p);\n557\t    const std::string field =\n558\t      path.substr(p, q == std::string::npos ? q : q - p);\n559\t    if (field.empty())\n560\t      return false;\n561\t    const typet st = ns.follow(migrate_type_back(e->type));\n562\t    if (st.id() != \"struct\")\n563\t      return false;\n564\t    bool hit = false;\n565\t    for (const auto &comp : to_struct_type(st).components())\n566\t      if (comp.get_name() == field || comp.get(\"#base_name\") == field)\n567\t      {\n568\t        e = member2tc(migrate_type(comp.type()), e, comp.get_name());\n569\t        hit = true;\n570\t        break;\n571\t      }\n572\t    if (!hit)\n573\t      return false;\n574\t    if (q == std::string::npos)\n575\t      return true;\n576\t    p = q + 1;\n577\t  }\n578\t  return false;\n579\t}\n580\t\n581\t// |R_c| for a punched interval (Definition 5): how many values of [lo, hi]\n582\t// survive once this coordinate's holes are removed.\n583\t//\n584\t// Shared by the two places that must not disagree — the choice between a hole\n585\t// and a side cut, and the test for whether the result is empty. A\n614\t  // refuted probe is not a failure — it is the ladder doing its job, and its\n615\t  // counterexample is a real input of pi with c > v.\n616\t  //\n617\t  // Nothing here is \"proven unreachable\": these verdicts are bounded exactly\n618\t  // like every other one in this pass, so an outer box is an outer box UNDER\n619\t  // THE DECLARED EXPLORATION. Stated because a box is the input to a soundness\n620\t  // argument downstream, and a bounded box silently promoted to an absolute one\n621\t  // is precisely how a certified region ends up too wide.\n622\t  struct bound_infot\n623\t  {\n624\t    bool have_u = false, have_l = false;\n625\t    BigInt u, l;\n626\t    // The TIGHTEST REFUTED probe on each side. `assert(temp_c <= v)` refuted\n627\t    // means some input of this path has c > v, so the true bound lies strictly\n628\t    // above v; together with the smallest holding probe it BRACKETS the bound.\n629\t    //\n630\t    // Reported because it is what makes the loop converge geometrically. A batch\n631\t    // of K probes gives resolution span/(K+1) in one round; refining the next\n632\t    // round's span to this bracket divides the resolution by (K+1) again, so the\n633\t    // precision is logarithmic in ROUNDS while each round stays one run. Without\n634\t    // the bracket a driver has no principled next span — and the recorded rule\n635\t    // it would otherwise use (take the span from the nearest sibling\n636\t    // counterexample) was measured NOT to work: a solver counterexample can sit\n637\t    // arbitrarily far from the boundary, and on the first contract tried it sat\n638\t    // at 2^256-1.\n639\t    bool have_ur = false, have_lr = false;\n640\t    BigInt ur, lr;\n641\t  };\n642\t  std::map<std::pair<uint64_t, std::string>, bound_infot> bounds;\n643\t  // Seed with the free bound: the coordinate's own type range (see the header).\n644\t  for (const auto &[enc, depth] : path_cov_outer_box_paths)\n645\t    for (const auto &[cname, r] : path_cov_outer_box_type_range)\n646\t    {\n647\t      bound_infot &b = bounds[{enc, cname}];\n648\t      b.have_l = b.have_u = true;\n649\t      b.l = string2integer(r.first);\n650\t      b.u = string2integer(r.second);\n651\t    }\n652\t  size_t decided = 0, undecided = 0;\n653\t  {\n654\t    std::lock_guard lock(claim_outcome_mutex);\n655\t    for (const auto &p : path_cov_outer_box_probes)\n656\t    {\n657\t      auto it = claim_outcome.find(p.key.first + \"\\t\" + p.key.second);\n658\t      if (it == claim_outcome.end())\n659\t      {\n660\t        ++undecided;\n661\t        continue;\n662\t      }\n663\t      ++decided;\n664\t      const BigInt v = string2integer(p.value);\n665\t      bound_infot &b = bounds[{p.enc, p.coord}];\n666\t      if (it->second == 'F')\n667\t      {\n668\t        // Refuted: keep the TIGHTEST one on each side, so the true bound is\n669\t        // bracketed rather than merely upper-bounded.\n670\t        if (p.upper)\n671\t        {\n672\t          if (!b.have_ur || v > b.ur)\n673\t          {\n674\t            b.ur = v;\n675\t            b.have_ur = true;\n676\t          }\n677\t        }\n678\t        else if (!b.have_lr || v < b.lr)\n679\t        {\n680\t          b.lr = v;\n681\t          b.have_lr = true;\n682\t        }\n683\t        continue;\n684\t      }\n685\t      if (it->second != 'P')\n686\t        continue; // unknown: establishes neither side\n687\t      if (p.upper)\n688\t      {\n689\t        if (!b.have_u || v < b.u)\n690\t        {\n691\t          b.u = v;\n692\t          b.have_u = true;\n693\t        }\n694\t      }\n695\t      else if (!b.have_l || v > b.l)\n696\t      {\n697\t        b.l = v;\n698\t        b.have_l = true;\n699\t      }\n700\t    }\n701\t  }\n702\t\n703\t  // Refused coordinates, named BEFORE any box is printed. A refused coordinate\n704\t  // emits no probe, so it appears in no box below — and an absence reads as\n705\t  // \"not asked about\", while the truth is \"asked about and refused\". Those are\n706\t  // different facts and only one of them is a gap in the coordinate set.\n707\t  if (!path_cov_refused_coords.empty())\n708\t  {\n709\t    std::string refused;\n710\t    for (const auto &[cn, why] : path_cov_refused_coords)\n711\t      refused += (refused.empty() ? \"\" : \"; \") + cn + \" (\" + why + \")\";\n712\t    log_warning(\n713\t      \"--path-cov-outer-box: {} coordinate(s) were REFUSED and appear in NO box \"\n714\t      \"below: {}. Their absence is a refusal, not a measurement — reading it as \"\n715\t      \"\\\"bounded by the whole type\\\" would attribute a measured bound to a \"\n716\t      \"coordinate nothing was measured on, and would widen every region that \"\n717\t      \"quoted it\",\n718\t      path_cov_refused_coords.size(),\n719\t      refused);\n720\t  }\n721\t\n722\t  std::string pin_note;\n723\t  for (const auto &[pn, pv] : path_cov_outer_box_pins)\n724\t    pin_note += (pin_note.empty() ? \"\" : \", \") + pn + \" == \" + pv;\n725\t  if (!pin_note.empty())\n726\t    log_status(\n727\t      \"--path-cov-outer-box: every box and every region below is measured under \"\n728\t      \"the PIN {} — they describe that SLICE of the input space, not the whole \"\n729\t      \"domain. Any test rendered from one must carry the pin as a `require` too, \"\n730\t      \"or it claims something about inputs that were never examined\",\n731\t      pin_note);\n732\t\n733\t  log_status(\n734\t    \"--path-cov-outer-box: {} of {} ladder probe(s) reached the solver. A probe \"\n735\t    \"that HOLDS is an outer bound; a refuted probe is the ladder working, and \"\n736\t    \"its counterexample is a genuine input of that path beyond the bound\",\n737\t    decided,\n738\t    decided + undecided);\n739\t\n740\t  // Coordinates, in the order the spec listed them.\n741\t  std::vector<std::string> coords;\n742\t  for (const auto &p : path_cov_outer_box_probes)\n743\t    if (std::find(coords.begin(), coords.end(), p.coord) == coords.end())\n744\t      coords.push_back(p.coord);\n745\t\n746\t  auto show = [&](uint64_t enc) {\n747\t    std::string s;\n748\t    for (const auto &c : coords)\n749\t    {\n750\t      auto it = bounds.find({enc, c});\n751\t      s += (s.empty() ? \"\" : \", \") + c + \" in \";\n752\t      if (it == bounds.end() || (!it->second.have_l && !it->second.have_u))\n753\t        s += \"(unbounded within the probed span)\";\n754\t      else\n755\t      {\n756\t        s += \"[\";\n757\t        s += it->second.have_l ? integer2string(it->second.l)\n758\t                               : std::string(\"<span lo\");\n759\t        s += \", \";\n760\t        s += it->second.have_u ? integer2string(it->second.u)\n761\t                               : std::string(\">span hi\");\n762\t        s += \"]\";\n763\t        // An inverted interval is EMPTY, and printed bare it reads as a measured\n764\t        // range. Say so at the interval itself, not only in a trailing note: the\n765\t        // number pair is what gets quoted.\n766\t        if (it->second.have_l && it->second.have_u && it->second.l > it->second.u)\n767\t          s += \" (EMPTY: lo > hi)\";\n768\t      }\n769\t    }\n770\t    return s;\n771\t  };\n772\t\n773\t  for (const auto &[enc, depth] : path_cov_outer_box_paths)\n774\t  {\n775\t    log_status(\n776\t      \"--path-cov-outer-box: path enc={} depth={} OUTER box (D_path is CONTAINED \"\n777\t      \"in it): {}\",\n778\t      enc,\n779\t      depth,\n780\t      show(enc));\n781\t    // The bracket: where the true bound still is. This is the next round's span,\n782\t    // and refining to it divides the resolution by (probes+1) again — which is\n783\t    // how a batch method reaches logarithmic precision without ever becoming an\n784\t    // adaptive query-per-step search.\n785\t    std::string br;\n786\t    for (const auto &c : coords)\n787\t    {\n788\t      auto it = bounds.find({enc, c});\n789\t      if (it == bounds.end())\n790\t        continue;\n791\t      if (it->second.have_ur && it->second.have_u)\n792\t        br += (br.empty() ? \"\" : \", \") + c + \" upper in (\" +\n793\t              integer2string(it->second.ur) + \", \" +\n794\t              integer2string(it->second.u) + \"]\";\n795\t      if (it->second.have_lr && it->second.have_l)\n796\t        br += (br.empty() ? \"\" : \", \") + c + \" lower in [\" +\n797\t              integer2string(it->second.l) + \", \" +\n798\t              integer2string(it->second.lr) + \")\";\n799\t    }\n800\t    if (!br.empty())\n801\t      log_status(\n802\t        \"--path-cov-outer-box: path enc={} BRACKET (refine the next batch's span \"\n803\t        \"to this): {}\",\n804\t        enc,\n805\t        br);\n806\t  }\n807\t\n808\t  // ---- 2. Subtract the siblings, greedily, one cut per sibling ----\n809\t  //\n810\t  // Zero queries. Path domains partition the input space, so an input in this\n811\t  // path's outer box and in NO sibling's outer box must walk this path. In one\n812\t  // dimension that difference is a union of segments; in more it is an L shape,\n813\t  // which cannot be written as one `require` per parameter. So each intersecting\n814\t  // sibling is removed by ONE cut along ONE coordinate — the result is a box,\n815\t  // and any point left in it is outside that sibling by construction.\n816\t  //\n817\t  // A cut is legal only if this path's own counterexample survives it: the CE is\n818\t  // a known member of D_path, so a cut that drops it has certainly cut into the\n819\t  // real domain. Among legal cuts, take the one that loses the least width on\n820\t  // the coordinate it cuts. Shrinking only ever makes the region SMALLER, so the\n821\t  // heuristic cannot break correctness — it only decides how much is kept, which\n822\t  // is why it is a free parameter and is reported rather than argued for.\n823\t  //\n824\t  // ---- WHY A THIRD KIND OF CUT: THE HOLE (Definition 5) ----\n825\t  //\n826\t  // The two side cuts cannot express \"everything except v\", and the cost of that\n827\t  // is not resolution, it is DETERMINISM. When a sibling occupies a single value\n828\t  // v strictly inside this box, both side cuts are legal and the one that gets\n829\t  // taken is decided by which side this path's own counterexample happens to sit\n830\t  // on — a value the solver chose. MEASURED on one address coordinate: supplying\n831\t  // 2^160-1 as the sibling counterexample yields `[256, 2^160-1]`, supplying 0\n832\t  // yields `[0, 254]`. Both are correct subsets of the true domain\n833\t  // `[0,254] U [256, 2^160-1]`; they differ by a factor of 5.7e45.\n834\t  //\n835\t  // Punching v out instead gives `[0, 2^160-1] \\ {v}` in BOTH cases. Same\n836\t  // legality rule (this path's CE must survive, so CE != v), same only-ever-\n837\t  // narrower invariant, and the answer stops depending on a value nobody chose.\n838\t  //\n839\t  // Restricted, deliberately, to a sibling whose outer box on the coordinate is\n840\t  // a SINGLE POINT. A sibling spanning several values could be punched out value\n841\t  // by value, and Definition 5 allows it — but how many points are worth\n842\t  // punching before a side cut is better is a policy knob with a yield question\n843\t  // behind it, and nothing has measured it. A multi-point sibling therefore\n844\t  // still gets a side cut, and that is a stated limit rather than an oversight.\n845\t  for (const auto &[enc, depth] : path_cov_outer_box_paths)\n846\t  {\n847\t    // Materialise this path's box; skip a coordinate with no bound at all.\n848\t    std::map<std::string, std::pair<BigInt, BigInt>> box;\n849\t    // Definition 5's H, per coordinate: the values removed from [lo, hi].\n850\t    std::map<std::string, std::set<BigInt>> holes;\n851\t    for (const auto &c : coords)\n852\t    {\n853\t      auto it = bounds.find({enc, c});\n854\t      if (it != bounds.end() && it->second.have_l && it->second.have_u)\n855\t        box[c] = {it->second.l, it->second.u};\n856\t    }\n857\t    if (box.empty())\n858\t    {\n859\t      log_status(\n860\t        \"--path-cov-outer-box: path enc={} has no fully bounded coordinate; no \"\n861\t        \"certified region is computed for it (the ladder span did not bracket \"\n862\t        \"its domain — widen the span or add probes)\",\n863\t        enc);\n864\t      continue;\n865\t    }\n866\t\n867\t    auto ce_of = [&](uint64_t e, const std::string &c, BigInt &out) {\n868\t      auto it = path_cov_outer_box_ce.find({e, c});\n869\t      if (it == path_cov_outer_box_ce.end())\n870\t        return false;\n871\t      out = string2integer(it->second);\n872\t      return true;\n873\t    };\n874\t\n875\t    size_t degenerate = 0;\n876\t    for (const auto &[senc, sdepth] : path_cov_outer_box_paths)\n877\t    {\n878\t      if (senc == enc)\n879\t        continue;\n880\t      // Does the sibling's box still intersect ours on every coordinate?\n881\t      bool intersects = true;\n882\t      std::map<std::string, std::pair<BigInt, BigInt>> sbox;\n883\t      for (const auto &c : coords)\n884\t      {\n885\t        auto it = bounds.find({senc, c});\n886\t        if (it == bounds.end() || !it->second.have_l || !it->second.have_u)\n887\t          continue; // unbounded there: cannot be used to separate on it\n888\t        sbox[c] = {it->second.l, it->second.u};\n889\t        auto ob = box.find(c);\n890\t        if (ob == box.end())\n891\t          continue;\n892\t        if (it->second.u < ob->second.first || it->second.l > ob->second.second)\n893\t          intersects = false;\n894\t      }\n895\t      if (!intersects)\n896\t        continue; // provably disjoint already: nothing to remove\n897\t      if (sbox.empty())\n898\t      {\n899\t        // The sibling has no coordinate bounded on BOTH sides, so there is no\n900\t        // cut that can be shown to exclude it — its domain may lie anywhere in\n901\t        // the probed span. Counting this as separated would silently keep a\n902\t        // region that provably contains foreign inputs, which is the one\n903\t        // outcome the subtraction must never produce. It is the same shape as\n904\t        // the missing-path warning above: an unmeasured sibling is not an\n905\t        // absent one.\n906\t        ++degenerate;\n907\t        continue;\n908\t      }\n909\t\n910\t      // Best legal cut across coordinates. Candidates are scored by how many\n911\t      // values SURVIVE on the coordinate they touch — not by raw width — because\n912\t      // a hole and a side cut are no longer comparable by width alone: a hole\n913\t      // keeps the full interval minus one point.\n914\t      bool best = false;\n915\t      std::string best_c;\n916\t      std::pair<BigInt, BigInt> best_range;\n917\t      bool best_is_hole = false;\n918\t      BigInt best_hole;\n919\t      BigInt best_kept;\n920\t      auto kept_in = [&](const std::string &c, const BigInt &lo,\n921\t                         const BigInt &hi) {\n922\t        return path_cov_kept_in(holes, c, lo, hi);\n923\t      };\n924\t      for (const auto &[c, sr] : sbox)\n925\t      {\n926\t        auto ob = box.find(c);\n927\t        if (ob == box.end())\n928\t          continue;\n929\t        BigInt ce;\n930\t        if (!ce_of(enc, c, ce))\n931\t          continue; // no CE for this coordinate: cannot check legality\n932\t        // THE HOLE, tried first so it wins ties: the sibling occupies exactly\n933\t        // one value here, that value is inside our interval, and our own\n934\t        // counterexample is not it. Removing it excludes the whole sibling while\n935\t        // keeping a known member of the domain.\n936\t        if (\n937\t          sr.first == sr.second && sr.first >= ob->second.first &&\n938\t          sr.first <= ob->second.second && ce != sr.first)\n939\t        {\n940\t          const BigInt k =\n941\t            kept_in(c, ob->second.first, ob->second.second) - 1;\n942\t          if (!best || k > best_kept)\n943\t          {\n944\t            best = true;\n945\t            best_is_hole = true;\n946\t            best_c = c;\n947\t            best_hole = sr.first;\n948\t            best_kept = k;\n949\t          }\n950\t        }\n951\t        // Keep the part strictly below the sibling, or strictly above it.\n952\t        if (sr.first > ob->second.first && ce < sr.first)\n953\t        {\n954\t          std::pair<BigInt, BigInt> r{ob->second.first, sr.first - 1};\n955\t          BigInt k = kept_in(c, r.first, r.second);\n956\t          if (!best || k > best_kept)\n957\t          {\n958\t            best = true;\n959\t            best_is_hole = false;\n960\t            best_c = c;\n961\t            best_range = r;\n962\t            best_kept = k;\n963\t          }\n964\t        }\n965\t        if (sr.second < ob->second.second && ce > sr.second)\n966\t        {\n967\t          std::pair<BigInt, BigInt> r{sr.second + 1, ob->second.second};\n968\t          BigInt k = kept_in(c, r.first, r.second);\n969\t          if (!best || k > best_kept)\n970\t          {\n971\t            best = true;\n972\t            best_is_hole = false;\n973\t            best_c = c;\n974\t            best_range = r;\n975\t            best_kept = k;\n976\t          }\n977\t        }\n978\t      }\n979\t      if (!best)\n980\t      {\n981\t        // No coordinate separates them while keeping the CE. This is the\n982\t        // documented degenerate case: the certified region collapses towards the\n983\t        // CE point and the path falls back to a concrete test. Reported, never\n984\t        // papered over by keeping a region that provably contains foreign inputs.\n985\t        ++degenerate;\n986\t        continue;\n987\t      }\n988\t      if (best_is_hole)\n989\t        holes[best_c].insert(best_hole);\n990\t      else\n991\t      {\n992\t        box[best_c] = best_range;\n993\t        // A hole outside the surviving interval removes nothing and would print\n994\t        // as a constraint on values the region no longer contains — a reader\n995\t        // would take it as evidence about the domain when it is evidence about\n996\t        // an interval that has been cut away since.\n997\t        auto h = holes.find(best_c);\n998\t        if (h != holes.end())\n999\t        {\n1000\t          std::set<BigInt> keep;\n1001\t          for (const BigInt &v : h->second)\n1002\t            if (v >= best_range.first && v <= best_range.second)\n1003\t              keep.insert(v);\n1004\t          h->second.swap(keep);\n1005\t        }\n1006\t      }\n1007\t    }\n1008\t\n1009\t    std::string s;\n1010\t    std::string empty_on;\n1011\t    size_t holes_punched = 0;\n1012\t    for (const auto &[c, r] : box)\n1013\t    {\n1014\t      s += (s.empty() ? \"\" : \", \") + c + \" in [\" + integer2string(r.first) +\n1015\t           \", \" + integer2string(r.second) + \"]\";\n1016\t      // Definition 5's punched interval, printed WITH the interval rather than\n1017\t      // in a trailing note: `[0, 2^160-1]` and `[0, 2^160-1] \\ {255}` are\n1018\t      // different regions and the numbers are what gets quoted.\n1019\t      auto h = holes.find(c);\n1020\t      if (h != holes.end() && !h->second.empty())\n1021\t      {\n1022\t        std::string hs;\n1023\t        for (const BigInt &v : h->second)\n1024\t          hs += (hs.empty() ? \"\" : \", \") + integer2string(v);\n1025\t        s += \" \\\\ {\" + hs + \"}\";\n1026\t        holes_punched += h->second.size();\n1027\t      }\n1028\t      // EMPTY has a second route once the interval can be punched: a\n1029\t      // well-formed [lo, hi] whose every value has been removed. Both routes\n1030\t      // land in the same note, because both mean the region holds no input.\n1031\t      if (\n1032\t        r.first > r.second ||\n1033\t        path_cov_kept_in(holes, c, r.first, r.second) <= 0)\n1034\t        empty_on += (empty_on.empty() ? \"\" : \", \") + c;\n1035\t    }\n1036\t\n1037\t    // AN EMPTY REGION IS NOT A REGION, and the heading is the dangerous part.\n1038\t    // The subtraction can invert an interval — measured: with the environment\n1039\t    // pinned, the ABI-gate revert path's domain is empty in that slice and the\n1040\t    // cut duly produced lo > hi. Printed under \"CERTIFIED region\" with no\n1041\t    // further comment, that reads to any reader as a region that was certified.\n1042\t    // Nothing here certifies anything (this whole stage is zero-query), and an\n1043\t    // empty box additionally certifies VACUOUSLY if it reaches the query.\n1044\t    //\n1045\t    // The driver already refuses these, which is exactly why the line KEEPS its\n1046\t    // parseable shape instead of being replaced: the driver finds the region by\n1047\t    // this prefix, and suppressing the line would drop it into its generic \"no\n1048\t    // fully bounded region was measured\" branch — trading a precise diagnosis\n1049\t    // for a vaguer one in the name of safety. Two defences, not one moved.\n1050\t    //\n1051\t    // What changes is that the emptiness travels WITH the numbers rather than\n1052\t    // after them. A caveat at the end of the line is read after the interval has\n1053\t    // already been read.\n1054\t    std::string empty_note;\n1055\t    if (!empty_on.empty())\n1056\t      empty_note =\n1057\t        \" — EMPTY, NOT CERTIFIED: no value survives on \" + empty_on +\n1058\t        \" (either lo > hi, or the holes remove every value the interval holds — \"\n1059\t        \"a punched interval can be empty while its endpoints look well-formed)\"\n1060\t        \", so this box contains no input at all. The subtraction removed \"\n1061\t        \"everything, which under a pin usually means the pin excluded this path \"\n1062\t        \"from the slice; the honest statement is that exclusion. Do NOT hand \"\n1063\t        \"this box to the certification query: an unsatisfiable assumption \"\n1064\t        \"answers SUCCESSFUL for want of any execution\";\n1065\t    std::string caveat;\n1066\t    if (degenerate > 0)\n1067\t      caveat =\n1068\t        \" — WARNING: \" + std::to_string(degenerate) +\n1069\t        \" sibling(s) could not be separated by any single coordinate cut that \"\n1070\t        \"keeps this path's counterexample, so the region above STILL OVERLAPS \"\n1071\t        \"them and must be certified before use (or the path falls back to its \"\n1072\t        \"concrete counterexample test)\";\n1073\t    log_status(\n1074\t      \"--path-cov-outer-box: path enc={} CERTIFIED region after subtracting \"\n1075\t      \"sibling outer boxes (zero queries): {}{}{}\",\n1076\t      enc,\n1077\t      s,\n1078\t      empty_note,\n1079\t      caveat);\n1080\t    // Printed as its own line, and printed as a COUNT, because the property a\n1081\t    // regression has to pin is \"the subtraction punched rather than took a\n1082\t    // side\" — which is invisible in the region text of a path that happened to\n1083\t    // need no hole, and which is exactly the property that stops the answer\n1084\t    // depending on which counterexample the solver returned.\n1085\t    if (holes_punched > 0)\n1086\t      log_status(\n1087\t        \"--path-cov-outer-box: path enc={} — {} of the cut(s) above are HOLES \"\n1088\t        \"(Definition 5), not side cuts: a sibling occupying a single value was \"\n1089\t        \"removed by excluding that value. This is the part of the region that \"\n1090\t        \"does NOT depend on which counterexample the solver returned for the \"\n1091\t        \"sibling; a side cut there would have kept only the side holding this \"\n1092\t        \"path's own counterexample\",\n1093\t        enc,\n1094\t        holes_punched);\n1095\t  }\n1096\t\n1097\t  log_status(\n1098\t    \"--path-cov-outer-box: these regions are CANDIDATES, not certificates. Used only to name things (path ids, fingerprints), never to make\n// a soundness decision: a collision would merge two path ids, so the space is\n// kept at 64 bits and the id is printed in full hex so a human can compare it.\nstatic uint64_t fnv1a(const std::string &s, uint64_t h = 1469598103934665603ULL)\n{\n  for (unsigned char c : s)\n  {\n    h ^= c;\n    h *= 1099511628211ULL;\n  }\n  return h;\n}\n\nstatic std::string hex64(uint64_t v)\n{\n  static const char *d = \"0123456789abcdef\";\n  std::string out(16, '0');\n  for (int i = 15; i >= 0; --i, v >>= 4)\n    out[i] = d[v & 0xF];\n  return out;\n}\n\nvoid goto_coveraget::write_path_covered_set_atomic()\n{\n  if (path_covered_outpath.empty())\n    return;\n  nlohmann::json out;\n  out[\"version\"] = 2;\n  out[\"kind\"] = \"solidity-complete-path\";\n  // The fingerprint is written so the NEXT run can refuse this file outright.\n  out[\"fingerprint\"] = path_cov_fingerprint;\n  out[\"covered\"] = nlohmann::json::array();\n  // A path counts as covered only when a counterexample was actually obtained\n  // ('F'). 'P' (no witness at this bound) and 'U' (undecided) are not evidence\n  // of anything and must never enter a cross-run cover.\n  std::set<std::string> ids = path_covered_ids;\n  {\n    std::lock_guard lock(claim_outcome_mutex);\n    for (const auto &[claim, id] : path_stable_id)\n    {\n      auto o = claim_outcome.find(claim.first + \"\\t\" + claim.second);\n      if (o != claim_outcome.end() && o->second == 'F')\n        ids.insert(id);\n    }\n  }\n  for (const auto &id : ids)\n    out[\"covered\"].push_back(id);\n  const std::string tmp = path_covered_outpath + \".tmp\";\n  {\n    std::ofstream f(tmp);\n    if (!f)\n    {\n      log_warning(\"coverage-covered-set: cannot write {}\", tmp);\n      return;\n    }\n    f << out.dump(2) << \"\\n\";\n  }\n  if (std::rename(tmp.c_str(), path_covered_outpath.c_str()) != 0)\n    log_warning(\n      \"coverage-covered-set: atomic rename to {} failed\", path_covered_outpath);\n}\n\nbool goto_coveraget::path_witnessed_earlier(\n  const std::pair<std::string, std::string> &claim_key)\n{\n  if (path_covered_ids.empty())\n    return false;\n  auto it = path_stable_id.find(claim_key);\n  return it != path_stable_id.end() && path_covered_ids.count(it->second) != 0;\n}\n\nconst std::vector<std::string> &goto_coveraget::path_u_reason_tokens()\n{\n  // Report order == classification priority, so the printed line reads in the\n  // same order the decision is made. `unit-not-entered` sits second on purpose;\n  // see path_u_reason_token.\n  static const std::vector<std::string> tokens = {\n    \"named-obstacle\",\n    \"unit-not-entered\",\n    \"bounded-holds\",\n    \"solver-unknown\",\n    \"not-solved-this-run\"};\n  return tokens;\n}\n\nstd::string goto_coveraget::path_u_reason_token(\n  const std::pair<std::string, std::string> &claim_key)\n{\n  // Most specific first.
