So any user-source ASSUME anywhere in\n3912\t    // the unit disqualifies EVERY path of that unit.\n3913\t    std::set<std::string> lost_decision_locs;\n3914\t    forall_goto_program_instructions (li, goto_program)\n3915\t      if (is_lost_decision(li))\n3916\t        lost_decision_locs.insert(li->location.as_string());\n3917\t    const bool unit_has_lost_decision = !lost_decision_locs.empty();\n3918\t    if (unit_has_lost_decision)\n3919\t      ++obstacle_units;\n3920\t\n3921\t    // Fold one decision into the running id. `site` is the decision's SOURCE\n3922\t    // location and `sub` its operand index within that site (several folded\n3923\t    // short-circuit operands share one location), so the key is content\n3924\t    // addressed: it does not move when other decisions are added or when the\n3925\t    // enumeration order changes. Mutates `occ` — callers copy it first for the\n3926\t    // branch they push.\n3927\t    // Recording the DFS side HERE, rather than at the three fan-out sites, is\n3928\t    // deliberate: this lambda is the single place a decision enters a path's\n3929\t    // identity, so a future fan-out that forgets to register itself cannot\n3930\t    // exist — it would also have to bypass the id, which would break the\n3931\t    // cross-run key first and far more loudly.\n3932\t    auto step_id = [&dfs_decision_sites](\n3933\t                     uint64_t idh,\n3934\t                     occt &occ,\n3935\t                     const std::string &site,\n3936\t                     unsigned sub,\n3937\t                     bool polarity) {\n3938\t      dfs_decision_sites.emplace(site, sub);\n3939\t      const uint64_t sk = fnv1a(site + \"#\" + std::to_string(sub));\n3940\t      const unsigned n = occ[sk]++;\n3941\t      uint64_t h = fnv1a(\"|\", idh);\n3942\t      h = fnv1a(hex64(sk), h);\n3943\t      h = fnv1a(polarity ? \"T\" : \"F\", h);\n3944\t      h = fnv1a(std::to_string(n), h);\n3945\t      return h;\n3946\t    };\n3947\t\n3948\t    // Deferred exit asserts (insert after the walk so we don't mutate the\n3949\t    // program mid-DFS). Each entry: (insertion pc, tr!=enc||cnt!=depth guard,\n3950\t    // claim comment, is_revert). An is_revert path exits through a custom-error\n3951\t    // `#sol_error` revert; its assert is placed right BEFORE that call (upstream\n3952\t    // of the callee's ASSUME(false), which would otherwise make an\n3953\t    // END_FUNCTION-placed assert vacuous -> path never covered) and gets\n3954\t    // stamped `sol_revert_edge` so the Foundry generator renders\n3955\t    // vm.expectRevert() (R0). Normal paths exit at END_FUNCTION, is_revert=false.\n3956\t    // 5th field: the content-addressed stable path id (cross-run key).\n3957\t    std::vector<std::\n3958\t                  tuple<goto_programt::targett, expr2tc, std::string, bool, std::string>>\n3959\t      to_insert;\n3960\t    bool capped = false;\n3961\t    // Set when a back-edge budget refused a continuation, i.e. this unit has a\n3962\t    // path that the loop bound cut short. The exit census below downgrades its\n3963\t    // hard failure to a bound obstacle when this is set, because an exit that\n3964\t    // is only reachable after more than `path_cov_unwind` iterations is\n3965\t    // legitimately absent from the enumeration.\n3966\t    bool loop_truncated = false;\n3967\t    const size_t dropped_before_unit = dropped_paths;\n3968\t    // Indices into `to_insert` whose path exits via a rollback revert; resolved\n3969\t    // to claim keys after the walk (the key needs the insertion location).\n3970\t    std::set<size_t> rollback_exits;\n3971\t    // Indices whose exit shape is ambiguous between a bare require-revert and a\n3972\t    // plain early return (see the END_FUNCTION arm below).\n3973\t    std::set<size_t> undetermined_exits;\n3974\t    // Hard cap on DFS work so a pathological CFG can never exhaust memory.\n3975\t    size_t pushes = 0;\n3976\t    const size_t push_cap = 50 * path_cov_max_goals + 100000;\n3977\t\n3978\t    // Emit one deferred exit assert for a complete path reaching `loc` with\n3979\t    // path number `penc` and decision depth `pdepth`. Returns false (and sets\n3980\t    // capped) when the per-function goal cap is hit, so the caller stops.\n3981\t    auto emit_exit = [&](\n3982\t                       goto_programt::targett loc,\n3983\t                       uint64_t penc,\n3984\t                       uint64_t pdepth,\n3985\t                       bool is_revert,\n3986\t                       uint64_t pidh) -> bool {\n3987\t      if (to_insert.size() >= path_cov_max_goals)\n3988\t      {\n3989\t        capped = true;\n3990\t        ++dropped_paths;\n3991\t        return false;\n3992\t      }\n3993\t      // assert(tr != enc || cnt != depth): falsified only on the exact path\n3994\t      // (same decision sequence AND same length), so a wrapped tr from a longer\n3995\t      // path cannot fire this shorter path's assert.\n3996\t      expr2tc g = or2tc(\n3997\t        notequal2tc(tr, constant_int2tc(utype, BigInt(penc))),\n3998\t        notequal2tc(cnt, constant_int2tc(utype, BigInt(pdepth))));\n3999\t      // The comment stays the readable run-local ordinal — it is what appears in\n4000\t      // the solver log and in every test.desc. The cross-run identity is the\n4001\t      // separate stable id below; the two are deliberately not the same string.\n4002\t      std::string comment =\n4003\t        id2string(f_it->first) + \":path:\" + std::to_string(penc);\n4004\t      // Mix the exit site in too. The decision sequence already determines the\n4005\t      // exit, so this adds nothing today; it costs nothing and means a future\n4006\t      // change that lets two decision sequences share an exit cannot collide.\n4007\t      const std::string stable =\n4008\t        hex64(fnv1a(\"exit:\" + loc->location.as_string(), pidh));\n4009\t      // Recorded here rather than derived later: this is the only place that\n4010\t      // knows the path's decision depth, and the stage-2 queries need it to\n4011\t      // identify the path at all.\n4012\t      path_decision_depth[{comment, loc->location.as_string()}] = pdepth;\n4013\t      to_insert.emplace_back(loc, g, comment, is_revert, stable);\n4014\t      return true;\n4015\t    };\n4016\t\n4017\t    // True iff `i` is the lowered call of a custom-error `revert E()` — a\n4018\t    // FUNCTION_CALL to a `#sol_error` function whose body is ASSUME(false).\n4019\t    // Reaching such a call means the path reverts unconditionally, so its\n4020\t    // identity assert must be placed right BEFORE the call (upstream of the\n4021\t    // callee's ASSUME(false)); an END_FUNCTION-placed assert would be\n4022\t    // downstream and vacuous. Checking the call instruction itself (rather than\n4023\t    // the incoming edge) catches EVERY revert shape — guarded `if(c) revert\n4024\t    // E()`, straight-line `revert E()` as the whole body, and reverts reached\n4025\t    // via an intervening unconditional GOTO — because the DFS always walks onto\n4026\t    // the call instruction. require()/revert(\"msg\") lower to a state-restoring\n4027\t    // rollback with NO #sol_error call, so they are excluded and correctly fall\n4028\t    // through to END_FUNCTION (try/catch). (codex: an earlier per-edge check\n4029\t    // missed unguarded / goto-reached reverts; this instruction check fixes it.)\n4030\t    // True iff `i` is the state-restoring assignment of a rollback revert:\n4031\t    // `require(cond)` / `require(cond,\"msg\")` / `revert(\"msg\")` in a function\n4032\t    // with an entry snapshot lower to `*this = _sol_save_this` followed by a\n4033\t    // jump to END_FUNCTION. Keying on the frontend's canonical snapshot symbol\n4034\t    // name is exact — no other assignment sources it. A path that walks over\n4035\t    // this instruction reverts, even though it reaches END_FUNCTION like a\n4036\t    // normal exit.\n4037\t    auto is_rollback_restore = [&](goto_programt::const_targett i) -> bool {\n4038\t      if (!i->is_assign() || !is_code_assign2t(i->code))\n4039\t        return false;\n4040\t      const expr2tc &src = to_code_assign2t(i->code).source;\n4041\t      return is_symbol2t(src) &&\n4042\t             to_symbol2t(src).thename.as_string().find(\"_sol_save_this\") !=\n4043\t               std::string::npos;\n4044\t    };\n4045\t\n4046\t    // True iff `i` is the frontend's explicit revert marker\n4047\t    // `_ESBMC_sol_mark_revert()`. Under the revert-observation gate (which\n4048\t    // --solidity-path-coverage turns on) EVERY require/revert failure edge\n4049\t    // carries this call, including the shapes that emit no state restore at\n4050\t    // all. It is the ONLY positive evidence separating a reverting exit from a\n4051\t    // plain early `return`: both otherwise lower to the identical\n4052\t    // `IF <guard> THEN GOTO <END_FUNCTION>`.\n4053\t    auto is_revert_mark = [&](goto_programt::const_targett i) -> bool {\n4054\t      if (!i->is_function_call() || !is_code_function_call2t(i->code))\n4055\t        return false;\n4056\t      const expr2tc &fn = to_code_function_call2t(i->code).function;\n4057\t      return is_symbol2t(fn) &&\n4058\t             to_symbol2t(fn).thename.as_string().find(\n4059\t               \"_ESBMC_sol_mark_revert\") != std::string::npos;\n4060\t    };\n4061\t\n4062\t    // True iff `i` is the function EPILOGUE's restore of the enclosing-contract\n4063\t    // context (`_ESBMC_enclosing_contract_address = _saved_encl_addr`). Every\n4064\t    // ordinary exit of a Solidity public function walks through it; a\n4065\t    // `require`-failure edge that precedes any state write is compiled as a\n4066\t    // BARE jump straight to END_FUNCTION and skips it. That makes \"did this\n4067\t    // path pass the epilogue?\" the only positive evidence available to tell an\n4068\t    // ordinary exit from such a bare revert edge.\n4069\t    auto is_epilogue_restore = [&](goto_programt::const_targett i) -> bool {\n4070\t      if (!i->is_assign() || !is_code_assign2t(i->code))\n4071\t        return false;\n4072\t      // An expanded callee brings its OWN epilogue along, and it matches the\n4073\t      // same symbol name. Counting it would let a path that ran the callee's\n4074\t      // epilogue and then took the caller's bare revert edge look like an\n4075\t      // ordinary exit. Only THIS unit's epilogue is evidence about this unit's\n4076\t      // exit, so instructions flagged by the expansion are not evidence.\n4077\t      if (i->location.get_bool(\"sol_path_inlined\"))\n4078\t        return false;\n4079\t      const expr2tc &src = to_code_assign2t(i->code).source;\n4080\t      return is_symbol2t(src) &&\n4081\t             to_symbol2t(src).thename.as_string().find(\"_saved_encl_addr\") !=\n4082\t               std::string::npos;\n4083\t    };\n4084\t\n4085\t    // Does this function HAVE an epilogue at all? Without one the marker above\n4086\t    // carries no information, so every path would look \"bypassed\" and be\n4087\t    // reported undetermined. Only apply the test where it is meaningful.\n4088\t    bool has_epilogue = false;\n4089\t    forall_goto_program_instructions (eit, goto_program)\n4090\t      if (is_epilogue_restore(eit))\n4091\t      {\n4092\t        has_epilogue = true;\n4093\t        break;\n4094\t      }\n4095\t\n4096\t    auto is_error_call = [&](goto_programt::const_targett i) -> bool {\n4097\t      if (!i->is_function_call() || !is_code_function_call2t(i->code))\n4098\t        return false;\n4099\t      const expr2tc &fn = to_code_function_call2t(i->code).function;\n4100\t      if (!is_symbol2t(fn))\n4101\t        return false;\n4102\t      const symbolt *s = ns.lookup(to_symbol2t(fn).thename);\n4103\t      return s && !s->type.get(\"#sol_error\").as_string().empty();\n4104\t    };\n4105\t\n4106\t    // \"A rolled-back execution never reaches a RETURN\" — MEASURED AND REFUTED.\n4107\t    //\n4108\t    // Had it held, reaching a RETURN would have been POSITIVE evidence of a\n4109\t    // normal exit, independent of the revert-observation gate and of which\n4110\t    // scopes that gate covers. It does not hold, and the reason is structural\n4111\t    // rather than a corner case: when the enclosing function returns a value,\n4112\t    // the frontend lowers a failing `require` to\n4113\t    //     { *this = _sol_save_this; return [nondet]; }\n4114\t    // so the reverting execution ends at a RETURN of the frontend's own making.\n4115\t    // Refuted on the simplest shape tried (compute a value, mutate state, then\n4116\t    // fail a require) and again on a modifier's require — the latter had been\n4117\t    // predicted to be a positive case, and is one only when the function\n4118\t    // returns nothing.\n4119\t    //\n4120\t    // Consequence, recorded so it is not quietly re-derived: the inference\n4121\t    // \"ends at a RETURN, therefore normal\" is NOT available. The counter below\n4122\t    // stays as an internal consistency check — such a path must always be\n4123\t    // classified as a rollback revert, never as normal — and is expected to be\n4124\t    // nonzero on ordinary contracts, so it logs at debug level rather than\n4125\t    // warning.\n4126\t    size_t rolled_back_return_exits = 0;\n4127\t    std::vector<std::string> rolled_back_return_locs;\n4128\t\n4129\t    // ---- WHY an exit came out `undetermined` ----\n4130\t    //\n4131\t    // `undetermined` means \"no positive evidence of a normal exit was found\".\n4132\t    // Since the frontend contract landed, every regression reports zero of them,\n4133\t    // so a nonzero count is now a hard signal rather than background noise — and\n4134\t    // a bare count says only THAT evidence is missing, never WHICH KIND. There\n4135\t    // are exactly three ways to get here, each missing a different witness, and\n4136\t    // they call for different fixes:\n4137\t    //\n4138\t    //   (1) the unit has NO epilogue at all, so the epilogue marker carries no\n4139\t    //       information for any of its paths (library / free-function scope);\n4140\t    //   (2) the unit HAS an epilogue and this path reached END_FUNCTION without\n4141\t    //       walking it — the bare-jump shape a pre-state-write `require` failure\n4142\t    //       and a plain early `return` share;\n4143\t    //   (3) the path ends at a RETURN carrying no `sol_source_return` marker and\n4144\t    //       walked no epilogue — either a return shape the frontend does not\n4145\t    //       stamp, or a RETURN the frontend synthesised for something else.\n4146\t    //\n4147\t    // Grouped per unit and by cause rather than listed per path: the lesson from\n4148\t    // chasing these one at a time is that two different defects can sit on the\n4149\t    // same function, and only a grouping shows which witness the whole group is\n4150\t    // missing.\n4151\t    size_t und_no_epilogue = 0;\n4152\t    size_t und_epilogue_skipped = 0;\n4153\t    size_t und_return_unmarked = 0;\n4154\t    std::set<std::string> und_locs_no_epilogue;\n4155\t    std::set<std::string> und_locs_epilogue_skipped;\n4156\t    std::set<std::string> und_locs_return_unmarked;\n4157\t\n4158\t    // Classify the exit just appended to `to_insert`. Shared by the\n4159\t    // END_FUNCTION arm and the RETURN arm so the two cannot drift apart.\n4160\t    //\n4161\t    // `src_return` is the frontend's POSITIVE marker (`sol_source_return`),\n4162\t    // stamped on RETURNs lowered from a source-level `return` and NOT on the\n4163\t    // one the frontend synthesises for a failing `require`\n4164\t    // (`{ *this = _sol_save_this; return [nondet]; }`). It is the second piece\n4165\t    // of positive evidence, alongside the epilogue: the epilogue cannot testify\n4166\t    // for a returning path because it is emitted after the RETURN, which is why\n4167\t    // every value-returning unit's normal exit used to be `undetermined`.\n4168\t    //\n4169\t    // The rollback test still runs FIRST and still wins. A source `return` can\n4170\t    // sit on a path that already walked a revert marker or a state restore, and\n4171\t    // on such a path the transaction reverts whatever the return statement says.\n4172\t    // Only a path with no rollback evidence AND an affirmative source-return\n4173\t    // marker is called normal — that is still a positive inference, not\n4174\t    // \"nothing said revert, so it must be fine\".\n4175\t    // (`se` can only be true when the function HAS an epilogue, since it is set\n4176\t    // by walking that very instruction — so the previous `!has_epilogue || !se`\n4177\t    // is exactly `!se`, and dropping the redundant term changes nothing.)\n4178\t    auto classify_exit = [&](\n4179\t                           size_t idx,\n4180\t                           bool rb,\n4181\t                           bool se,\n4182\t                           bool src_return,\n4183\t                           const std::string &site) {\n4184\t      if (rb)\n4185\t        rollback_exits.insert(idx);\n4186\t      else if (!se && !src_return)\n4187\t      {\n4188\t        undetermined_exits.insert(idx);\n4189\t        ++und_return_unmarked;\n4190\t        und_locs_return_unmarked.insert(site);\n4191\t      }\n4192\t    };\n4193\t\n4194\t    while (!stack.empty())\n4195\t    {\n4196\t      auto [pc, enc, becnt, depth, rolled_back, saw_epilogue, idh, occ] =\n4197\t        stack.back();\n4198\t      stack.pop_back();\n4199\t\n4200\t      while (true)\n4201\t      {\n4202\t        if (pc == goto_program.instructions.end() || pc->is_end_function())\n4203\t        {\n4204\t          if (pc != goto_program.instructions.end())\n4205\t          {\n4206\t            if (!emit_exit(pc, enc, depth, false, idh))\n4207\t              break;\n4208\t            const size_t idx = to_insert.size() - 1;\n4209\t            // An END_FUNCTION exit is never itself a source `return`: a bare\n4210\t            // `return;` lowers to a JUMP to END_FUNCTION, so the marker sits on\n4211\t            // the jump, not here. Such a path in a function WITH an epilogue\n4212\t            // already walks it and is normal on that evidence.\n4213\t            if (rolled_back)\n4214\t              // Positive evidence of a rollback revert.\n4215\t              rollback_exits.insert(idx);\n4216\t            else if (!has_epilogue || !saw_epilogue)\n4217\t              // No positive evidence of a normal exit. Either the path reached\n4218\t              // END_FUNCTION while SKIPPING the epilogue, or the function has\n4219\t              // no epilogue at all (library / free function — exactly the\n4220\t              // scopes the revert-observation gate does NOT mark, so a revert\n4221\t              // there carries no marker either). Both a `require` failing\n4222\t              // before any state write and a plain early `return` compile to\n4223\t              // this same shape, with nothing on the edge to separate them.\n4224\t              // Report undetermined rather than guess: calling it \"normal\"\n4225\t              // would claim a reverted transaction succeeded — measured on\n4226\t              // a library whose function reverts, that is exactly what the\n4227\t              // previous \"no epilogue => normal\" default did.\n4228\t              //\n4229\t              // The two sub-cases are counted apart (see the declaration): \"the\n4230\t              // unit has no epilogue at all\" is a scope problem affecting every\n4231\t              // path of the unit, while \"the epilogue exists and this path\n4232\t              // skipped it\" is a per-path shape. Fixing one does nothing for the\n4233\t              // other.\n4234\t              {\n4235\t                undetermined_exits.insert(idx);\n4236\t                if (has_epilogue)\n4237\t                {\n4238\t                  ++und_epilogue_skipped;\n4239\t                  und_locs_epilogue_skipped.insert(pc->location.as_string());\n4240\t                }\n4241\t                else\n4242\t                {\n4243\t                  ++und_no_epilogue;\n4244\t                  und_locs_no_epilogue.insert(pc->location.as_string());\n4245\t                }\n4246\t              }\n4247\t          }\n4248\t          break;\n4249\t        }\n4250\t        if (is_rollback_restore(pc) || is_revert_mark(pc))\n4251\t          rolled_back = true;\n4252\t        if (is_epilogue_restore(pc))\n4253\t          saw_epilogue = true;\n4254\t        // Custom-error revert exit: the DFS reached the `#sol_error` call\n4255\t        // (guarded, straight-line, or via an unconditional GOTO). Emit the\n4256\t        // identity assert HERE (upstream of the callee's ASSUME(false), so it is\n4257\t        // reachable) and stop; flag it for vm.expectRevert() (R0).\n4258\t        if (is_error_call(pc))\n4259\t        {\n4260\t          if (!emit_exit(pc, enc, depth, true, idh))\n4261\t            break;\n4262\t          break;\n4263\t        }\n4264\t        if (pc->is_goto())\n4265\t        {\n4266\t          const bool back = pc->is_backwards_goto();\n4267\t          if (is_true(pc->guard))\n4268\t          {\n4269\t            // Unconditional goto. A backward one is one iteration of the loop\n4270\t            // whose head is the goto's target; bound that loop independently.\n4271\t            if (back)\n4272\t            {\n4273\t              const unsigned key = pc->get_target()->target_number;\n4274\t              if (becnt[key] >= path_cov_unwind)\n4275\t              {\n4276\t                loop_truncated = true;\n4277\t                break; // this loop's bound reached: path truncated\n4278\t              }\n4279\t              ++becnt[key];\n4280\t            }\n4281\t            pc = pc->get_target();\n4282\t            continue;\n4283\t          }\n4284\t          // Conditional. Keep enc within 64 bits (leading sentinel + one bit\n4285\t          // per decision on the path); drop over-long paths rather than alias.\n4286\t          if (enc >= (uint64_t(1) << 62))\n4287\t          {\n4288\t            ++dropped_paths;\n4289\t            break;\n4290\t          }\n4291\t          // guard-true/taken successor -> target. If that edge is a loop\n4292\t          // back-edge, its own loop is bounded by path_cov_unwind.\n4293\t          bool take = true;\n4294\t          becntt becnt_taken = becnt;\n4295\t          if (back)\n4296\t          {\n4297\t            const unsigned key = pc->get_target()->target_number;\n4298\t            if (becnt_taken[key] >= path_cov_unwind)\n4299\t            {\n4300\t              take = false;\n4301\t              loop_truncated = true;\n4302\t            }\n4303\t            else\n4304\t              ++becnt_taken[key];\n4305\t          }\n4306\t          // Push the guard-true/taken successor; the guard-false/fall-through\n4307\t          // continues in-place. A reverting successor (custom-error revert) is\n4308\t          // detected at the top of the loop when the DFS reaches the\n4309\t          // `#sol_error` call instruction, so no per-edge revert test is needed.\n4310\t          const std::string dsite = pc->location.as_string();\n4311\t          if (take)\n4312\t          {\n4313\t            if (++pushes > push_cap)\n4314\t            {\n4315\t              capped = true;\n4316\t              ++dropped_paths;\n4317\t              break;\n4318\t            }\n4319\t            // Both arms consume the SAME occurrence of this site, so each starts\n4320\t            // from its own copy of the counters.\n4321\t            occt occ_taken = occ;\n4322\t            const uint64_t idh_taken =\n4323\t              step_id(idh, occ_taken, dsite, 0, /*polarity=*/true);\n4324\t            note_decision(enc * 2 + 1, pc->location, pc->guard, 0);\n4325\t            stack.push_back(\n4326\t              {pc->get_target(),\n4327\t               enc * 2 + 1,\n4328\t               becnt_taken,\n4329\t               depth + 1,\n4330\t               rolled_back,\n4331\t               saw_epilogue,\n4332\t               idh_taken,\n4333\t               occ_taken});\n4334\t          }\n4335\t          // guard-false/fallthrough successor -> next (never a back-edge).\n4336\t          idh = step_id(idh, occ, dsite, 0, /*polarity=*/false);\n4337\t          note_decision(enc * 2 + 0, pc->location, pc->guard, 0);\n4338\t          enc = enc * 2 + 0;\n4339\t          ++depth;\n4340\t          pc = std::next(pc);\n4341\t          continue;\n4342\t        }\n4343\t        // A RETURN is a path EXIT, not a straight-line instruction.\n4344\t        //\n4345\t        // symex terminates the frame at RETURN — it does not fall through to\n4346\t        // END_FUNCTION — so an identity assert placed at END_FUNCTION sits\n4347\t        // downstream of the frame exit and can never execute. Measured on four\n4348\t        // variants that isolate the cause: a unit that writes state and returns\n4349\t        // nothing covers 3/3, while the SAME body with a return value covers\n4350\t        // 1/3, and the one path that stays coverable is exactly the ABI\n4351\t        // value-reject path — the only one that reaches END_FUNCTION by a plain\n4352\t        // GOTO instead of through the RETURN. Purity, and whether an explicit\n4353\t        // `return` statement is written at all (a named return variable behaves\n4354\t        // identically), make no difference.\n4355\t        //\n4356\t        // Effect before this: EVERY unit with a return value had all of its body\n4357\t        // paths reported U — a systematic, silent deflation of coverage on any\n4358\t        // real contract, since getters and view functions all return values.\n4359\t        //\n4360\t        // Emitting here places the assert immediately BEFORE the RETURN:\n4361\t        // downstream of this path's tr/cnt updates (Phase 1 inserted those\n4362\t        // before the RETURN earlier, so they end up further from it) and\n4363\t        // upstream of the frame exit.\n4364\t        if (pc->is_return() && is_code_return2t(pc->code))\n4365\t        {\n4366\t          const expr2tc &rsrc = to_code_return2t(pc->code).operand;\n4367\t          // Collected, not merely counted: the operand EXPRESSION is what the\n4368\t          // branch metric keys its claim on, so recording the decision needs the\n4369\t          // operand itself. Collect order is the bit order (see the DFS below).\n4370\t          std::vector<expr2tc> rops;\n4371\t          if (pc->location.property().as_string() != \"skipped\")\n4372\t            collect_short_circuit_decisions(\n4373\t              rsrc, [&](const expr2tc &e) { rops.push_back(e); });\n4374\t          const size_t RK = rops.size();\n4375\t          const std::string rsite = pc->location.as_string();\n4376\t          // The frontend's positive normal-exit marker (see classify_exit).\n4377\t          // Read from the RETURN instruction itself, so a synthesised\n4378\t          // rollback RETURN — which carries no marker — cannot borrow it.\n4379\t          const bool src_return = pc->location.get_bool(\"sol_source_return\");\n4380\t          if (RK > 0 && RK <= SC_DECISION_MAX)\n4381\t          {\n4382\t            // Folded short-circuit operands in the returned expression are\n4383\t            // decisions like any other; each combination is its own exit.\n4384\t            for (uint64_t mask = 0; mask < (uint64_t(1) << RK); ++mask)\n4385\t            {\n4386\t              uint64_t e = enc, d = depth, h = idh;\n4387\t              occt o = occ;\n4388\t              bool overflowed = false;\n4389\t              for (size_t j = 0; j < RK; ++j)\n4390\t              {\n4391\t                if (e >= (uint64_t(1) << 62))\n4392\t                {\n4393\t                  overflowed = true;\n4394\t                  break;\n4395\t                }\n4396\t                const bool bit = ((mask >> j) & 1) != 0;\n4397\t                e = e * 2 + (bit ? 1 : 0);\n4398\t                h = step_id(h, o, rsite, (unsigned)j, bit);\n4399\t                note_decision(e, pc->location, rops[j], (unsigned)j);\n4400\t                ++d;\n4401\t              }\n4402\t              if (overflowed)\n4403\t              {\n4404\t                ++dropped_paths;\n4405\t                break;\n4406\t              }\n4407\t              if (!emit_exit(pc, e, d, false, h))\n4408\t                break;\n4409\t              classify_exit(\n4410\t                to_insert.size() - 1,\n4411\t                rolled_back,\n4412\t                saw_epilogue,\n4413\t                src_return,\n4414\t                rsite);\n4415\t              if (rolled_back)\n4416\t              {\n4417\t                ++rolled_back_return_exits;\n4418\t                rolled_back_return_locs.push_back(pc->location.as_string());\n4419\t              }\n4420\t            }\n4421\t          }\n4422\t          else if (emit_exit(pc, enc, depth, false, idh))\n4423\t          {\n4424\t            classify_exit(\n4425\t              to_insert.size() - 1,\n4426\t              rolled_back,\n4427\t              saw_epilogue,\n4428\t              src_return,\n4429\t              rsite);\n4430\t            if (rolled_back)\n4431\t            {\n4432\t              ++rolled_back_return_exits;\n4433\t              rolled_back_return_locs.push_back(pc->location.as_string());\n4434\t            }\n4435\t          }\n4436\t          break;\n4437\t        }\n4438\t        // Folded short-circuit/ternary operands (no control-flow branch):\n4439\t        // each was snapshotted into tr in Phase 1. Fan the DFS out over the\n4440\t        // 2^K operand-value combinations, appending K bits to enc/depth (in\n4441\t        // collect order, matching tr) so each combination is a distinct path.\n4442\t        if (\n4443\t          pc->is_assign() &&\n4444\t          pc->location.property().as_string() != \"skipped\")\n4445\t        {\n4446\t          const expr2tc &src = to_code_assign2t(pc->code).source;\n4447\t          // Collected rather than counted, for the same reason as the RETURN\n4448\t          // arm above: the recorder needs the operand expression.\n4449\t          std::vector<expr2tc> aops;\n4450\t          collect_short_circuit_decisions(\n4451\t            src, [&](const expr2tc &e) { aops.push_back(e); });\n4452\t          const size_t K = aops.size();\n4453\t          // Cap MUST match Phase 1's (see SC_DECISION_MAX): a site Phase 1\n4454\t          // skipped contributes nothing to tr/cnt, so the DFS must not add bits\n4455\t          // for it either — and vice versa.\n4456\t          if (K > 0 && K <= SC_DECISION_MAX)\n4457\t          {\n4458\t            bool overflowed = false;\n4459\t            const std::string asite = pc->location.as_string();\n4460\t            for (uint64_t mask = 0; mask < (uint64_t(1) << K); ++mask)\n4461\t            {\n4462\t              uint64_t e = enc, d = depth, h = idh;\n4463\t              occt o = occ;\n4464\t              for (size_t j = 0; j < K; ++j)\n4465\t              {\n4466\t                if (e >= (uint64_t(1) << 62))\n4467\t                {\n4468\t                  overflowed = true;\n4469\t                  break;\n4470\t                }\n4471\t                const bool bit = ((mask >> j) & 1) != 0;\n4472\t                e = e * 2 + (bit ? 1 : 0);\n4473\t                h = step_id(h, o, asite, (unsigned)j, bit);\n4474\t                note_decision(e, pc->location, aops[j], (unsigned)j);\n4475\t                ++d;\n4476\t              }\n4477\t              if (overflowed)\n4478\t              {\n4479\t                ++dropped_paths;\n4480\t                break;\n4481\t              }\n4482\t              if (++pushes > push_cap)\n4483\t              {\n4484\t                capped = true;\n4485\t                ++dropped_paths;\n4486\t                break;\n4487\t              }\n4488\t              stack.push_back(\n4489\t                {std::next(pc), e, becnt, d, rolled_back, saw_epilogue, h, o});\n4490\t            }\n4491\t            break; // this path forked into the 2^K continuations\n4492\t          }\n4493\t        }\n4494\t        pc = std::next(pc); // straight-line\n4495\t      }\n4496\t      if (capped)\n4497\t        break;\n4498\t    }\n4499\t\n4500\t    // Did this unit lose paths to the per-unit goal cap / length cap?\n4501\t    //\n4502\t    // Truncation WEAKENS the assertions this unit can support. It does NOT make\n4503\t    // them wrong, and the distinction is mechanical rather than a judgement\n4504\t    // call:\n4505\t    //\n4506\t    //   the certification query is `assume(L <= x <= U); assert(tr == pi)`.\n4507\t    //   The goal cap limits how many EXIT ASSERTS are emitted; it does not touch\n4508\t    //   the Phase-1 accounting, which still updates `tr`/`cnt` at every decision\n4509\t    //   of every path. So an input that walks a DROPPED path pi'' still carries\n4510\t    //   pi'''s number in `tr` at the exit, the query `tr == pi` fails on it, and\n4511\t    //   the candidate interval is rejected and shrunk. Certification therefore\n4512\t    //   never needs the dropped path to have been enumerated — it only needs the\n4513\t    //   accounting, which is intact.\n4514\t    //\n4515\t    // That is what separates this from a `require` lowered to a control-flow-free\n4516\t    // assume, which stays a named obstacle: there the reverting execution does\n4517\t    // not exist in the model AT ALL, so no query can see it and no interval can\n4518\t    // be shrunk away from it. Existing-but-unenumerated and non-existent are not\n4519\t    // the same failure, and only the second can ship a test that is red on the\n4520\t    // unmodified contract.\n4521\t    //\n4522\t    // For completeness, the other two ways paths go missing:\n4523\t    //   * a call left unexpanded (depth bound, or a withdrawal by degradation)\n4524\t    //     COARSENS the recorded decision sequence. The classes still partition\n4525\t    //     the input space, so this is sound and weaker.\n4526\t    //   * a loop cut at the unwind bound is cut IN BOTH PLACES — symex assumes\n4527\t    //     away the same over-bound iterations. Inside the declared bound the\n4528\t    //     domain is complete; outside it, the model and the real chain diverge\n4529\t    //     and the certification query cannot see that either. That is a declared\n4530\t    //     bound of the method rather than a defect, so it belongs in the\n4531\t    //     proposition's wording, not here.\n4532\t    //\n4533\t    // So this is reported as an absolute count and a strength annotation, and\n4534\t    // degradation exists precisely so it should not be reached at all.\n4535\t    const bool unit_truncated =\n4536\t      capped || dropped_paths > dropped_before_unit;\n4537\t\n4538\t    // ---- Path-count distribution measurement ----\n4539\t    {\n4540\t      const std::string uname = f_it->first.as_string();\n4541\t      const size_t after = to_insert.size();\n4542\t      if (after > max_unit_paths)\n4543\t      {\n4544\t        max_unit_paths = after;\n4545\t        max_unit_name = uname;\n4546\t      }\n4547\t      if (unit_truncated)\n4548\t      {\n4549\t        ++units_at_cap;\n4550\t        // ORDERING INVARIANT, reported rather than assumed: degradation runs\n4551\t        // first and is supposed to bring every unit inside the budget, so in\n4552\t        // the intended steady state the goal cap never fires. That it fired is\n4553\t        // therefore a result in its own right, and the two ways it can happen\n4554\t        // say different things — hence they are distinguished here instead of\n4555\t        // being lumped into one \"capped\" count.\n4556\t        auto bs = budget_state.find(uname);\n4557\t        const budget_statet st =\n4558\t          bs == budget_state.end() ? budget_statet::fits : bs->second;\n4559\t        switch (st)\n4560\t        {\n4561\t        case budget_statet::degraded_over:\n4562\t          log_warning(\n4563\t            \"--solidity-path-coverage: unit '{}' hit the goal cap ({}) after \"\n4564\t            \"degradation withdrew every one of its {} withdrawable call \"\n4565\t            \"point(s) and it was STILL over budget. Expected, not a policy \"\n4566\t            \"failure: the unit's own source decisions exceed the budget, so \"\n4567\t            \"there was nothing left to give up\",\n4568\t            uname,\n4569\t            path_cov_max_goals,\n4570\t            degraded_call_sites[uname].size());\n4571\t          break;\n4572\t        case budget_statet::no_candidates:\n4573\t          log_warning(\n4574\t            \"--solidity-path-coverage: unit '{}' hit the goal cap ({}) with no \"\n4575\t            \"withdrawable call point to degrade (warned above). Expected, not \"\n4576\t            \"a policy failure\",\n4577\t            uname,\n4578\t            path_cov_max_goals);\n4579\t          break;\n4580\t        case budget_statet::degraded_fits:\n4581\t          // NOT a defect, and deliberately not worded as one. Degradation\n4582\t          // stopped because the flat counter said the unit fits; the cap then\n4583\t          // fired on a count produced by the enumerating DFS. Two different\n4584\t          // computations of \"how many paths\" — that is the point of keeping\n4585\t          // them separate (a DFS bug cannot hide in both) and the price is that\n4586\t          // their COUNTING UNITS can differ. Both numbers are printed so the\n4587\t          // question \"is this the same quantity?\" can be answered by looking,\n4588\t          // rather than by opening an investigation into a bug that may not\n4589\t          // exist.\n4590\t          log_warning(\n4591\t            \"--solidity-path-coverage: unit '{}' hit the goal cap ({}) after \"\n4592\t            \"degradation withdrew {} call point(s) and stopped, because the \"\n4593\t            \"pre-enumeration count then read {} (within budget). The \"\n4594\t            \"enumeration produced {}. These are two different computations, so \"\n4595\t            \"a gap here means their counting units disagree — reconcile the two \"\n4596\t            \"definitions; it is not by itself a defect. If they DO agree, the \"\n4597\t            \"degradation policy simply stopped one withdrawal too early\",\n4598\t            uname,\n4599\t            path_cov_max_goals,\n4600\t            degraded_call_sites[uname].size(),\n4601\t            estimated_paths[uname],\n4602\t            after);\n4603\t          break;\n4604\t        case budget_statet::fits:\n4605\t          log_warning(\n4606\t            \"--solidity-path-coverage: unit '{}' hit the goal cap ({}) but its \"\n4607\t            \"pre-enumeration count was {}, inside the budget, so degradation \"\n4608\t            \"was never offered the unit — while the enumeration produced {}. \"\n4609\t            \"This is the one case that IS a defect: the number the budget \"\n4610\t            \"decision was taken on is not the number the enumeration produces, \"\n4611\t            \"and nothing in the pipeline noticed\",\n4612\t            uname,\n4613\t            path_cov_max_goals,\n4614\t            estimated_paths[uname],\n4615\t            after);\n4616\t          break;\n4617\t        }\n4618\t      }\n4619\t\n4620\t      size_t before = 0;\n4621\t      auto snap = pre_inline_body.find(uname);\n4622\t      if (snap != pre_inline_body.end())\n4623\t      {\n4624\t        bool snap_capped = false;\n4625\t        before = count_paths_no_instrument(\n4626\t          snap->second, ns, path_cov_unwind, path_cov_max_goals, snap_capped);\n4627\t        pre_expansion_total += before;\n4628\t\n4629\t        // The measurement is itself measured. When nothing was expanded into\n4630\t        // this unit, the counter and the real enumeration are looking at the\n4631\t        // same program and MUST agree — after discounting the ABI gate, which\n4632\t        // is inserted after the snapshot and contributes exactly one path. A\n4633\t        // mismatch means the two traversals have drifted, which would silently\n4634\t        // corrupt every ratio computed from them.\n4635\t        const size_t after_no_gate = after - (gate_inserted && after > 0 ? 1 : 0);\n4636\t        if (\n4637\t          expanded_into_unit[uname] == 0 && !capped && !snap_capped &&\n4638\t          !loop_truncated && before != after_no_gate)\n4639\t        {\n4640\t          log_error(\n4641\t            \"--solidity-path-coverage: INTERNAL DEFECT: the path counter and \"\n4642\t            \"the path enumeration disagree on unit '{}' ({} vs {}) even though \"\n4643\t            \"nothing was expanded into it and no bound was hit. The two \"\n4644\t            \"traversals have drifted, so every expansion ratio derived from \"\n4645\t            \"them would be wrong.\",\n4646\t            uname,\n4647\t            before,\n4648\t            after_no_gate);\n4649\t          abort();\n4650\t        }\n4651\t      }\n4652\t      log_debug(\n4653\t        \"coverage\",\n4654\t        \"unit '{}': {} path(s) after expansion, {} before, {} call(s) expanded\",\n4655\t        uname,\n4656\t        after,\n4657\t        before,\n4658\t        expanded_into_unit[uname]);\n4659\t    }\n4660\t\n4661\t    // ---- Report WHY this unit has undetermined exits (grouped by cause) ----\n4662\t    if (!undetermined_exits.empty())\n4663\t    {\n4664\t      // The three causes must account for every undetermined exit. This is a\n4665\t      // \"two counts agree\" property, independent of how any exit is classified,\n4666\t      // so it stays true whatever the frontend does next — unlike an assertion\n4667\t      // that forbids a particular outcome, which pins the symptom of whatever\n4668\t      // was broken when it was written.\n4669\t      const size_t summed =\n4670\t        und_no_epilogue + und_epilogue_skipped + und_return_unmarked;\n4671\t      if (summed != undetermined_exits.size())\n4672\t      {\n4673\t        log_error(\n4674\t          \"--solidity-path-coverage: INTERNAL DEFECT in unit '{}': {} exit(s) \"\n4675\t          \"were classified undetermined but only {} of them were attributed to \"\n4676\t          \"a cause. An undetermined exit with no recorded cause means a fourth \"\n4677\t          \"route into the class exists and the breakdown below is silently \"\n4678\t          \"incomplete.\",\n4679\t          id2string(f_it->first),\n4680\t          undetermined_exits.size(),\n4681\t          summed);\n4682\t        abort();\n4683\t      }\n4684\t      // An END_FUNCTION instruction carries no source location, so its set is\n4685\t      // legitimately empty. Say that, rather than printing `[]` — an empty\n4686\t      // bracket reads like \"the locations were lost\", which would send someone\n4687\t      // looking for a bug in the reporting instead of at the named unit.\n4688\t      auto join = [](const std::set<std::string> &s) {\n4689\t        std::string out;\n4690\t        for (const auto &e : s)\n4691\t          out += (out.empty() ? \"\" : \"; \") + e;\n4692\t        return out.empty() ? std::string(\"no source location on the exit \"\n4693\t                                         \"instruction; see the unit named above\")\n4694\t                           : out;\n4695\t      };\n4696\t      log_warning(\n4697\t        \"--solidity-path-coverage: unit '{}' has {} exit(s) with NO positive \"\n4698\t        \"evidence of a normal exit, by cause: \"\n4699\t        \"(1) {} at END_FUNCTION in a unit with NO epilogue at all [{}]; \"\n4700\t        \"(2) {} at END_FUNCTION having SKIPPED this unit's epilogue [{}]; \"\n4701\t        \"(3) {} at a RETURN carrying no `sol_source_return` marker [{}]. \"\n4702\t        \"Each cause is missing a DIFFERENT witness and needs a different fix; \"\n4703\t        \"an undetermined exit cannot become an oracle, so these are the paths \"\n4704\t        \"R0 cannot serve\",\n4705\t        id2string(f_it->first),\n4706\t        undetermined_exits.size(),\n4707\t        und_no_epilogue,\n4708\t        join(und_locs_no_epilogue),\n4709\t        und_epilogue_skipped,\n4710\t        join(und_locs_epilogue_skipped),\n4711\t        und_return_unmarked,\n4712\t        join(und_locs_return_unmarked));\n4713\t    }\n4714\t\n4715\t    if (rolled_back_return_exits > 0)\n4716\t    {\n4717\t      std::string where;\n4718\t      for (const auto &l : rolled_back_return_locs)\n4719\t        where += (where.empty() ? \"\" : \"; \") + l;\n4720\t      // Every such path must have been classified as a rollback revert. If one\n4721\t      // ever escapes that classification it would be reported as an ordinary\n4722\t      // exit of a transaction that in fact reverted — the single wrong answer\n4723\t      // this classifier must never give.\n4724\t      //\n4725\t      // Stated as a COUNT, not as \"no RETURN exit may be ordinary\". The older\n4726\t      // form asserted the latter, which was equivalent only while a RETURN\n4727\t      // could never be classified normal at all: the epilogue that would have\n4728\t      // proved it is emitted after the RETURN. Now that the frontend marks its\n4729\t      // source-level returns, a RETURN exit CAN legitimately be normal, and the\n4730\t      // old form fired on the first correct classification — it was pinning an\n4731\t      // artefact of the missing evidence, not the property it names.\n4732\t      size_t rb_return_exits_classified = 0;\n4733\t      for (size_t i = 0; i < to_insert.size(); ++i)\n4734\t        if (std::get<0>(to_insert[i])->is_return() && rollback_exits.count(i))\n4735\t          ++rb_return_exits_classified;\n4736\t      if (rb_return_exits_classified != rolled_back_return_exits)\n4737\t      {\n4738\t        log_error(\n4739\t          \"--solidity-path-coverage: INTERNAL DEFECT in unit '{}': {} path(s) \"\n4740\t          \"walked a rollback/revert marker and ended at a RETURN ({}), but \"\n4741\t          \"only {} of them were classified as reverting exits. The rest would \"\n4742\t          \"be reported as ordinary exits of transactions that in fact \"\n4743\t          \"reverted.\",\n4744\t          id2string(f_it->first),\n4745\t          rolled_back_return_exits,\n4746\t          where,\n4747\t          rb_return_exits_classified);\n4748\t        abort();\n4749\t      }\n4750\t      log_debug(\n4751\t        \"coverage\",\n4752\t        \"unit '{}': {} path(s) end at a RETURN after a rollback/revert marker \"\n4753\t        \"({}) — expected: the frontend lowers a failing require in a \"\n4754\t        \"value-returning function to a restore-and-return block\",\n4755\t        id2string(f_it->first),\n4756\t        rolled_back_return_exits,\n4757\t        where);\n4758\t    }\n4759\t\n4760\t    // ---- `tr` completeness check (see the declaration above) ----\n4761\t    //\n4762\t    // Runs BEFORE the exit census so that, if both would fire, the reader sees\n4763\t    // the accumulator problem first: an unaccounted decision makes every path\n4764\t    // through it uncoverable, which then also shows up as a missing exit. Order\n4765\t    // the diagnosis from cause to symptom.\n4766\t    {\n4767\t      std::vector<std::string> unaccounted;\n4768\t      for (const auto &[site, sub] : dfs_decision_sites)\n4769\t        if (phase1_decision_sites.count({site, sub}) == 0)\n4770\t          unaccounted.push_back(site + \" (operand \" + std::to_string(sub) + \")\");\n4771\t      if (!unaccounted.empty())\n4772\t      {\n4773\t        std::string where;\n4774\t        for (const auto &u : unaccounted)\n4775\t          where += (where.empty() ? \"\" : \"; \") + u;\n4776\t        log_error(\n4777\t          \"--solidity-path-coverage: INTERNAL DEFECT in unit '{}'. {} decision \"\n4778\t          \"site(s) are branched on by the path enumeration but are NOT \"\n4779\t          \"accumulated into `tr` at run time: {}. A path that walks over\n    // this instruction reverts, even though it reaches END_FUNCTION like a\n    // normal exit.\n    auto is_rollback_restore = [&](goto_programt::const_targett i) -> bool {\n      if (!i->is_assign() || !is_code_assign2t(i->code))\n        return false;\n      const expr2tc &src = to_code_assign2t(i->code).source;\n      return is_symbol2t(src) &&\n             to_symbol2t(src).thename.as_string().find(\"_sol_save_this\") !=\n               std::string::npos;\n    };\n\n    // True iff `i` is the frontend's explicit revert marker\n    // `_ESBMC_sol_mark_revert()`. Under the revert-observation gate (which\n    // --solidity-path-coverage turns on) EVERY require/revert failure edge\n    // carries this call, including the shapes that emit no state restore at\n    // all. It is the ONLY positive evidence separating a reverting exit from a\n    // plain early `return`: both otherwise lower to the identical\n    // `IF <guard> THEN GOTO <END_FUNCTION>`.\n    auto is_revert_mark = [&](goto_programt::const_targett i) -> bool {\n      if (!i->is_function_call() || !is_code_function_call2t(i->code))\n        return false;\n      const expr2tc &fn = to_code_function_call2t(i->code).function;\n      return is_symbol2t(fn) &&\n             to_symbol2t(fn).thename.as_string().find(\n               \"_ESBMC_sol_mark_revert\") != std::string::npos;\n    };\n\n    // True iff `i` is the function EPILOGUE's restore of the enclosing-contract\n    // context (`_ESBMC_enclosing_contract_address = _saved_encl_addr`). Every\n    // ordinary exit of a Solidity public function walks through it; a\n    // `require`-failure edge that precedes any state write is compiled as a\n    // BARE jump straight to END_FUNCTION and skips it. That makes \"did this\n    // path pass the epilogue?\" the only positive evidence available to tell an\n    // ordinary exit from such a bare revert edge.\n    auto is_epilogue_restore = [&](goto_programt::const_targett i) -> bool {\n      if (!i->is_assign() || !is_code_assign2t(i->code))\n        return false;\n      // An expanded callee brings its OWN epilogue along, and it matches the\n      // same symbol name. Counting it would let a path that ran the callee's\n      // epilogue and then took the caller's bare revert edge look like an\n      // ordinary exit. Only THIS unit's epilogue is evidence about this unit's\n      // exit, so instructions flagged by the expansion are not evidence.\n      if (i->location.get_bool(\"sol_path_inlined\"))\n        return false;\n      const expr2tc &src = to_code_assign2t(i->code).source;\n      return is_symbol2t(src) &&\n             to_symbol2t(src).thename.as_string().find(\"_saved_encl_addr\") !=\n               std::string::npos;\n    };\n\n    // Does this function HAVE an epilogue at all? Without one the marker above\n    // carries no information, so every path would look \"bypassed\" and be\n    // reported undetermined. Only apply the test where it is meaningful.\n    bool has_epilogue = false;\n    forall_goto_program_instructions (eit, goto_program)\n      if (is_epilogue_restore(eit))\n      {\n        has_epilogue = true;\n        break;\n      }\n\n    auto is_error_call = [&](goto_programt::const_targett i) -> bool {\n      if (!i->is_function_call() || !is_code_function_call2t(i->code))\n        return false;\n      const expr2tc &fn = to_code_function_call2t(i->code).function;\n      if (!is_symbol2t(fn))\n        return false;\n      const symbolt *s = ns.lookup(to_symbol2t(fn).thename);\n      return s && !s->type.get(\"#sol_error\").as_string().empty();\n    };\n\n    // \"A rolled-back execution never reaches a RETURN\" — MEASURED AND REFUTED.\n    //\n    // Had it held, reaching a RETURN would have been POSITIVE evidence of a\n    // normal exit, independent of the revert-observation gate and of which\n    // scopes that gate covers. It does not hold, and the reason is structural\n    // rather than a corner case: when the enclosing function returns a value,\n    // the frontend lowers a failing `require` to\n    //     { *this = _sol_save_this; return [nondet]; }\n    // so the reverting execution ends at a RETURN of the frontend's own making.\n    // Refuted on the simplest shape tried (compute a value, mutate state, then\n    // fail a require) and again on a modifier's require — the latter had been\n    // predicted to be a positive case, and is one only when the function\n    // returns nothing.\n    //\n    // Consequence, recorded so it is not quietly re-derived: the inference\n    // \"ends at a RETURN, therefore normal\" is NOT available. The counter below\n    // stays as an internal consistency check — such a path must always be\n    // classified as a rollback revert, never as normal — and is expected to be\n    // nonzero on ordinary contracts, so it logs at debug level rather than\n    // warning.\n    size_t rolled_back_return_exits = 0;\n    std::vector<std::string> rolled_back_return_locs;\n\n    // ---- WHY an exit came out `undetermined` ----\n    //\n    // `undetermined` means \"no positive evidence of a normal exit was found\".\n    // Since the frontend contract landed, every regression reports zero of them,\n    // so a nonzero count is now a hard signal rather than background noise — and\n    // a bare count says only THAT evidence is missing, never WHICH KIND. There\n    // are exactly three ways to get here, each missing a different witness, and\n    // they call for different fixes:\n    //\n    //   (1) the unit has NO epilogue at all, so the epilogue marker carries no\n    //       information for any of its paths (library / free-function scope);\n    //   (2) the unit HAS an epilogue and this path reached END_FUNCTION without\n    //       walking it — the bare-jump shape a pre-state-write `require` failure\n    //       and a plain early `return` share;\n    //   (3) the path ends at a RETURN carrying no `sol_source_return` marker and\n    //       walked no epilogue — either a return shape the frontend does not\n    //       stamp, or a RETURN the frontend synthesised for something else.\n    //\n    // Grouped per unit and by cause rather than listed per path: the lesson from\n    // chasing these one at a time is that two different defects can sit on the\n    // same function, and only a grouping shows which witness the whole group is\n    // missing.\n    size_t und_no_epilogue = 0;\n    size_t und_epilogue_skipped = 0;\n    size_t und_return_unmarked = 0;\n    std::set<std::string> und_locs_no_epilogue;\n    std::set<std::string> und_locs_epilogue_skipped;\n    std::set<std::string> und_locs_return_unmarked;\n\n    // Classify the exit just appended to `to_insert`. Shared by the\n    // END_FUNCTION arm and the RETURN arm so the two cannot drift apart.\n    //\n    // `src_return` is the frontend's POSITIVE marker (`sol_source_return`),\n    // stamped on RETURNs lowered from a source-level `return` and NOT on the\n    // one the frontend synthesises for a failing `require`\n    // (`{ *this = _sol_save_this; return [nondet]; }`). It is the second piece\n    // of positive evidence, alongside the epilogue: the epilogue cannot testify\n    // for a returning path because it is emitted after the RETURN, which is why\n    // every value-returning unit's normal exit used to be `undetermined`.\n    //\n    // The rollback test still runs FIRST and still wins. A source `return` can\n    // sit on a path that already walked a revert marker or a state restore, and\n    // on such a path the transaction reverts whatever the return statement says.\n    // Only a path with no rollback evidence AND an affirmative source-return\n    // marker is called normal — that is still a positive inference, not\n    // \"nothing said revert, so it must be fine\".\n    // (`se` can only be true when the function HAS an epilogue, since it is set\n    // by walking that very instruction — so the previous `!has_epilogue || !se`\n    // is exactly `!se`, and dropping the redundant term changes nothing.)\n    auto classify_exit = [&](\n                           size_t idx,\n                           bool rb,\n                           bool se,\n                           bool src_return,\n                           const std::string &site) {\n      if (rb)\n        rollback_exits.insert(idx);\n      else if (!se && !src_return)\n      {\n        undetermined_exits.insert(idx);\n        ++und_return_unmarked;\n        und_locs_return_unmarked.insert(site);\n      }\n    };\n\n    while (!stack.empty())\n    {\n      auto [pc, enc, becnt, depth, rolled_back, saw_epilogue, idh, occ] =\n        stack.back();\n      stack.pop_back();\n\n      while (true)\n      {\n        if (pc == goto_program.instructions.end() || pc->is_end_function())\n        {\n          if (pc != goto_program.instructions.end())\n          {\n            if (!emit_exit(pc, enc, depth, false, idh))\n              break;\n            const size_t idx = to_insert.size() - 1;\n            // An END_FUNCTION exit is never itself a source `return`: a bare\n            // `return;` lowers to a JUMP to END_FUNCTION, so the marker sits on\n            // the jump, not here. Such a path in a function WITH an epilogue\n            // already walks it and is normal on that evidence.\n            if (rolled_back)\n              // Positive evidence of a rollback revert.\n              rollback_exits.insert(idx);\n            else if (!has_epilogue || !saw_epilogue)\n              // No positive evidence of a normal exit. Either the path reached\n              // END_FUNCTION while SKIPPING the epilogue, or the function has\n              // no epilogue at all (library / free function — exactly the\n              // scopes the revert-observation gate does NOT mark, so a revert\n              // there carries no marker either). Both a `require` failing\n              // before any state write and a plain early `return` compile to\n              // this same shape, with nothing on the edge to separate them.\n              // Report undetermined rather than guess: calling it \"normal\"\n              // would claim a reverted transaction succeeded — measured on\n              // a library whose function reverts, that is exactly what the\n              // previous \"no epilogue => normal\" default did.\n              //\n              // The two sub-cases are counted apart (see the declaration): \"the\n              // unit has no epilogue at all\" is a scope problem affecting every\n              // path of the unit, while \"the epilogue exists and this path\n              // skipped it\" is a per-path shape. Fixing one does nothing for the\n              // other.\n              {\n                undetermined_exits.insert(idx);\n                if (has_epilogue)\n                {\n                  ++und_epilogue_skipped;\n                  und_locs_epilogue_skipped.insert(pc->location.as_string());\n                }\n                else\n                {\n                  ++und_no_epilogue;\n                  und_locs_no_epilogue.insert(pc->location.as_string());\n                }\n              }\n          }\n          break;\n        }\n        if (is_rollback_restore(pc) || is_revert_mark(pc))\n          rolled_back = true;\n        if (is_epilogue_restore(pc))\n          saw_epilogue = true;\n        // Custom-error revert exit: the DFS reached the `#sol_error` call\n        // (guarded, straight-line, or via an unconditional GOTO). Emit the\n        // identity assert HERE (upstream of the callee's ASSUME(false), so it is\n        // reachable) and stop; flag it for vm.expectRevert() (R0).\n        if (is_error_call(pc))\n        {\n          if (!emit_exit(pc, enc, depth, true, idh))\n            break;\n          break;\n        }\n        if (pc->is_goto())\n        {\n          const bool back = pc->is_backwards_goto();\n          if (is_true(pc->guard))\n          {\n            // Unconditional goto. A backward one is one iteration of the loop\n            // whose head is the goto's target; bound that loop independently.\n            if (back)\n            {\n              const unsigned key = pc->get_target()->target_number;\n              if (becnt[key] >= path_cov_unwind)\n              {\n                loop_truncated = true;\n                break; // this loop's bound reached: path truncated\n              }\n              ++becnt[key];\n            }\n            pc = pc->get_target();\n            continue;\n          }\n          // Conditional. Keep enc within 64 bits (leading sentinel + one bit\n          // per decision on the path); drop over-long paths rather than alias.\n          if (enc >= (uint64_t(1) << 62))\n          {\n            ++dropped_paths;\n            break;\n          }\n          // guard-true/taken successor -> target. If that edge is a loop\n          // back-edge, its own loop is bounded by path_cov_unwind.\n          bool take = true;\n          becntt becnt_taken = becnt;\n          if (back)\n          {\n            const unsigned key = pc->get_target()->target_number;\n            if (becnt_taken[key] >= path_cov_unwind)\n            {\n              take = false;\n              loop_truncated = true;\n            }\n            else\n              ++becnt_taken[key];\n          }\n          // Push the guard-true/taken successor; the guard-false/fall-through\n          // continues in-place. A reverting successor (custom-error revert) is\n          // detected at the top of the loop when the DFS reaches the\n          // `#sol_error` call instruction, so no per-edge revert test is needed.\n          const std::string dsite = pc->location.as_string();\n          if (take)\n          {\n            if (++pushes > push_cap)\n            {\n              capped = true;\n              ++dropped_paths;\n              break;\n            }\n            // Both arms consume the SAME occurrence of this site, so each starts\n            // from its own copy of the counters.\n            occt occ_taken = occ;\n            const uint64_t idh_taken =\n              step_id(idh, occ_taken, dsite, 0, /*polarity=*/true);\n            note_decision(enc * 2 + 1, pc->location, pc->guard, 0);\n            stack.push_back(\n              {pc->get_target(),\n               enc * 2 + 1,\n               becnt_taken,\n               depth + 1,\n               rolled_back,\n               saw_epilogue,\n               idh_taken,\n               occ_taken});\n          }\n          // guard-false/fallthrough successor -> next (never a back-edge).\n          idh = step_id(idh, occ, dsite, 0, /*polarity=*/false);\n          note_decision(enc * 2 + 0, pc->location, pc->guard, 0);\n          enc = enc * 2 + 0;\n          ++depth;\n          pc = std::next(pc);\n          continue;\n        }\n        // A RETURN is a path EXIT, not a straight-line instruction.\n        //\n        // symex terminates the frame at RETURN — it does not fall through to\n        // END_FUNCTION — so an identity assert placed at END_FUNCTION sits\n        // downstream of the frame exit and can never execute. Measured on four\n        // variants that isolate the cause: a unit that writes state and returns\n        // nothing covers 3/3, while the SAME body with a return value covers\n        // 1/3, and the one path that stays coverable is exactly the ABI\n        // value-reject path — the only one that reaches END_FUNCTION by a plain\n        // GOTO instead of through the RETURN. Purity, and whether an explicit\n        // `return` statement is written at all (a named return variable behaves\n        // identically), make no difference.\n        //\n        // Effect before this: EVERY unit with a return value had all of its body\n        // paths reported U — a systematic, silent deflation of coverage on any\n        // real contract, since getters and view functions all return values.\n        //\n        // Emitting here places the assert immediately BEFORE the RETURN:\n        // downstream of this path's tr/cnt updates (Phase 1 inserted those\n        // before the RETURN earlier, so they end up further from it) and\n        // upstream of the frame exit.\n        if (pc->is_return() && is_code_return2t(pc->code))\n        {\n          const expr2tc &rsrc = to_code_return2t(pc->code).operand;\n          // Collected, not merely counted: the operand EXPRESSION is what the\n          // branch metric keys its claim on, so recording the decision needs the\n          // operand itself. Collect order is the bit order (see the DFS below).\n          std::vector<expr2tc> rops;\n          if (pc->location.property().as_string() != \"skipped\")\n            collect_short_circuit_decisions(\n              rsrc, [&](const expr2tc &e) { rops.push_back(e); });\n          const size_t RK = rops.size();\n          const std::string rsite = pc->location.as_string();\n          // The frontend's positive normal-exit marker (see classify_exit).\n          // Read from the RETURN instruction itself, so a synthesised\n          // rollback RETURN — which carries no marker — cannot borrow it.\n          const bool src_return = pc->location.get_bool(\"sol_source_return\");\n          if (RK > 0 && RK <= SC_DECISION_MAX)\n          {\n            // Folded short-circuit operands in the returned expression are\n            // decisions like any other; each combination is its own exit.\n            for (uint64_t mask = 0; mask < (uint64_t(1) << RK); ++mask)\n            {\n              uint64_t e = enc, d = depth, h = idh;\n              occt o = occ;\n              bool overflowed = false;\n              for (size_t j = 0; j < RK; ++j)\n              {\n                if (e >= (uint64_t(1) << 62))\n                {\n                  overflowed = true;\n                  break;\n                }\n                const bool bit = ((mask >> j) & 1) != 0;\n                e = e * 2 + (bit ? 1 : 0);\n                h = step_id(h, o, rsite, (unsigned)j, bit);\n                note_decision(e, pc->location, rops[j], (unsigned)j);\n                ++d;\n              }\n              if (overflowed)\n              {\n                ++dropped_paths;\n                break;\n              }\n              if (!emit_exit(pc, e, d, false, h))\n                break;\n              classify_exit(\n                to_insert.size() - 1,\n                rolled_back,\n                saw_epilogue,\n                src_return,\n                rsite);\n              if (rolled_back)\n              {\n                ++rolled_back_return_exits;\n                rolled_back_return_locs.push_back(pc->location.as_string());\n              }\n            }\n          }\n          else if (emit_exit(pc, enc, depth, false, idh))\n          {\n            classify_exit(\n              to_insert.size() - 1,\n              rolled_back,\n              saw_epilogue,\n              src_return,\n              rsite);\n            if (rolled_back)\n            {\n              ++rolled_back_return_exits;\n              rolled_back_return_locs.push_back(pc->location.as_string());\n            }\n          }\n          break;\n        }\n        // Folded short-circuit/ternary operands (no control-flow branch):\n        // each was snapshotted into tr in Phase 1. Fan the DFS out over the\n        // 2^K operand-value combinations, appending K bits to enc/depth (in\n        // collect order, matching tr) so each combination is a distinct path.\n        if (\n          pc->is_assign() &&\n          pc->location.property().as_string() != \"skipped\")\n        {\n          const expr2tc &src = to_code_assign2t(pc->code).source;\n          // Collected rather than counted, for the same reason as the RETURN\n          // arm above: the recorder needs the operand expression.\n          std::vector<expr2tc> aops;\n          collect_short_circuit_decisions(\n            src, [&](const expr2tc &e) { aops.push_back(e); });\n          const size_t K = aops.size();\n          // Cap MUST match Phase 1's (see SC_DECISION_MAX): a site Phase 1\n          // skipped contributes nothing to tr/cnt, so the DFS must not add bits\n          // for it either — and vice versa.\n          if (K > 0 && K <= SC_DECISION_MAX)\n          {\n            bool overflowed = false;\n            const std::string asite = pc->location.as_string();\n            for (uint64_t mask = 0; mask < (uint64_t(1) << K); ++mask)\n            {\n              uint64_t e = enc, d = depth, h = idh;\n              occt o = occ;\n              for (size_t j = 0; j < K; ++j)\n              {\n                if (e >= (uint64_t(1) << 62))\n                {\n                  overflowed = true;\n                  break;\n                }\n                const bool bit = ((mask >> j) & 1) != 0;\n                e = e * 2 + (bit ? 1 : 0);\n                h = step_id(h, o, asite, (unsigned)j, bit);\n                note_decision(e, pc->location, aops[j], (unsigned)j);\n                ++d;\n              }\n              if (overflowed)\n              {\n                ++dropped_paths;\n                break;\n              }\n              if (++pushes > push_cap)\n              {\n                capped = true;\n                ++dropped_paths;\n                break;\n              }\n              stack.push_back(\n                {std::next(pc), e, becnt, d, rolled_back, saw_epilogue, h, o});\n            }\n            break; // this path forked into the 2^K continuations\n          }\n        }\n        pc = std::next(pc); // straight-line\n      }\n      if (capped)\n        break;\n    }\n\n    // Did this unit lose paths to the per-unit goal cap / length cap?\n    //\n    // Truncation WEAKENS the assertions this unit can support. It does NOT make\n    // them wrong, and the distinction is mechanical rather than a judgement\n    // call:\n    //\n    //   the certification query is `assume(L <= x <= U); assert(tr == pi)`.\n    //   The goal cap limits how many EXIT ASSERTS are emitted; it does not touch\n    //   the Phase-1 accounting, which still updates `tr`/`cnt` at every decision\n    //   of every path. So an input that walks a DROPPED path pi'' still carries\n    //   pi'''s number in `tr` at the exit, the query `tr == pi` fails on it, and\n    //   the candidate interval is rejected and shrunk. Certification therefore\n    //   never needs the dropped path to have been enumerated — it only needs the\n    //   accounting, which is intact.\n    //\n    // That is what separates this from a `require` lowered to a control-flow-free\n    // assume, which stays a named obstacle: there the reverting execution does\n    // not exist in the model AT ALL, so no query can see it and no interval can\n    // be shrunk away from it. Existing-but-unenumerated and non-existent are not\n    // the same failure, and only the second can ship a test that is red on the\n    // unmodified contract.\n    //\n    // For completeness, the other two ways paths go missing:\n    //   * a call left unexpanded (depth bound, or a withdrawal by degradation)\n    //     COARSENS the recorded decision sequence. The classes still partition\n    //     the input space, so this is sound and weaker.\n    //   * a loop cut at the unwind bound is cut IN BOTH PLACES — symex assumes\n    //     away the same over-bound iterations. Inside the declared bound the\n    //     domain is complete; outside it, the model and the real chain diverge\n    //     and the certification query cannot see that either. That is a declared\n    //     bound of the method rather than a defect, so it belongs in the\n    //     proposition's wording, not here.\n    //\n    // So this is reported as an absolute count and a strength annotation, and\n    // degradation exists precisely so it should not be reached at all.\n    const bool unit_truncated =\n      capped || dropped_paths > dropped_before_unit;\n\n    // ---- Path-count distribution measurement ----\n    {\n      const std::string uname = f_it->first.as_string();\n      const size_t after = to_insert.size();\n      if (after > max_unit_paths)\n      {\n        max_unit_paths = after;\n        max_unit_name = uname;\n      }\n      if (unit_truncated)\n      {\n        ++units_at_cap;\n        // ORDERING INVARIANT, reported rather than assumed: degradation runs\n        // first and is supposed to bring every unit inside the budget, so in\n        // the intended steady state the goal cap never fires. That it fired is\n        // therefore a result in its own right, and the two ways it can happen\n        // say different things — hence they are distinguished here instead of\n        // being lumped into one \"capped\" count.\n        auto bs = budget_state.find(uname);\n        const budget_statet st =\n          bs == budget_state.end() ? budget_statet::fits : bs->second;\n        switch (st)\n        {\n        case budget_statet::degraded_over:\n          log_warning(\n            \"--solidity-path-coverage: unit '{}' hit the goal cap ({}) after \"\n            \"degradation withdrew every one of its {} withdrawable call \"\n            \"point(s) and it was STILL over budget. Expected, not a policy \"\n            \"failure: the unit's own source decisions exceed the budget, so \"\n            \"there was nothing left to give up\",\n            uname,\n            path_cov_max_goals,\n            degraded_call_sites[uname].size());\n          break;\n        case budget_statet::no_candidates:\n          log_warning(\n            \"--solidity-path-coverage: unit '{}' hit the goal cap ({}) with no \"\n            \"withdrawable call point to degrade (warned above). Expected, not \"\n            \"a policy failure\",\n            uname,\n            path_cov_max_goals);\n          break;\n        case budget_statet::degraded_fits:\n          // NOT a defect, and deliberately not worded as one. Degradation\n          // stopped because the flat counter said the unit fits; the cap then\n          // fired on a count produced by the enumerating DFS. Two different\n          // computations of \"how many paths\" — that is the point of keeping\n          // them separate (a DFS bug cannot hide in both) and the price is that\n          // their COUNTING UNITS can differ. Both numbers are printed so the\n          // question \"is this the same quantity?\" can be answered by looking,\n          // rather than by opening an investigation into a bug that may not\n          // exist.\n          log_warning(\n            \"--solidity-path-coverage: unit '{}' hit the goal cap ({}) after \"\n            \"degradation withdrew {} call point(s) and stopped, because the \"\n            \"pre-enumeration count then read {} (within budget). The \"\n            \"enumeration produced {}. These are two different computations, so \"\n            \"a gap here means their counting units disagree — reconcile the two \"\n            \"definitions; it is not by itself a defect. If they DO agree, the \"\n            \"degradation policy simply stopped one withdrawal too early\",\n            uname,\n            path_cov_max_goals,\n            degraded_call_sites[uname].size(),\n            estimated_paths[uname],\n            after);\n          break;\n        case budget_statet::fits:\n          log_warning(\n            \"--solidity-path-coverage: unit '{}' hit the goal cap ({}) but its \"\n            \"pre-enumeration count was {}, inside the budget, so degradation \"\n            \"was never offered the unit — while the enumeration produced {}. \"\n            \"This is the one case that IS a defect: the number the budget \"\n            \"decision was taken on is not the number the enumeration produces, \"\n            \"and nothing in the pipeline noticed\",\n            uname,\n            path_cov_max_goals,\n            estimated_paths[uname],\n            after);\n          break;\n        }\n      }\n\n      size_t before = 0;\n      auto snap = pre_inline_body.find(uname);\n      if (snap != pre_inline_body.end())\n      {\n        bool snap_capped = false;\n        before = count_paths_no_instrument(\n          snap->second, ns, path_cov_unwind, path_cov_max_goals, snap_capped);\n        pre_expansion_total += before;\n\n        // The measurement is itself measured. A\n        // mismatch means the two traversals have drifted, which would silently\n        // corrupt every ratio computed from them.\n        const size_t after_no_gate = after - (gate_inserted && after > 0 ? 1 : 0);\n        if (\n          expanded_into_unit[uname] == 0 && !capped && !snap_capped &&\n          !loop_truncated && before != after_no_gate)\n        {\n          log_error(\n            \"--solidity-path-coverage: INTERNAL DEFECT: the path counter and \"\n            \"the path enumeration disagree on unit '{}' ({} vs {}) even though \"\n            \"nothing was expanded into it and no bound was hit.
