Emitting no probe leaves\n5055\t          // it out of `bounds` entirely, so no bound is ever attributed to it —\n5056\t          // and it is recorded by name so the omission is visible instead of\n5057\t          // reading as \"measured, and it came out as the whole type\".\n5058\t          path_cov_refused_coords[c.name] = why;\n5059\t          log_warning(\n5060\t            \"--path-cov-outer-box: unit '{}' — REFUSING coordinate '{}': {}. No \"\n5061\t            \"probe is emitted for it and no bound is attributed to it; the \"\n5062\t            \"remaining coordinates are measured as usual. This is a refusal, \"\n5063\t            \"NOT a measurement of the full type range: those two are the same \"\n5064\t            \"constraint to the solver and opposite claims to a reader\",\n5065\t            uid,\n5066\t            c.name,\n5067\t            why);\n5068\t          continue;\n5069\t        }\n5070\t        const type2tc ct = cexpr->type;\n5071\t        symbolt ssym;\n5072\t        ssym.type = migrate_type_back(ct);\n5073\t        ssym.name = \"__ESBMC_outer$\" + i2string(ghost_counter++);\n5074\t        ssym.id = \"path_cov::\" + id2string(ssym.name);\n5075\t        ssym.lvalue = true;\n5076\t        ssym.static_lifetime = false;\n5077\t        ssym.is_extern = false;\n5078\t        symbolt *psn;\n5079\t        cov_context->move(ssym, psn);\n5080\t        expr2tc sn = symbol2tc(migrate_type(psn->type), psn->id);\n5081\t        auto entry = goto_program.instructions.begin();\n5082\t        goto_programt::instructiont dcl;\n5083\t        dcl.type = DECL;\n5084\t        dcl.code = code_decl2tc(ct, psn->id);\n5085\t        dcl.location = entry->location;\n5086\t        dcl.location.property(\"skipped\");\n5087\t        dcl.function = entry->location.get_function();\n5088\t        goto_program.instructions.insert(entry, dcl);\n5089\t        goto_programt::instructiont asg;\n5090\t        asg.type = ASSIGN;\n5091\t        asg.code = code_assign2tc(sn, cexpr);\n5092\t        asg.location = entry->location;\n5093\t        asg.location.property(\"skipped\");\n5094\t        asg.function = entry->location.get_function();\n5095\t        goto_program.instructions.insert(entry, asg);\n5096\t        snap[c.name] = sn;\n5097\t        // The type's own range, taken without asking the solver anything.\n5098\t        if (is_unsignedbv_type(ct))\n5099\t        {\n5100\t          BigInt hi = 1;\n5101\t          for (unsigned b = 0; b < ct->get_width(); ++b)\n5102\t            hi *= 2;\n5103\t          path_cov_outer_box_type_range[c.name] = {\"0\", integer2string(hi - 1)};\n5104\t          // PUBLISHED, not just used internally. The driver chooses the ladder\n5105\t          // and cannot choose it correctly without knowing how wide the\n5106\t          // coordinate is -- measured: the geometric ladder lays probes up to\n5107\t          // 2^255 whatever the type is, so on a 160-bit `address` the\n5108\t          // out-of-type values WRAP, the bracket comes back claiming a holding\n5109\t          // lower bound of 2^255 on a type that stops at 2^160-1, and the\n5110\t          // driver's next span is inverted. The tool had this number the whole\n5111\t          // time and kept it to itself.\n5112\t          log_status(\n5113\t            \"--path-cov-outer-box: coordinate '{}' has TYPE RANGE [0, {}] \"\n5114\t            \"({}-bit unsigned). Probe values outside it are meaningless: a \"\n5115\t            \"bound is built as a constant of this type, so an out-of-range \"\n5116\t            \"value wraps and the probe asks about a different number\",\n5117\t            c.name,\n5118\t            integer2string(hi - 1),\n5119\t            ct->get_width());\n5120\t        }\n5121\t      }\n5122\t\n5123\t      // A pin whose coordinate was refused cannot be established, so it must\n5124\t      // stop being CLAIMED. The pins are what every measured and every\n5125\t      // subtracted region below is labelled with (\"measured under bal == 0\"),\n5126\t      // and an unapplied pin left in that label describes a slice nothing was\n5127\t      // restricted to. Dropping it from the antecedent instead makes the run\n5128\t      // measure a LARGER slice — less informative, and honestly labelled.\n5129\t      std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> pins_applied;\n5130\t      for (const auto &p : outer_pins)\n5131\t        if (snap.count(p.first) != 0)\n5132\t          pins_applied.push_back(p);\n5133\t      if (pins_applied.size() != outer_pins.size())\n5134\t        log_warning(\n5135\t          \"--path-cov-outer-box: unit '{}' — {} of {} requested pin(s) name a \"\n5136\t          \"REFUSED coordinate and were NOT applied. Every region below is \"\n5137\t          \"therefore a statement about a WIDER slice than the one requested, \"\n5138\t          \"and is labelled with the pins that were actually applied — never \"\n5139\t          \"with the ones that were asked for\",\n5140\t          uid,\n5141\t          outer_pins.size() - pins_applied.size(),\n5142\t          outer_pins.size());\n5143\t      path_cov_outer_box_pins = pins_applied;\n5144\t\n5145\t      // Each path's ladder goes at THAT path's own exit. Putting every probe at\n5146\t      // every exit would multiply the claim count by the number of exits for no\n5147\t      // information: at another exit the antecedent `tr == enc` is false and the\n5148\t      // implication is vacuous.\n5149\t      size_t emitted = 0;\n5150\t      for (const auto &[penc, pdepth] : path_cov_outer_box_paths)\n5151\t      {\n5152\t        goto_programt::targett exit_pc;\n5153\t        bool found = false;\n5154\t        for (auto &e : to_insert)\n5155\t        {\n5156\t          const std::string &cm = std::get<2>(e);\n5157\t          const size_t q = cm.rfind(\":path:\");\n5158\t          if (q == std::string::npos)\n5159\t            continue;\n5160\t          if (strtoull(cm.substr(q + 6).c_str(), nullptr, 10) == penc)\n5161\t          {\n5162\t            exit_pc = std::get<0>(e);\n5163\t            found = true;\n5164\t            break;\n5165\t          }\n5166\t        }\n5167\t        if (!found)\n5168\t        {\n5169\t          log_warning(\n5170\t            \"--path-cov-outer-box: path enc={} is not among this unit's \"\n5171\t            \"enumerated paths; no probe emitted for it, and it therefore also \"\n5172\t            \"contributes NOTHING to the sibling subtraction — which makes every \"\n5173\t            \"other path's certified region a claim about a partition that is \"\n5174\t            \"missing a part\",\n5175\t            penc);\n5176\t          continue;\n5177\t        }\n5178\t        // The ordered decision sequence, walked out of `enc`. Printed per path\n5179\t        // so that two paths the payload cannot separate can be compared HERE:\n5180\t        // their sequences agree up to the decision that splits them, and the\n5181\t        // guard at that source line is where the separating quantity is written.\n5182\t        // That is the one place it can be named when it is absent from the\n5183\t        // counterexample — which, measured, is every reach-gate path so far.\n5184\t        if (trace_decisions && pdepth > 0)\n5185\t        {\n5186\t          // Reads the PUBLISHED tables, not a second private copy: the log line\n5187\t          // and the report field are then the same data, so a defect in the\n5188\t          // recording cannot show up in one and not the other.\n5189\t          const auto &tbl = path_decision_table[uid];\n5190\t          const auto &idx = path_decision_index[uid];\n5191\t          std::string seq;\n5192\t          for (uint64_t k = 0; k < pdepth; ++k)\n5193\t          {\n5194\t            const uint64_t key = penc >> (pdepth - 1 - k);\n5195\t            auto dit = idx.find(key);\n5196\t            seq += \"\\n    #\" + std::to_string(k + 1) + \" \";\n5197\t            // A missing key is reported, not skipped. Silence here would read\n5198\t            // as \"this path has fewer decisions\", which is a claim about the\n5199\t            // path rather than about the recording.\n5200\t            if (dit == idx.end() || dit->second >= tbl.size())\n5201\t              seq += \"<not recorded — enc key \" + std::to_string(key) + \">\";\n5202\t            else\n5203\t            {\n5204\t              const auto &d = tbl[dit->second];\n5205\t              seq += d.loc + \" (operand \" + std::to_string(d.sub) + \") [guard \" +\n5206\t                     ((key & 1) ? \"TRUE\" : \"FALSE\") + \"]\" +\n5207\t                     (d.synthetic_abi_gate ? \" [synthesised ABI value gate]\"\n5208\t                                           : \"\");\n5209\t            }\n5210\t          }\n5211\t          log_status(\n5212\t            \"--path-cov-outer-box: path enc={} depth={} DECISION SEQUENCE (in \"\n5213\t            \"order; two paths diverge at the first index where these differ, \"\n5214\t            \"and the guard on that line names the quantity that separates \"\n5215\t            \"them):{}\",\n5216\t            penc,\n5217\t            pdepth,\n5218\t            seq);\n5219\t        }\n5220\t\n5221\t        // `tr != enc || cnt != depth || !pins || <bound>` — the implication,\n5222\t        // written out. The pins join the ANTECEDENT: the bound is then asserted\n5223\t        // only about the slice through them, which is exactly what makes a\n5224\t        // diagonal domain measurable at all.\n5225\t        expr2tc not_this_path = or2tc(\n5226\t          notequal2tc(tr, constant_int2tc(utype, BigInt(penc))),\n5227\t          notequal2tc(cnt, constant_int2tc(utype, BigInt(pdepth))));\n5228\t        for (const auto &[pname, pval] : pins_applied)\n5229\t        {\n5230\t          const expr2tc &pexpr = snap.at(pname);\n5231\t          not_this_path = or2tc(\n5232\t            not_this_path,\n5233\t            notequal2tc(\n5234\t              pexpr, constant_int2tc(pexpr->type, string2integer(pval))));\n5235\t        }\n5236\t        for (const auto &c : outer_coords)\n5237\t        {\n5238\t          // Refused above: no snapshot exists, so no probe can be built. Note\n5239\t          // `snap[c.name]` would CREATE a null entry here rather than tell us\n5240\t          // that — the lookup has to come first.\n5241\t          if (snap.count(c.name) == 0)\n5242\t            continue;\n5243\t          const type2tc ct = snap[c.name]->type;\n5244\t          // Either the driver's explicit values, or a uniform subdivision of\n5245\t          // [lo, hi]. Both end up as the same kind of probe; only the choice of\n5246\t          // where to put them differs, and that choice is policy.\n5247\t          std::vector<BigInt> probe_vals;\n5248\t          for (const auto &v : c.values)\n5249\t            probe_vals.push_back(string2integer(v));\n5250\t          if (c.subdivide)\n5251\t          {\n5252\t            const BigInt lo = string2integer(c.lo), hi = string2integer(c.hi);\n5253\t            if (hi < lo)\n5254\t            {\n5255\t              // exit, NOT abort. This is a malformed SPEC -- the caller handed\n5256\t              // in an inverted span -- and it is reachable from an ordinary\n5257\t              // driver bug: a bracket computed across a coordinate's wrapped\n5258\t              // probes produces exactly this. A SIGABRT turns a recordable\n5259\t              // refusal into a core dump, which unattended is the difference\n5260\t              // between a datum and a lost run; measured, that is how it\n5261\t              // surfaced.\n5262\t              log_error(\n5263\t                \"--path-cov-outer-box: REFUSING coordinate '{}': hi < lo \"\n5264\t                \"(lo={}, hi={}), so the span contains no probe value. This is a \"\n5265\t                \"malformed span in the SPEC, not a property of the path\",\n5266\t                c.name,\n5267\t                c.lo,\n5268\t                c.hi);\n5269\t              exit(1);\n5270\t            }\n5271\t            const BigInt span = hi - lo;\n5272\t            for (size_t k = 0; k <= outer_probes + 1; ++k)\n5273\t              probe_vals.push_back(\n5274\t                lo +\n5275\t                (span * BigInt((int64_t)k)) /\n5276\t                  BigInt((int64_t)(outer_probes + 1)));\n5277\t          }\n5278\t          // ---- DROP probe values the coordinate's type cannot hold ----\n5279\t          //\n5280\t          // The bound is `constant_int2tc(ct, v)`, so a value above the type's\n5281\t          // maximum WRAPS and the probe asks about a different number than the\n5282\t          // one the driver wrote down. That is not a weaker measurement, it is a\n5283\t          // wrong one: measured on a 160-bit `address`, the geometric ladder's\n5284\t          // 2^255 probe came back HOLDING as a lower bound -- on a type whose\n5285\t          // largest value is 2^160-1 -- and the driver's next span was inverted,\n5286\t          // which killed the whole loop.\n5287\t          //\n5288\t          // Dropped rather than clamped. Clamping invents a probe nobody asked\n5289\t          // for; dropping removes one that could not mean anything, and the\n5290\t          // type maximum is already seeded as the free bound, so nothing is\n5291\t          // lost. Counted and reported, because a silently shorter ladder is a\n5292\t          // silently coarser measurement.\n5293\t          size_t out_of_type = 0;\n5294\t          if (is_unsignedbv_type(ct))\n5295\t          {\n5296\t            BigInt tmax = 1;\n5297\t            for (unsigned b = 0; b < ct->get_width(); ++b)\n5298\t              tmax *= 2;\n5299\t            tmax -= 1;\n5300\t            std::vector<BigInt> kept;\n5301\t            kept.reserve(probe_vals.size());\n5302\t            for (const BigInt &v : probe_vals)\n5303\t            {\n5304\t              if (v >= 0 && v <= tmax)\n5305\t                kept.push_back(v);\n5306\t              else\n5307\t                ++out_of_type;\n5308\t            }\n5309\t            probe_vals.swap(kept);\n5310\t          }\n5311\t          // The two sources can overlap; a duplicated probe is a duplicated\n5312\t          // claim name, which collides in `all_claims` and silently drops one.\n5313\t          std::sort(probe_vals.begin(), probe_vals.end());\n5314\t          probe_vals.erase(\n5315\t            std::unique(probe_vals.begin(), probe_vals.end()),\n5316\t            probe_vals.end());\n5317\t          if (out_of_type > 0)\n5318\t            log_warning(\n5319\t              \"--path-cov-outer-box: coordinate '{}' — DROPPED {} probe \"\n5320\t              \"value(s) that do not fit its type; {} probe value(s) remain. \"\n5321\t              \"Those values would have been built as constants of this type and \"\n5322\t              \"WRAPPED, so each would have measured a different number than the \"\n5323\t              \"one requested. The ladder is correspondingly coarser here, which \"\n5324\t              \"is a resolution loss, not a wrong bound\",\n5325\t              c.name,\n5326\t              out_of_type,\n5327\t              probe_vals.size());\n5328\t          if (probe_vals.empty())\n5329\t          {\n5330\t            log_warning(\n5331\t              \"--path-cov-outer-box: coordinate '{}' — NO probe value survives \"\n5332\t              \"the type check, so NOTHING is measured on it and it appears in \"\n5333\t              \"no box below. Its absence is a refusal, not a measurement of the \"\n5334\t              \"full type range\",\n5335\t              c.name);\n5336\t            path_cov_refused_coords[c.name] =\n5337\t              \"every requested probe value lies outside the coordinate's own \"\n5338\t              \"type range, so every probe would have wrapped and measured a \"\n5339\t              \"different number\";\n5340\t            continue;\n5341\t          }\n5342\t          for (const BigInt &v : probe_vals)\n5343\t          {\n5344\t            for (int dir = 0; dir < 2; ++dir)\n5345\t            {\n5346\t              const bool upper = dir == 0;\n5347\t              const expr2tc cmp =\n5348\t                upper ? lessthanequal2tc(snap[c.name], constant_int2tc(ct, v))\n5349\t                      : greaterthanequal2tc(\n5350\t                          snap[c.name], constant_int2tc(ct, v));\n5351\t              const std::string comment =\n5352\t                id2string(f_it->first) + \":path:\" + std::to_string(penc) + \"#\" +\n5353\t                (upper ? \"ub\" : \"lb\") + \"_\" + c.name + \"_\" + integer2string(v);\n5354\t              const std::string loc = exit_pc->location.as_string();\n5355\t              all_claims.insert({comment, loc});\n5356\t              path_cov_outer_box_probes.push_back(\n5357\t                {penc, c.name, upper, integer2string(v), {comment, loc}});\n5358\t              insert_assert(\n5359\t                goto_program, exit_pc, or2tc(not_this_path, cmp), comment);\n5360\t              ++emitted;\n5361\t            }\n5362\t          }\n5363\t        }\n5364\t      }\n5365\t      log_status(\n5366\t        \"--path-cov-outer-box: unit '{}' — emitted {} ladder probe(s) as ONE \"\n5367\t        \"batch. The assumption is fixed per path and only the assertions vary, \"\n5368\t        \"which is exactly what lets a whole ladder be judged in a single run \"\n5369\t        \"instead of one query per widening step\",\n5370\t        uid,\n5371\t        emitted);\n5372\t      total_paths += emitted;\n5373\t      continue;\n5374\t    }\n5375\t\n5376\t    // ---- STAGE 2: the certification query ----\n5377\t    //\n5378\t    // Reached only with --path-cov-certify. Everything above still ran —\n5379\t    // expansion, the ABI gate, Phase-1 `tr`/`cnt` accounting, the\n5380\t    // `tr`-completeness invariant, the exit census, the decision-set census —\n5381\t    // because they are the defences, and certifying against accounting that\n5382\t    // nothing checked would be certifying nothing. It also matters that the\n5383\t    // query below reads the SAME `tr` the enumeration writes: the argument that\n5384\t    // certification is immune to goal-cap truncation is exactly \"the cap drops\n5385\t    // exit asserts, never the accounting\", and two separate accumulators would\n5386\t    // break it.\n5387\t    if (certify_on)\n5388\t    {\n5389\t      const std::string uid = f_it->first.as_string();\n5390\t      const bool is_target =\n5391\t        uid == certify_unit ||\n5392\t        uid.find(\"@F@\" + certify_unit + \"#\") != std::string::npos;\n5393\t      if (!is_target)\n5394\t        continue; // other units contribute nothing to this query\n5395\t\n5396\t      // 1. Assume the box at unit entry. Each bound names either a call\n5397\t      //    argument (resolved against this unit's own parameter list) or an EVM\n5398\t      //    environment value (`msg.value` etc.). An unresolvable name is FATAL:\n5399\t      //    silently dropping a bound would widen the box being certified beyond\n5400\t      //    what was asked for, and the run would still say SUCCESSFUL.\n5401\t      const symbolt *fsym = ns.lookup(f_it->first);\n5402\t      size_t bounds_emitted = 0;\n5403\t      // Counted at the EMISSION, not at the parse. A hole that was read out of\n5404\t      // the spec and then never reached the assumption would leave the query\n5405\t      // certifying a WIDER region than the one reported — and the parse-time\n5406\t      // line would still say the holes were there.\n5407\t      size_t holes_emitted = 0;\n5408\t\n5409\t      // ---- AN EMPTY BOX IS NOT A CERTIFICATE ----\n5410\t      //\n5411\t      // `lo > hi` makes the entry assumption `lo <= c <= hi` UNSATISFIABLE. Then\n5412\t      // nothing executes, every exit assert holds because it is never reached,\n5413\t      // and the query answers VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL. Measured on this very\n5414\t      // fixture before this check existed: `a in [100, 11]` certified cleanly,\n5415\t      // exit 0, with the box printed beside it.\n5416\t      //\n5417\t      // That is the SECOND route to a false certificate found in one night — the\n5418\t      // first was a driver reading the verdict as a substring of an ESBMC\n5419\t      // warning — and it is the worse-looking one, because the output is not\n5420\t      // merely green: it is a certificate naming a region that contains no\n5421\t      // inputs at all. The driver already refuses these, but the only\n5422\t      // reliability gate this method has should not depend on its caller\n5423\t      // guarding it, and that caller's own gate has already failed once.\n5424\t      //\n5425\t      // The refusal belongs BEFORE the query is emitted, not where its answer is\n5426\t      // read. An unsatisfiable assumption does not make the question hard, it\n5427\t      // makes the question meaningless; there is nothing to interpret afterwards.\n5428\t      {\n5429\t        std::set<std::string> box_names;\n5430\t        for (const auto &b : certify_box)\n5431\t        {\n5432\t          std::string bad;\n5433\t          if (string2integer(b.hi) < string2integer(b.lo))\n5434\t            bad = \"the box is EMPTY on this coordinate (lo=\" + b.lo +\n5435\t                  \" > hi=\" + b.hi +\n5436\t                  \"), so the entry assumption is unsatisfiable and every exit \"\n5437\t                  \"assert would hold for want of an execution\";\n5438\t          // Closes the obvious hole in the check above: bounding one name twice\n5439\t          // can intersect to nothing while each bound is individually fine, and\n5440\t          // a per-bound test would wave both through. Duplicates carry no\n5441\t          // meaning in this spec anyway, so refusing them costs nothing and\n5442\t          // leaves no case where \"not empty by this test\" and \"not empty\" come\n5443\t          // apart.\n5444\t          else if (!box_names.insert(b.name).second)\n5445\t            bad = \"the coordinate is bounded TWICE in this spec; two bounds on \"\n5446\t                  \"one name can intersect to an empty box while each is \"\n5447\t                  \"individually well-formed, which the emptiness test above \"\n5448\t                  \"would not see\";\n5449\t          else if (!b.holes.empty())\n5450\t          {\n5451\t            // A PUNCHED interval has a SECOND way of being empty, and it is the\n5452\t            // one a `lo <= hi` test cannot see: `a in [5,5] \\ {5}` passes that\n5453\t            // test and still admits no input at all. Same consequence as the\n5454\t            // inverted interval — an unsatisfiable assumption certifies\n5455\t            // VACUOUSLY — so it gets the same refusal rather than a warning.\n5456\t            //\n5457\t            // Counting distinct holes INSIDE [lo, hi] is what makes this exact:\n5458\t            // a hole outside the interval removes nothing, and counting it would\n5459\t            // refuse a perfectly good box. The count is bounded by the spec's\n5460\t            // own size, so comparing it against a 256-bit span is safe.\n5461\t            const BigInt lo = string2integer(b.lo), hi = string2integer(b.hi);\n5462\t            std::set<std::string> inside;\n5463\t            for (const auto &h : b.holes)\n5464\t            {\n5465\t              const BigInt hv = string2integer(h);\n5466\t              if (hv >= lo && hv <= hi)\n5467\t                inside.insert(integer2string(hv));\n5468\t            }\n5469\t            if (BigInt((int64_t)inside.size()) >= (hi - lo + 1))\n5470\t              bad = \"the PUNCHED box is EMPTY on this coordinate: [\" + b.lo +\n5471\t                    \", \" + b.hi + \"] holds \" + integer2string(hi - lo + 1) +\n5472\t                    \" value(s) and the holes remove all of them, so the entry \"\n5473\t                    \"assumption is unsatisfiable. `lo <= hi` does NOT catch \"\n5474\t                    \"this — the interval is well-formed and the punching is \"\n5475\t                    \"what empties it\";\n5476\t          }\n5477\t          if (!bad.empty())\n5478\t          {\n5479\t            log_error(\n5480\t              \"--path-cov-certify: unit '{}' — REFUSING THE QUERY on coordinate \"\n5481\t              \"'{}': {}. An unsatisfiable assumption certifies VACUOUSLY: the \"\n5482\t              \"run would print VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL next to a box holding no \"\n5483\t              \"inputs, which is a false certificate rather than a weak one. \"\n5484\t              \"Certification is not attempted\",\n5485\t              uid,\n5486\t              b.name,\n5487\t              bad);\n5488\t            exit(1);\n5489\t          }\n5490\t        }\n5491\t      }\n5492\t\n5493\t      for (const auto &b : certify_box)\n5494\t      {\n5495\t        expr2tc bs;\n5496\t        std::string why;\n5497\t        if (!resolve_coord(fsym, b.name, bs))\n5498\t          why =\n5499\t            \"the name does not resolve to an input of this unit. Name a \"\n5500\t            \"parameter of this unit, an environment value as `msg.value` / \"\n5501\t            \"`tx.origin` / `block.timestamp`, or a state variable at entry as \"\n5502\t            \"`state.<field>` (which reaches the contract object's own \"\n5503\t            \"components only — a mapping or a dynamic array does not resolve)\";\n5504\t        else\n5505\t          coord_expressible(bs->type, why);\n5506\t        if (!why.empty())\n5507\t        {\n5508\t          // REFUSE THE QUERY, not just the coordinate — the opposite of the\n5509\t          // outer box, and deliberately so. There, one missing coordinate costs\n5510\t          // information; here it would change the ANSWER: certification asks\n5511\t          // \"does every input in THIS box walk this path\", and a box missing one\n5512\t          // of its requested bounds is a strictly WIDER box. The run could then\n5513\t          // answer SUCCESSFUL about a region nobody asked about, which is the\n5514\t          // single outcome this query exists to prevent.\n5515\t          //\n5516\t          // Exiting rather than aborting is the actual fix. The verdict is the\n5517\t          // same refusal it always was; what changes is that it is now a clean\n5518\t          // non-zero exit with a readable reason instead of SIGABRT, so an\n5519\t          // unattended driver records a named failure instead of a core dump.\n5520\t          // Note that no verdict line is printed either, so a caller reading\n5521\t          // SUCCESSFUL/FAILED as whole lines sees its explicit third state.\n5522\t          // Deliberately NOT recorded in path_cov_refused_coords. The only\n5523\t          // reader of that map is report_outer_boxes, which is unreachable from\n5524\t          // here -- this branch exits the process. A write nothing can observe\n5525\t          // is not defence in depth, it is a line that reads like one, and the\n5526\t          // next person to add a consumer would have to discover for themselves\n5527\t          // that this entry never arrives.\n5528\t          log_error(\n5529\t            \"--path-cov-certify: unit '{}' — REFUSING THE QUERY because \"\n5530\t            \"coordinate '{}' cannot be expressed: {}. Certification is not \"\n5531\t            \"attempted: dropping the bound would certify a WIDER box than the \"\n5532\t            \"one asked for, and answering about a different box is worse than \"\n5533\t            \"not answering. Re-run with a box this stage can express, or read \"\n5534\t            \"this as the path being out of reach of the current coordinate set\",\n5535\t            uid,\n5536\t            b.name,\n5537\t            why);\n5538\t          exit(1);\n5539\t        }\n5540\t        const type2tc bt = bs->type;\n5541\t\n5542\t        // ---- The spec's decimals must FIT the coordinate's own type ----\n5543\t        //\n5544\t        // Every bound is built with constant_int2tc ON THE COORDINATE'S TYPE, so\n5545\t        // a decimal above the type's maximum WRAPS silently and the query is\n5546\t        // emitted about a different value than the one written down. The verdict\n5547\t        // then describes a box nobody asked for, and if it comes back\n5548\t        // SUCCESSFUL it is a false certificate — the same shape as the signed\n5549\t        // hole documented in coord_expressible, arrived at through the value\n5550\t        // rather than through the type.\n5551\t        //\n5552\t        // Checked here rather than in the structural block above because this is\n5553\t        // the first point where the coordinate's TYPE is known; the block above\n5554\t        // can only compare decimals with each other. coord_expressible has\n5555\t        // already restricted `bt` to an unsigned bit-vector, so the admissible\n5556\t        // range is exactly [0, 2^width - 1].\n5557\t        {\n5558\t          BigInt tmax = 1;\n5559\t          for (unsigned w = 0; w < bt->get_width(); ++w)\n5560\t            tmax *= 2;\n5561\t          tmax -= 1;\n5562\t          std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> vals = {\n5563\t            {\"lo\", b.lo}, {\"hi\", b.hi}};\n5564\t          for (const auto &h : b.holes)\n5565\t            vals.push_back({\"hole\", h});\n5566\t          for (const auto &[what, txt] : vals)\n5567\t          {\n5568\t            const BigInt v = string2integer(txt);\n5569\t            if (v >= 0 && v <= tmax)\n5570\t              continue;\n5571\t            log_error(\n5572\t              \"--path-cov-certify: unit '{}' — REFUSING THE QUERY on coordinate \"\n5573\t              \"'{}': the {} value {} does not fit the coordinate's own type \"\n5574\t              \"(admissible range [0, {}]). The bound is built as a constant of \"\n5575\t              \"that type, so an out-of-range decimal WRAPS and the query would \"\n5576\t              \"be emitted about a different value than the one written here — \"\n5577\t              \"answering SUCCESSFUL about a box nobody asked for. Certification \"\n5578\t              \"is not attempted\",\n5579\t              uid,\n5580\t              b.name,\n5581\t              what,\n5582\t              txt,\n5583\t              integer2string(tmax));\n5584\t            exit(1);\n5585\t          }\n5586\t        }\n5587\t\n5588\t        // `lo <= c <= hi`, then one `c != h` per hole (Definition 5). With no\n5589\t        // holes this is byte for byte the assumption emitted before punched\n5590\t        // intervals existed, so every existing spec is unaffected.\n5591\t        expr2tc bguard = and2tc(\n5592\t          greaterthanequal2tc(bs, constant_int2tc(bt, string2integer(b.lo))),\n5593\t          lessthanequal2tc(bs, constant_int2tc(bt, string2integer(b.hi))));\n5594\t        for (const auto &h : b.holes)\n5595\t        {\n5596\t          bguard = and2tc(\n5597\t            bguard,\n5598\t            notequal2tc(bs, constant_int2tc(bt, string2integer(h))));\n5599\t          // Incremented HERE, inside the conjunction, and not from\n5600\t          // `b.holes.size()` next to the insert. MEASURED on the fault injection\n5601\t          // for this very change: with the conjunction disabled the query\n5602\t          // correctly flipped to FAILED while the line above still reported\n5603\t          // \"1 hole(s) punched\" — a counter that reads the SPEC cannot witness\n5604\t          // whether the spec reached the formula, which is the only thing it was\n5605\t          // added to witness.\n5606\t          ++holes_emitted;\n5607\t        }\n5608\t\n5609\t        goto_programt::instructiont asm_i;\n5610\t        asm_i.type = ASSUME;\n5611\t        asm_i.guard = bguard;\n5612\t        asm_i.location = goto_program.instructions.begin()->location;\n5613\t        // \"skipped\" keeps this out of the decision-set census, which flags a\n5614\t        // user-source ASSUME as a lowered-away branch. This one is ours.\n5615\t        asm_i.location.property(\"skipped\");\n5616\t        asm_i.function = goto_program.instructions.begin()->location.get_function();\n5617\t        goto_program.instructions.insert(goto_program.instructions.begin(), asm_i);\n5618\t        ++bounds_emitted;\n5619\t      }\n5620\t\n5621\t      // 2. Assert the path identity at EVERY exit — see the header comment.\n5622\t      //    Collected first, then inserted: inserting while walking the same\n5623\t      //    list is how the ABI gate acquired a self-loop once already.\n5624\t      std::vector<goto_programt::targett> exits;\n5625\t      Forall_goto_program_instructions (xit, goto_program)\n5626\t        if (xit->is_return() || xit->is_end_function() || is_error_call(xit))\n5627\t          exits.push_back(xit);\n5628\t\n5629\t      const expr2tc cert_guard = and2tc(\n5630\t        equality2tc(tr, constant_int2tc(utype, BigInt(certify_enc))),\n5631\t        equality2tc(cnt, constant_int2tc(utype, BigInt(certify_depth))));\n5632\t      size_t exit_idx = 0;\n5633\t      for (auto xpc : exits)\n5634\t      {\n5635\t        // Comment shape MUST stay `<unit-id>:path:<enc>` — the unit id first,\n5636\t        // with nothing in front of it. MEASURED: a leading \"certify:\" made the\n5637\t        // report's `path_function` read `certify:sol:@C@Box@F@f#18`, the\n5638\t        // counterexample harvest builds the expected argument scope from that\n5639\t        // string, every nondet then failed the scope test and was filed as\n5640\t        // harness-internal (dropped 19 -> 25, `inputs` empty). The refutation\n5641\t        // still printed a verdict, so the loss was silent — and the witness\n5642\t        // VALUE is the entire point of a refutation: without it there is\n5643\t        // nothing to shrink the box with. The mode is announced by the banner\n5644\t        // above, not by decorating a key another component parses.\n5645\t        const std::string comment = id2string(f_it->first) +\n5646\t                                    \":path:\" + std::to_string(certify_enc) +\n5647\t                                    \"#exit\" + std::to_string(exit_idx++);\n5648\t        all_claims.insert({comment, xpc->location.as_string()});\n5649\t        insert_assert(goto_program, xpc, cert_guard, comment);\n5650\t      }\n5651\t\n5652\t      ++certify_units_matched;\n5653\t      log_status(\n5654\t        \"--path-cov-certify: unit '{}' — assumed {} input bound(s) ({} hole(s) \"\n5655\t        \"punched) at entry \"\n5656\t        \"and asserted `tr == {} && cnt == {}` at ALL {} exit(s) of the unit. \"\n5657\t        \"Asserting at every exit is what makes the query non-vacuous: an input \"\n5658\t        \"inside the box that walks a DIFFERENT path leaves through a different \"\n5659\t        \"exit, and would never be checked if the assert sat only on this \"\n5660\t        \"path's own exit\",\n5661\t        uid,\n5662\t        bounds_emitted,\n5663\t        holes_emitted,\n5664\t        certify_enc,\n5665\t        certify_depth,\n5666\t        exits.size());\n5667\t      total_paths += exits.size();\n5668\t      continue;\n5669\t    }\n5670\t\n5671\t    size_t ins_idx = 0;\n5672\t    for (auto &[pc, g, comment, is_revert, stable_id] : to_insert)\n5673\t    {\n5674\t      const size_t this_idx = ins_idx++;\n5675\t      // Claim key == the (comment, location) pair get_total_cond_assert() and\n5676\t      // bmc.cpp's claim_sig use, so universe / covered-set / numerator stay\n5677\t      // key-aligned. insert_assert copies pc->location onto the new assert,\n5678\t      // so reading it here (pre-insert) gives the same string.\n5679\t      const std::string loc = pc->location.as_string();\n5680\t      const std::pair<std::string, std::string> key(comment, loc);\n5681\t      // Static universe FIRST: every enumerated path counts in the\n5682\t      // denominator whether or not it is instrumented this round.\n5683\t      all_claims.insert(key);\n5684\t      // exit_kind for the report: this path leaves via a detected\n5685\t      // custom-error revert rather than the normal END_FUNCTION exit.\n5686\t      if (is_revert)\n5687\t        revert_paths.insert(key);\n5688\t      // ...or via a require/revert(\"msg\") rollback, which reaches END_FUNCTION\n5689\t      // but still reverts the transaction.\n5690\t      if (rollback_exits.count(this_idx))\n5691\t        rollback_revert_paths.insert(key);\n5692\t      if (undetermined_exits.count(this_idx))\n5693\t        undetermined_exit_paths.insert(key);\n5694\t      // POSITIVE record of a normal exit. The other three sets already name\n5695\t      // what went wrong; without this one, \"normal\" could only be inferred from\n5696\t      // absence — and a consumer that infers it would also call every claim\n5697\t      // from a DIFFERENT coverage mode normal, since those appear in no set at\n5698\t      // all. Measured, not hypothetical: reading normality as absence broke\n5699\t      // three branch-coverage regressions on the first run.\n5700\t      //\n5701\t      // Recorded here rather than derived, for the same reason the census\n5702\t      // demands positive evidence in the first place: this is the one judgement\n5703\t      // that authorises a generated test to assert something.\n5704\t      //\n5705\t      // ...AND the unit is not disqualified. An obstacle means the model admits\n5706\t      // an execution the chain does not have, so this path's counterexample can\n5707\t      // describe something that cannot happen -- precisely the case in which a\n5708\t      // test must NOT be authorised to assert. The two flags are per-unit and\n5709\t      // already computed above, so the guard is free.\n5710\t      //\n5711\t      // WITHOUT IT the two records contradicted each other: the same key went\n5712\t      // into `named_obstacle_paths` (\"must not be turned into a test\", per the\n5713\t      // header) three lines below, and into this set (\"the one judgement that\n5714\t      // authorises a generated test to assert something\") right here. The\n5715\t      // emitter reads this set and never read that map, so the authorisation\n5716\t      // won -- an obstructed path was emitted BARE, with a comment saying the\n5717\t      // path exits normally and a revert would fail the test.\n5718\t      //\n5719\t      // The emitter now refuses obstructed cases outright (foundry.cpp), which\n5720\t      // is the primary fix; this is the same rule stated where the\n5721\t      // authorisation is granted, so a future consumer of this set inherits it\n5722\t      // without having to know about the other one.\n5723\t      if (\n5724\t        !is_revert && !rollback_exits.count(this_idx) &&\n5725\t        !undetermined_exits.count(this_idx) && !unit_has_lost_decision &&\n5726\t        !unit_calls_gated_unit)\n5727\t        normal_exit_paths.insert(key);\n5728\t      // Named obstacle, applied to EVERY path of the unit (see the census\n5729\t      // comment above for why per-path containment is unsound here). The paths\n5730\t      // stay in the denominator — they are real — but none of them may become a\n5731\t      // test or join the sibling set for the stage-3 subtraction.\n5732\t      if (unit_has_lost_decision)\n5733\t      {\n5734\t        ++obstacle_paths_assume;\n5735\t        named_obstacle_paths[key] =\n5736\t          \"unit contains a source-level decision the frontend lowered to a \"\n5737\t          \"control-flow-free assume (internal library / free-function \"\n5738\t          \"require); the reverting execution does not exist in the model, so \"\n5739\t          \"it is absent from the sibling set of EVERY path of this unit\";\n5740\t      }\n5741\t      if (unit_calls_gated_unit)\n5742\t      {\n5743\t        ++obstacle_paths_residual;\n5744\t        named_obstacle_paths[key] =\n5745\t          \"unit still calls another UNIT's own body unexpanded (\" +\n5746\t          residual_unit_names +\n5747\t          \"); that body carries the ABI value gate, which models an EXTERNAL \"\n5748\t          \"entry, so the model admits the callee reverting for carrying value \"\n5749\t          \"inside an INTERNAL call that on-chain proceeds — an execution that \"\n5750\t          \"does not exist on chain\";\n5751\t      }\n5752\t      if (unit_truncated)\n5753\t      {\n5754\t        // NOT an obstacle: a strength annotation. The dropped paths exist in the\n5755\t        // model and their Phase-1 accounting is still instrumented, so the\n5756\t        // certification query `assume(interval); assert(tr == pi)` still rejects\n5757\t        // any candidate interval that reaches them — the interval shrinks rather\n5758\t        // than being wrong. Recorded per path so a downstream consumer can say\n5759\t        // \"this one's certified region is narrower than it would otherwise be\",\n5760\t        // and deliberately kept OUT of named_obstacle_paths so it cannot be\n5761\t        // confused with the model/reality divergences that must not ship a test.\n5762\t        ++truncation_weakened_paths;\n5763\t        truncation_weakened[key] =\n5764\t          \"unit lost paths to the per-unit goal/length cap; the dropped paths \"\n5765\t          \"exist in the model and are still accounted for in `tr`, so the \"\n5766\t          \"certification query still excludes their inputs — this narrows the \"\n5767\t          \"certified region rather than invalidating it\";\n5768\t      }\n5769\t      // Remember this run's claim key -> stable id so the run-end write-back can\n5770\t      // persist exactly the paths that were witnessed.\n5771\t      path_stable_id[key] = stable_id;\n5772\t      if (path_covered_ids.count(stable_id))\n5773\t      {\n5774\t        ++skipped_paths; // already witnessed in an earlier round\n5775\t        continue;\n5776\t      }\n5777\t      insert_assert(goto_program, pc, g, comment);\n5778\t      // Stamp the just-inserted assert (now at std::prev(pc)) so the Foundry\n5779\t      // generator emits vm.expectRevert() for this detected revert path (R0).\n5780\t      //\n5781\t      // ONLY for `is_revert`, whose assert sits at the `#sol_error` call — an\n5782\t      // instruction reachable on that path ALONE. A rollback revert's assert\n5783\t      // sits at the shared END_FUNCTION, where every path's assert is stacked:\n5784\t      // the generator marks a transaction as reverting when ANY reached assert\n5785\t      // step carries the flag, so stamping there makes a NON-reverting path's\n5786\t      // counterexample pick the flag up and emit `vm.expectRevert()` before a\n5787\t      // call that does not revert — a test that fails when run. Measured: all 3\n5788\t      // of D's tests (two of them normal paths) got the wrapper.\n5789\t      // The JSON already carries `exit_kind: \"revert\"` for these, so a\n5790\t      // generator can emit the oracle from there without this bleed.\n5791\t      if (is_revert)\n5792\t        std::prev(pc)->location.set(\"sol_revert_edge\", true);\n5793\t      ++total_paths;\n5794\t    }\n5795\t\n5796\t  }\n5797\t\n5798\t  // ---- A CERTIFICATION QUERY THAT MATCHED NO UNIT IS NOT A CERTIFICATE ----\n5799\t  //\n5800\t  // The FIFTH false-certification route, found by enumerating the assumption\n5801\t  // side of the gate rather than by colliding with it. `--path-cov-certify` with\n5802\t  // a unit name nothing matches -- a typo, a renamed function, a driver reading\n5803\t  // the wrong field -- skips every unit, so NO assume and NO assert are ever\n5804\t  // emitted. The run then has nothing to check, everything holds for want of an\n5805\t  // obligation, and it prints VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL with exit 0.\n5806\t  //\n5807\t  // Measured: {\"unit\": \"nosuchfn\", ...} on a contract with one unit returned\n5808\t  // SUCCESSFUL, exit 0, indistinguishable from a real certificate.\n5809\t  //\n5810\t  // Same shape as the other four (an inverted interval, a signed coordinate, a\n5811\t  // punched-empty box, a one-value ladder): the query answers SUCCESSFUL for a\n5812\t  // question it never asked. Exiting non-zero with a named reason puts it in the\n5813\t  // third state, where a caller reading whole verdict lines can see it.\n5814\t  if (certify_on && certify_units_matched == 0)\n5815\t  {\n5816\t    log_error(\n5817\t      \"--path-cov-certify: unit '{}' matched NO enumerated unit, so not one \"\n5818\t      \"assume and not one assert was emitted -- the run would otherwise print \"\n5819\t      \"VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL for a query it never asked. Check the name \"\n5820\t      \"against the report's `path_function` (mangled form \"\n5821\t      \"sol:@C@<contract>@F@<name>#<id>). This is a false certificate, not a \"\n5822\t      \"weak result\",\n5823\t      certify_unit);\n5824\t    exit(1);\n5825\t  }\n5826\t\n5827\t  // all_claims is the no-skip static universe built in the loop above (one\n5828\t  // entry per enumerated complete path), NOT get_total_cond_assert() — the\n5829\t  // latter counts instrumented asserts only, so a covered-set skip would\n5830\t  // shrink the denominator and spuriously inflate coverage.\n5831\t  if (dropped_paths > 0)\n5832\t    log_warning(\n5833\t      \"--solidity-path-coverage: per-function path/length cap ({}) hit; {} \"\n5834\t      \"path(s) dropped (coverage is complete only up to the cap for those \"\n5835\t      \"functions)\",\n5836\t      path_cov_max_goals,\n5837\t      dropped_paths);\n5838\t  log_status(\n5839\t    \"--solidity-path-coverage: instrumented {} complete path(s) across {} \"\n5840\t    \"unit(s) (loop bound = {} iterations)\",\n5841\t    total_paths,\n5842\t    units_enumerated,\n5843\t    path_cov_unwind);\n5844\t  if (!named_obstacle_paths.empty())\n5845\t    log_warning(\n5846\t      \"--solidity-path-coverage: NAMED OBSTACLE — {} path(s) excluded, being \"\n5847\t      \"ALL paths of every affected unit. Both causes are the SAME failure — the \"\n5848\t      \"model and the chain disagree, so a counterexample can describe an \"\n5849\t      \"execution that does not exist and the test built from it is RED on the \"\n5850\t      \"UNMODIFIED contract — reached by two different routes, so they are \"\n5851\t      \"counted apart:\\n\"\n5852\t      \"  (a) {} path(s) across {} unit(s): the unit contains a construct that \"\n5853\t      \"removes executions WITHOUT a branch — an explicitly written \"\n5854\t      \"`__ESBMC_assume`, or a `require` still lowered to a control-flow-free \"\n5855\t      \"assume (the library / free-function case; seeing that again means the \"\n5856\t      \"revert-observation widening regressed). Those executions do not exist in \"\n5857\t      \"the model at all, so no certification query can even see them.\\n\"\n5858\t      \"  (b) {} path(s) across {} unit(s): the unit still calls another UNIT's \"\n5859\t      \"own body unexpanded (depth bound), routing an INTERNAL call through the \"\n5860\t      \"EXTERNAL-entry body and its ABI value gate. Raise --unwind to expand \"\n5861\t      \"them; an expanded copy is gate-free.\\n\"\n5862\t      \"Exclusion is per UNIT, not per path. Reported as an absolute count and \"\n5863\t      \"NOT folded into the coverage percentage — an obstacle is not partial \"\n5864\t      \"credit\",\n5865\t      named_obstacle_paths.size(),\n5866\t      obstacle_paths_assume,\n5867\t      obstacle_units,\n5868\t      obstacle_paths_residual,\n5869\t      obstacle_units_residual);\n5870\t  if (truncation_weakened_paths > 0)\n5871\t    log_warning(\n5872\t      \"--solidity-path-coverage: ASSERTION STRENGTH — {} path(s) across {} \"\n5873\t      \"unit(s) have a NARROWER certified region than they otherwise would, \"\n5874\t      \"because their unit lost paths to the goal cap ({}). This is a strength \"\n5875\t      \"annotation, NOT an obstacle: the dropped paths exist in the model and \"\n5876\t      \"their decision accounting is still instrumented, so an input reaching \"\n5877\t      \"one still carries its path number in `tr` and the certification query \"\n5878\t      \"`assume(interval); assert(tr == pi)` rejects it — the interval shrinks \"\n5879\t      \"rather than being wrong. Degradation runs first precisely so this should \"\n5880\t      \"not be reached; each unit above says why it was\",\n5881\t      truncation_weakened_paths,\n5882\t      units_at_cap,\n5883\t      path_cov_max_goals);\n5884\t  if (units_enumerated > 0)\n5885\t  {\n5886\t    // One line carrying everything the distribution question needs, so it never\n5887\t    // has to be re-run to answer a follow-up.\n5888\t    //\n5889\t    // The total here is the ENUMERATED count (all_claims), NOT the count\n5890\t    // instrumented this round. The distribution is a structural property of the\n5891\t    // contract, so mixing in a per-round number would make it change between\n5892\t    // rounds of the same escalation: measured on a resumed run, 7 of 8 paths\n5893\t    // were carried over from the covered set and this line read \"1 path(s)\n5894\t    // total ... 0.33x\" for a contract whose real figures are 8 and 2.67x. `max`\n5895\t    // and the pre-expansion total were already structural, so the mix was\n5896\t    // silent — the kind of number that gets quoted.\n5897\t    const size_t enumerated_total = all_claims.size();\n5898\t    const double ratio =\n5899\t      pre_expansion_total > 0\n5900\t        ? (double)enumerated_total / (double)pre_expansion_total\n5901\t        : 0.0;\n5902\t    log_status(\n5903\t      \"--solidity-path-coverage: path distribution — {} unit(s), {} path(s) \"\n5904\t      \"total, max {} in '{}', mean {:.1f}; before internal-call expansion the \"\n5905\t      \"same units had {} path(s), so expansion multiplied them by {:.2f}x\",\n5906\t      units_enumerated,\n5907\t      enumerated_total,\n5908\t      max_unit_paths,\n5909\t      max_unit_name,\n5910\t      (double)enumerated_total / (double)units_enumerated,\n5911\t      pre_expansion_total,\n5912\t      ratio);\n5913\t    if (units_at_cap > 0)\n5914\t      log_warning(\n5915\t        \"--solidity-path-coverage: {} of {} unit(s) hit the per-unit goal cap \"\n5916\t        \"({}), so the totals reported above are LOWER BOUNDS for those units \"\n5917\t        \"and the tail of this distribution must not be presented as complete. \"\n5918\t        \"Their paths keep a valid — but narrower — Counted and reported, because a silently shorter ladder is a\n          // silently coarser measurement.\n          size_t out_of_type = 0;\n          if (is_unsignedbv_type(ct))\n          {\n            BigInt tmax = 1;\n            for (unsigned b = 0; b < ct->get_width(); ++b)\n              tmax *= 2;\n            tmax -= 1;\n            std::vector<BigInt> kept;\n            kept.reserve(probe_vals.size());\n            for (const BigInt &v : probe_vals)\n            {\n              if (v >= 0 && v <= tmax)\n                kept.push_back(v);\n              else\n                ++out_of_type;\n            }\n            probe_vals.swap(kept);\n          }\n          // The two sources can overlap; a duplicated probe is a duplicated\n          // claim name, which collides in `all_claims` and silently drops one.\n          std::sort(probe_vals.begin(), probe_vals.end());\n          probe_vals.erase(\n            std::unique(probe_vals.begin(), probe_vals.end()),\n            probe_vals.end());\n          if (out_of_type > 0)\n            log_warning(\n              \"--path-cov-outer-box: coordinate '{}' — DROPPED {} probe \"\n              \"value(s) that do not fit its type; {} probe value(s) remain. \"\n              \"Those values would have been built as constants of this type and \"\n              \"WRAPPED, so each would have measured a different number than the \"\n              \"one requested. Same consequence as the\n            // inverted interval — an unsatisfiable assumption certifies\n            // VACUOUSLY — so it gets the same refusal rather than a warning.\n            //\n            // Counting distinct holes INSIDE [lo, hi] is what makes this exact:\n            // a hole outside the interval removes nothing, and counting it would\n            // refuse a perfectly good box. The count is bounded by the spec's\n            // own size, so comparing it against a 256-bit span is safe.\n            const BigInt lo = string2integer(b.lo), hi = string2integer(b.hi);\n            std::set<std::string> inside;\n            for (const auto &h : b.holes)\n            {\n              const BigInt hv = string2integer(h);\n              if (hv >= lo && hv <= hi)\n                inside.insert(integer2string(hv));\n            }\n            if (BigInt((int64_t)inside.size()) >= (hi - lo + 1))\n              bad = \"the PUNCHED box is EMPTY on this coordinate: [\" + b.lo +\n                    \", \" + b.hi + \"] holds \" + integer2string(hi - lo + 1) +\n                    \" value(s) and the holes remove all of them, so the entry \"\n                    \"assumption is unsatisfiable. `lo <= hi` does NOT catch \"\n                    \"this — the interval is well-formed and the punching is \"\n                    \"what empties it\";\n          }\n          if (!bad.empty())\n          {\n            log_error(\n              \"--path-cov-certify: unit '{}' — REFUSING THE QUERY on coordinate \"\n              \"'{}': {}. Name a \"\n            \"parameter of this unit, an environment value as `msg.value` / \"\n            \"`tx.origin` / `block.timestamp`, or a state variable at entry as \"\n            \"`state.<field>` (which reaches the contract object's own \"\n            \"components only — a mapping or a dynamic array does not resolve)\";\n        else\n          coord_expressible(bs->type, why);\n        if (!why.empty())\n        {\n          // REFUSE THE QUERY, not just the coordinate — the opposite of the\n          // outer box, and deliberately so. A write nothing can observe\n          // is not defence in depth, it is a line that reads like one, and the\n          // next person to add a consumer would have to discover for themselves\n          // that this entry never arrives.\n          log_error(\n            \"--path-cov-certify: unit '{}' — REFUSING THE QUERY because \"\n            \"coordinate '{}' cannot be expressed: {}. The verdict\n        // then describes a box nobody asked for, and if it comes back\n        // SUCCESSFUL it is a false certificate — the same shape as the signed\n        // hole documented in coord_expressible, arrived at through the value\n        // rather than through the type.\n        //\n        // Checked here rather than in the structural block above because this is\n        // the first point where the coordinate's TYPE is known; the block above\n        // can only compare decimals with each other. coord_expressible has\n        // already restricted `bt` to an unsigned bit-vector, so the admissible\n        // range is exactly [0, 2^width - 1].\n        {\n          BigInt tmax = 1;\n          for (unsigned w = 0; w < bt->get_width(); ++w)\n            tmax *= 2;\n          tmax -= 1;\n          std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> vals = {\n            {\"lo\", b.lo}, {\"hi\", b.hi}};\n          for (const auto &h : b.holes)\n            vals.push_back({\"hole\", h});\n          for (const auto &[what, txt] : vals)\n          {\n            const BigInt v = string2integer(txt);\n            if (v >= 0 && v <= tmax)\n              continue;\n            log_error(\n              \"--path-cov-certify: unit '{}' — REFUSING THE QUERY on coordinate \"\n              \"'{}': the {} value {} does not fit the coordinate's own type \"\n              \"(admissible range [0, {}]). The bound is built as a constant of \"\n              \"that type, so an out-of-range decimal WRAPS and the query would \"\n              \"be emitted about a different value than the one written here — \"\n              \"answering SUCCESSFUL about a box nobody asked for. Assert the path identity at EVERY exit — see the header comment.\n      //    Collected first, then inserted: inserting while walking the same\n      //    list is how the ABI gate acquired a self-loop once already.\n      std::vector<goto_programt::targett> exits;\n      Forall_goto_program_instructions (xit, goto_program)\n        if (xit->is_return() || xit->is_end_function() || is_error_call(xit))\n          exits.push_back(xit);\n\n      const expr2tc cert_guard = and2tc(\n        equality2tc(tr, constant_int2tc(utype, BigInt(certify_enc))),\n        equality2tc(cnt, constant_int2tc(utype, BigInt(certify_depth))));\n      size_t exit_idx = 0;\n      for (auto xpc : exits)\n      {\n        // Comment shape MUST stay `<unit-id>:path:<enc>` — the unit id first,\n        // with nothing in front of it. insert_assert(goto_program, xpc, cert_guard, comment);\n      }\n\n      ++certify_units_matched;\n      log_status(\n        \"--path-cov-certify: unit '{}' — assumed {} input bound(s) ({} hole(s) \"\n        \"punched) at entry \"\n        \"and asserted `tr == {} && cnt == {}` at ALL {} exit(s) of the unit. \"\n        \"Asserting at every exit is what makes the query non-vacuous: an input \"\n        \"inside the box that walks a DIFFERENT path leaves through a different \"\n        \"exit, and would never be checked if the assert sat only on this \"\n        \"path's own exit\",\n ins_idx = 0;\n    for (auto &[pc, g, comment, is_revert, stable_id] : to_insert)\n    {\n      const size_t this_idx = ins_idx++;\n      // Claim key == the (comment, location) pair get_total_cond_assert() and\n      // bmc.cpp's claim_sig use, so universe / covered-set / numerator stay\n      // key-aligned. insert_assert copies pc->location onto the new assert,\n      // so reading it here (pre-insert) gives the same string.\n      const std::string loc = pc->location.as_string();\n      const std::pair<std::string, std::string> key(comment, loc);\n      // Static universe FIRST: every enumerated path counts in the\n      // denominator whether or not it is instrumented this round.\n      all_claims.insert(key);\n      // exit_kind for the report: this path leaves via a detected\n      // custom-error revert rather than the normal END_FUNCTION exit.\n      if (is_revert)\n        revert_paths.insert(key);\n      // ...or via a require/revert(\"msg\") rollback, which reaches END_FUNCTION\n      // but still reverts the transaction.\n      if (rollback_exits.count(this_idx))\n        rollback_revert_paths.insert(key);\n      if (undetermined_exits.count(this_idx))\n        undetermined_exit_paths.insert(key);\n      // POSITIVE record of a normal exit. }\n\n        // a>b;\n        else if (it->is_other())\n        {\n          if (is_code_expression2t(it->code))\n          {\n            const expr2tc &other = to_code_expression2t(it->code).operand;\n            if (!is_nil_expr(other))\n              handle_operands_guard(other, goto_program, it);\n          }\n        }\n\n        // e.g. RETURN a>b;\n        else if (it->is_return())\n        {\n          const expr2tc &ret = to_code_return2t(it->code).operand;\n          if (!is_nil_expr(ret))\n            handle_operands_guard(ret, goto_program, it);\n        }\n\n        // e.g. func(a>b);\n        else if (it->is_function_call())\n        {\n          for (const expr2tc &op : to_code_function_call2t(it->code).operands)\n            if (!is_nil_expr(op))\n              handle_operands_guard(op, goto_program, it);\n        }\n\n        // reset target number\n        target_num = -1;\n      }\n    }\n\n  total_cond = get_total_cond_assert();\n  all_claims = total_cond;\n\n  // recalculate line number/ target number\n  goto_functions.update();\n}\n\n/*\n  algo:\n  if(b==0 && c > 90)\n  => assert(b==0)\n  => assert(!(b==0));\n  => assert(!(b==0 && c>90))\n  => assert(!(b==0 && !(c>90)))\n\n  if(b==0 || c > 90)\n  => assert(b==0)\n  => assert((b==0));\n  => assert(!(!b==0 && c>90))\n  => assert(!(!(b==0) && !(c>90)))\n*/\n/// Recurse into all sub-expressions of @p ptr, calling\n/// gen_cond_cov_assert on each.\nvoid goto_coveraget::gen_cond_cov_assert(\n  const expr2tc &ptr,\n  const expr2tc &pre_cond,\n  goto_programt &goto_program,\n  goto_programt::instructiont::targett &it)\n{\n  if (is_nil_expr(ptr))\n    return;\n  const std::size_t n = ptr->get_num_sub_exprs();\n  if (n == 0)\n    return; // atom\n\n  auto recurse_all = [&]() {\n    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)\n      gen_cond_cov_assert(*ptr->get_sub_expr(i), pre_cond, goto_program, it);\n  };\n\n  if (n == 1)\n  {\n    // (a!=0)++, !a, -a, (_Bool)(int)a\n    recurse_all();\n  }\n  else if (n == 2)\n  {\n    if (is_comparison_expr(ptr))\n    {\n      recurse_all();\n      add_cond_cov_assert(ptr, pre_cond, goto_program, it);\n    }\n    else if (is_and2t(ptr))\n    {\n      const expr2tc &lhs = *ptr->get_sub_expr(0);\n      const expr2tc &rhs = *ptr->get_sub_expr(1);\n      gen_cond_cov_assert(lhs, pre_cond, goto_program, it);\n\n      // update pre-condition: pre_cond && lhs\n      expr2tc new_pre =\n        is_nil_expr(pre_cond) ? lhs : gen_and_expr(pre_cond, lhs);\n      gen_cond_cov_assert(rhs, new_pre, goto_program, it);\n    }\n    else if (is_or2t(ptr))\n    {\n      const expr2tc &lhs = *ptr->get_sub_expr(0);\n      const expr2tc &rhs = *ptr->get_sub_expr(1);\n      gen_cond_cov_assert(lhs, pre_cond, goto_program, it);\n\n      // update pre-condition: !(pre_cond && lhs)\n      expr2tc new_pre =\n        is_nil_expr(pre_cond) ? lhs : gen_and_expr(pre_cond, lhs);\n      new_pre = gen_not_expr(new_pre);\n      gen_cond_cov_assert(rhs, new_pre, goto_program, it);\n    }\n    else\n    {\n      // a+=b; a>>(b!=0);\n      recurse_all();\n    }\n  }\n  else if (n == 3)\n  {\n    // ternary if\n    const expr2tc &cond = *ptr->get_sub_expr(0);\n    const expr2tc &t_val = *ptr->get_sub_expr(1);\n    const expr2tc &f_val = *ptr->get_sub_expr(2);\n\n    gen_cond_cov_assert(cond, pre_cond, goto_program, it);\n\n    // update pre-condition: pre_cond && cond\n    expr2tc pre_cond_1 =\n      is_nil_expr(pre_cond) ? cond : gen_and_expr(pre_cond, cond);\n    gen_cond_cov_assert(t_val, pre_cond_1, goto_program, it);\n\n    // update pre-condition: pre_cond && !cond\n    expr2tc not_cond = gen_not_expr(cond);\n    expr2tc pre_cond_2 =\n      is_nil_expr(pre_cond) ? not_cond : gen_and_expr(pre_cond, not_cond);\n    gen_cond_cov_assert(f_val, pre_cond_2, goto_program, it);\n  }\n  else\n  {\n    log_error(\"unexpected operand size\");\n    abort();\n  }\n}\n\nvoid goto_coveraget::add_cond_cov_assert(\n  const expr2tc &expr,\n  const expr2tc &pre_cond,\n  goto_programt &goto_program,\n  goto_programt::instructiont::targett &it)\n{\n  expr2tc cond = is_nil_expr(pre_cond) ? expr : gen_and_expr(pre_cond, expr);\n\n  // e.g. assert(!(a==1));  // a==1\n  // the idf is used as the claim_msg\n  // note that it's different from the actual guard.\n  std::string idf = from_expr(ns, \"\", expr);\n  expr2tc guard = gen_not_expr(cond);\n  insert_assert(goto_program, it, guard, idf);\n\n  // reversal\n  expr2tc not_expr = gen_not_expr(expr);\n  cond = is_nil_expr(pre_cond) ? not_expr : gen_and_expr(pre_cond, not_expr);\n  idf = from_expr(ns, \"\", not_expr);\n  guard = gen_not_expr(cond);\n  insert_assert(goto_program, it, guard, idf);\n}\n\nexpr2tc goto_coveraget::gen_not_eq_expr(const expr2tc &lhs, const expr2tc &rhs)\n{\n  expr2tc _lhs = (lhs->type == rhs->type) ? lhs : typecast2tc(rhs->type, lhs);\n  return notequal2tc(_lhs, rhs);\n}\n\nexpr2tc goto_coveraget::gen_and_expr(const expr2tc &lhs, const expr2tc &rhs)\n{\n  type2tc bt = get_bool_type();\n  expr2tc _lhs = is_bool_type(lhs->type) ? lhs : typecast2tc(bt, lhs);\n  expr2tc _rhs = is_bool_type(rhs->type) ? rhs : typecast2tc(bt, rhs);\n  return and2tc(_lhs, _rhs);\n}\n\nexpr2tc goto_coveraget::gen_not_expr(const expr2tc &guard)\n{\n  if (is_not2t(guard))\n    return to_not2t(guard).value;\n  return not2tc(guard);\n}\n\n/*\n  This function convert single guard to a non_equal_to_false expression\n  e.g. if(true) ==> if(true!=false)\n Do not add if it's already a binary boolean expression in 2. \n    e.g. if(x==1 && a++) => if(x==1 && a++ !=0)\n  4. Others: for any other expresison, including unary, binary and teranry, traverse its op with handle_single_guard recursivly. convert it to not equal in the top level only.\n    e.g. if((bool)a+b+c) => if((bool)(a+b+c)!=0)\n    typecast <--- add not equal here\n    - +\n      - a\n      - + \n        - b\n        - c\n  e.g. if(a) => if(a!=0); if(true) => if(true != 0); if(a?b:c:d) => if((a?b:c:d)!=0)\n  if(a==b) => if(a==b); if(a&&b) => if(a != 0 && b!=0 )\n*/\n/// Recursively maps each operand of @p expr through handle_single_guard\n/// (with the supplied @p sub_top_level), in place. Foreach_operand detaches\n/// the irep_container before mutating, so this is safe even when @p expr\n/// shares storage with its caller.\nstatic void replace_operands(\n  expr2tc &expr,\n  bool sub_top_level,\n  const std::function<expr2tc(const expr2tc &, bool)> &recurse)\n{\n  expr->Foreach_operand([&](expr2tc &op) { op = recurse(op, sub_top_level); });\n}\n\nexpr2tc goto_coveraget::handle_single_guard(\n  const expr2tc &expr,\n  bool top_level /* = true */)\n{\n  if (is_nil_expr(expr))\n    return expr;\n  const std::size_t n = expr->get_num_sub_exprs();\n  auto recurse = [this](const expr2tc &e, bool tl) {\n    return handle_single_guard(e, tl);\n  };\n\n  // --- Rule 1: Atomic expressions ---\n  // If the expression has no operands (a symbol or constant),\n expressions (like x in !(!(x))) get wrapped.\n  if (is_not2t(expr))\n  {\n    expr2tc result = expr;\n    replace_operands(result, /*sub_top_level=*/true, recurse);\n    return result;\n  }\n\n  // --- Special-case for typecasts to bool ---\n  // If we have (bool)(X) and X is not already a recognized guard\n  // (comparison or logical AND/OR), unwrap the typecast and wrap X.\n  if (is_typecast2t(expr) && is_bool_type(expr->type))\n  {\n    expr2tc inner = handle_single_guard(to_typecast2t(expr).from, top_level);\n    if (!(is_comparison_expr(inner) || is_and2t(inner) || is_or2t(inner)))\n      return gen_not_eq_expr(inner, gen_false_expr());\n    return inner;\n  }\n\n  // --- Process Binary Operators (exactly 2 operands) ---\n  if (n == 2)\n  {\n    expr2tc result = expr;\n    if (is_and2t(expr) || is_or2t(expr))\n    {\n      // Process each operand as an independent guard (top_level = true).\n      replace_operands(result, /*sub_top_level=*/true, recurse);\n      return result;\n    }\n    if (is_comparison_expr(expr))\n    {\n      replace_operands(result, /*sub_top_level=*/false, recurse);\n      return result;\n    }\n    // Other binary operators (e.g. arithmetic '+').\n    replace_operands(result, /*sub_top_level=*/false, recurse);\n    if (top_level)\n      return gen_not_eq_expr(result, gen_false_expr());\n    return result;\n  }\n\n  // --- Process Non-Binary Operators (Unary, Ternary, etc.) ---\n  expr2tc result = expr;\n  replace_operands(result, /*sub_top_level=*/false, recurse);\n\n  // For any other expression producing a Boolean value, if at the outer\n  // guard (top_level true) and its kind is not among our no-wrap set, then\n  // wrap it with \"!= false\". This catches cases like member accesses.\n  if (\n    top_level && is_bool_type(result->type) && !is_and2t(result) &&\n    !is_or2t(result) && !is_not2t(result) && !is_comparison_expr(result))\n    return gen_not_eq_expr(result, gen_false_expr());\n  return result;\n}\n\n/*\n  add condition instrumentation for OTHER, ASSIGN, FUNCTION_CALL..\n  whose operands might contain conditions\n  we handle guards for each boolean sub-operand.\n*/\nvoid goto_coveraget::handle_operands_guard(\n  const expr2tc &expr,\n  goto_programt &goto_program,\n  goto_programt::instructiont::targett &it)\n{\n  if (is_nil_expr(expr))\n    return;\n  const std::size_t n = expr->get_num_sub_exprs();\n  if (n == 0)\n    return;\n\n  expr2tc pre_cond; // nil\n\n  if (n == 1)\n  {\n    // e.g. RETURN ++(x&&y);\n    handle_operands_guard(*expr->get_sub_expr(0), goto_program, it);\n  }\n  else if (n == 2)\n  {\n    expr2tc target = expr;\n    if (is_and2t(expr) || is_or2t(expr))\n    {\n      // we do not need to add a !=false at top level\n      // e.g. return x?1:0 != return (x?1:0)!=false\n      target->Foreach_operand(\n        [this](expr2tc &op) { op = handle_single_guard(op, false); });\n    }\n    gen_cond_cov_assert(target, pre_cond, goto_program, it);\n  }\n  else\n  {\n    // this could only be ternary boolean\n    expr2tc rewrapped = handle_single_guard(expr, false);\n    gen_cond_cov_assert(rewrapped, pre_cond, goto_program, it);\n  }\n}\n\n// set the target function from \"--function\"\nvoid goto_coveraget::set_target(const std::string &_tgt)\n{\n  target_function = _tgt;\n}\n\n// check if it's the target function\nbool goto_coveraget::is_target_func(\n  const irep_idt &f,\n  const std::string &tgt_name) const\n{\n  const symbolt *sym = ns.lookup(f);\n  if (sym == nullptr)\n  {\n    log_error(\"Cannot find target function\");\n    abort();\n  }\n\n  exprt symbol = symbol_expr(*ns.lookup(f));\n  std::string sym_name = symbol.name().as_string();\n  if (sym_name == tgt_name)\n    return true;\n\n  // For Solidity: modifier expansion renames functions from \"func\" to\n  // \"func_modifierName\". Support prefix matching so that --function func\n  // matches func_modifierName.\n  if (\n    config.language.lid == language_idt::SOLIDITY &&\n    sym_name.size() > tgt_name.size() &&\n    sym_name.substr(0, tgt_name.size()) == tgt_name &&\n    sym_name[tgt_name.size()] == '_')\n    return true;\n\n  return false;\n}\n\n// Parse the --negating-property spec \"[contract:]function[:line]\".\n//   1 token  -> function\n//   2 tokens -> last all-digits: function:line ; pos != std::string::npos;\n       pos = spec.find(':', start))\n  {\n    tok.push_back(spec.substr(start, pos - start));\n    start = pos + 1;\n  }\n  tok.push_back(spec.substr(start));\n\n  if (tok.size() == 1)\n    fname = tok[0];\n  else if (tok.size() == 2)\n  {\n    if (all_digits(tok[1]))\n    {\n      fname = tok[0];\n      line = tok[1];\n    }\n    else\n    {\n      contract = tok[0];\n      fname = tok[1];\n    }\n  }\n  else if (tok.size() == 3)\n  {\n    contract = tok[0];\n    fname = tok[1];\n    if (all_digits(tok[2]))\n      line = tok[2];\n  }\n  else\n  {\n    log_warning(\n      \"--negating-property: malformed spec '{}', treating it as a plain \"\n      \"function name\",\n      spec);\n    fname = spec;\n  }\n\n  if (fname.empty())\n  {\n    log_warning(\n      \"--negating-property: empty function name in spec '{}', treating it as \"\n      \"a plain function name\",\n      spec);\n    contract.clear();\n    line.clear();\n    fname = spec;\n  }\n}\n\n// Extract the contract name from a Solidity mangled id of the form\n// \"sol:@C@<Contract>@F@...\". cpos);\n}\n\n// negate the condition inside the assertion\n// The idea is that, if the claim is verified safe, and its negated claim is also verified safe, then we say this claim is unreachable\nvoid goto_coveraget::negating_asserts(const std::string &tgt_spec)\n{\n  std::string contract, fname, target_line;\n  parse_negate_spec(tgt_spec, contract, fname, target_line);\n\n  std::string old = target_function;\n  target_function = fname;\n\n  std::unordered_set<std::string> location_pool = {};\n  location_pool.insert(get_filename_from_path(filename));\n  for (auto const &inc : config.ansi_c.include_files)\n    location_pool.insert(get_filename_from_path(inc));\n\n  // First pass: collect candidate asserts in functions matching the\n  // function-name filter (and the optional case-sensitive contract filter),\n  // restricted to the user source files.\n  std::vector<goto_programt::instructiont::targett> candidates;\n  Forall_goto_functions (f_it, goto_functions)\n    if (f_it->second.body_available && f_it->first != \"__ESBMC_main\")\n    {\n      goto_programt &goto_program = f_it->second.body;\n      if (filter(f_it->first, goto_program))\n        continue;\n      if (!contract.empty() && contract_of(f_it->first.as_string()) != contract)\n        continue;\n\n      Forall_goto_program_instructions (it, goto_program)\n      {\n        std::string cur_filename =\n          get_filename_from_path(it->location.file().as_string());\n        if (location_pool.count(cur_filename) == 0)\n          continue;\n\n        if (it->is_assert())\n          candidates.push_back(it);\n      }\n    }\n\n  // Select the asserts to negate. When a line is given, keep only those on\n  // that source line; if none match, silently fall back to whole-function\n  // negation (all candidates).\n  std::vector<goto_programt::instructiont::targett> matched;\n  if (!target_line.empty())\n  {\n    for (auto &it : candidates)\n      if (it->location.get_line().as_string() == target_line)\n        matched.push_back(it);\n    if (matched.empty())\n    {\n      log_debug(\n        \"coverage\",\n        \"--negating-property: no assert at line {} in '{}', falling back to \"\n        \"whole-function negation\",\n        target_line,\n        fname);\n      matched = candidates;\n    }\n  }\n  else\n    matched = candidates;\n\n  for (auto &it : matched)\n    replace_assert_to_guard(gen_not_expr(it->guard), it, false);\n\n  target_function = old;\n}\n\n// return true if this function is skipped\nbool goto_coveraget::filter(\n  const irep_idt &func_name,\n  const goto_programt &goto_program) const\n{\n  // \"--function\" mode\n  if (target_function != \"\" && !is_target_func(func_name, target_function))\n    return true;\n\n  // Skip the function that is labelled with \"__ESBMC_HIDE\"\n  // Extended to support Python in addition to Solidity\n  if (\n    goto_program.hide && (config.language.lid == language_idt::SOLIDITY ||\n                          config.language.lid == language_idt::PYTHON))\n    return true;\n  return false;\n}\n","numLines":704,"startLine":6000,"totalLines":6703}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"1f94d10f-89f1-48c8-afe7-f8a3a75cdfc9","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/samson/workspace/paper_review","sessionId":"e0047351-2714-4000-919d-058ca8af97c5","version":"2.1.220","gitBranch":"VeriPUT","slug":"synchronous-wondering-flame"}

(1) DEGRADATION: \"\n887\t      \"a unit whose full expansion exceeds the budget has internal call points \"\n888\t      \"withdrawn from its path identity — the callees still execute, they just \"\n889\t      \"stop contributing decisions, so the path classes get coarser while \"\n890\t      \"still partitioning the input space (sound, weaker assertions). VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL means every \"\n902\t      \"input in the box walks that path (the box is certified); FAILED gives a \"\n903\t      \"counterexample input that is inside the box but leaves the path, which \"\n904\t      \"is exactly the witness needed to shrink the box. The assert is on every \"\n905\t      \"exit on purpose — placed only on the path's own exit, an escaping input \"\n906\t      \"would leave elsewhere and never be checked, making the query vacuously \"\n907\t      \"true. Expansion, the ABI gate, Phase-1 accounting and both censuses all \"\n908\t      \"still run, and the query uses the SAME `tr` the enumeration does\"},\n909\t     {\"path-cov-outer-box\",\n910\t      boost::program_options::value<std::string>()->value_name(\"file\"),\n911\t      \"Measure each enumerated path's OUTER box in one batch, then subtract the \"\n912\t      \"siblings' boxes to get a certified region at zero further queries. JSON: \"\n913\t      \"{unit, probes, coords:[{name,lo,hi}], paths:[{enc,depth,ce:{name:val}}]}. \"\n914\t      \"For every path the assumption `tr == enc` is FIXED and only the candidate \"\n915\t      \"bounds vary, so an entire ladder — all paths, all coordinates, both \"\n916\t      \"directions — is judged in a single run rather than one query per widening \"\n917\t      \"step. `lo`/`hi` are the ladder span, which the driver takes from the \"\n918\t      \"nearest sibling counterexamples, and `ce` is the path's own \"\n919\t      \"counterexample, used to reject a subtraction cut that would carve away a \"\n920\t      \"known member of the path's domain. Resolution is (hi-lo)/(probes+1): a \"\n921\t      \"non-adaptive batch cannot give logarithmic precision, so refine with a \"\n922\t      \"second batch on a narrower span\"},\n923\t     {\"solidity-path-coverage\",\n924\t      NULL,\n925\t      \"Solidity complete-path coverage (entry->exit path coverage for test \"\n926\t      \"generation). False positives (memory or local\n1060\t      // arrays) only result in CVC5 being chosen instead of Bitwuzla,\n1061\t      // which is sound (just potentially slower for non-nested shapes).\n1062\t      const std::string padded_solvers =\n1063\t        std::string(\" \") + ESBMC_AVAILABLE_SOLVERS + \" \";\n1064\t      const bool cvc5_available =\n1065\t        padded_solvers.find(\" cvc5 \") != std::string::npos;\n1066\t      bool nested_dyn_detected = false;\n1067\t      // A scalar-valued ≥3-level nested mapping\n1068\t      // (`mapping(K1=>mapping(K2=>mapping(K3=>uint256)))`) lowers to a\n1069\t      // CONST_ARRAY-initialised infinite mapping array that Bitwuzla\n1070\t      // cannot equate (asymmetric `(= ca freshsym)` from IS-havoc →\n1071\t      // \"Equality over constant arrays not fully supported yet\" abort\n1072\t      // under assertion BMC; k-induction non-convergence under\n1073\t      // coverage). The\n1075\t      // typeIdentifier marker is `t_mapping$_` (NOT `t_array$_`), so it\n1076\t      // is detected separately below and routed to plain CVC5 (no\n1077\t      // native-tuples — that flag is array-tuple-encoding-specific).\n1078\t      // See notes/Results/branch_cov/STAGE5_RESIDUAL_DIAG.md.\n1079\t      bool deep_mapping_detected = false;\n1080\t      // Pattern B: --k-induction with multi-contract dispatch. c;\n1176\t          while ((c = f.get()) != EOF)\n1177\t          {\n1178\t            char ch = static_cast<char>(c);\n1179\t            // Comment/string stripping only for .sol source — f.get();\n1195\t                  in_block = false;\n1196\t                }\n1197\t                continue;\n1198\t              }\n1199\t              if (in_str)\n1200\t              {\n1201\t f.get();\n1213\t                in_line = true;\n1214\t                continue;\n1215\t              }\n1216\t              if (ch == '/' && f.peek() == '*')\n1217\t              {\n1218\t (≥3 nesting).\n1235\t              if (ch == ta_marker[ta_match_pos])\n1236\t              {\n1237\t                ++ta_match_pos;\n1238\t                if (ta_match_pos == ta_marker.size())\n1239\t                {\n1240\t                  ++ta_run;\n1241\t                  ta_match_pos = 0;\n1242\t                  if (ta_run >= 3)\n1243\t                  {\n1244\t                    nested_dyn_detected = true;\n1245\t                    break;\n1246\t                  }\n1247\t                }\n1248\t              }\n1249\t              else\n1250\t              {\n1251\t                ta_match_pos = (ch == ta_marker[0]) ? 1 : 0;\n1252\t                if (ta_match_pos == 0)\n1253\t                  ta_run = 0;\n1254\t              }\n1255\t              // Count `t_mapping$_` markers WITHIN ONE typeIdentifier\n1256\t              // JSON string.
