 return false;\n}\n\n// This method creates a GOTO program by parsing the input program files.\n//\n// \\param options - options to be passed to the program parser,\n// \\param goto_functions - this is where the created GOTO program is stored.\nbool esbmc_parseoptionst::parse_goto_program(\n  optionst &options,\n  goto_functionst &goto_functions)\n{\n  try\n  {\n    if (parse(cmdline))\n      return true;\n\n    if (cmdline.isset(\"parse-tree-too\") || cmdline.isset(\"parse-tree-only\"))\n    {\n      std::ostringstream oss;\n      for (auto &it : langmap)\n        it.second->show_parse(oss);\n      log_status(\"{}\", oss.str());\n      if (cmdline.isset(\"parse-tree-only\"))\n        exit(0);\n    }\n\n    // Typechecking (old frontend) or adjust (clang frontend)\n    if (typecheck())\n      return true;\n    if (final())\n      return true;\n\n    // we no longer need any parse trees or language files\n    clear_parse();\n\n    if (cmdline.isset(\"symbol-table-too\") || cmdline.isset(\"symbol-table-only\"))\n    {\n      std::ostringstream oss;\n      show_symbol_table_plain(oss);\n      log_status(\"{}\", oss.str());\n      if (cmdline.isset(\"symbol-table-only\"))\n        exit(0);\n    }\n\n    // Solidity implicit default: enable --no-standard-checks for any\n    // Solidity run. C-level safety checks (pointer/align/vla/scanf/...)\n    // emit false positives on Yul-lowered code, and the two\n    // semantically-meaningful checks (bounds, div-by-zero) are now\n    // opt-in via the positive --bounds-check / --div-by-zero-check.\n    {\n      bool is_solidity = cmdline.isset(\"sol\");\n      if (!is_solidity)\n        for (const auto &arg : cmdline.args)\n          if (arg.size() >= 4 && arg.substr(arg.size() - 4) == \".sol\")\n          {\n            is_solidity = true;\n            break;\n          }\n      if (is_solidity)\n        options.set_option(\"no-standard-checks\", true);\n\n      // Solidity coverage auto-enable: drop user/library asserts (under\n      // branch/condition coverage modes only — assertion-coverage is exempt\n      // because it would self-zero) and symex pointer-points-to claims, so\n      // coverage metrics aren't contaminated by stdlib/Solidity-model guards\n      // nor by dynamic dereference claims. Must run BEFORE goto_convert\n      // because no-assertions is consumed by convert_assert\n      // (goto_convert.cpp:978).\n      if (is_solidity)\n      {\n        const bool any_assert_cov = cmdline.isset(\"assertion-coverage\") ||\n                                    cmdline.isset(\"assertion-coverage-claims\");\n        const bool any_branch_or_cond_cov =\n          cmdline.isset(\"branch-coverage\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"branch-coverage-claims\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"branch-function-coverage\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"branch-function-coverage-claims\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"condition-coverage\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"condition-coverage-claims\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"condition-coverage-rm\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"condition-coverage-claims-rm\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"solidity-path-coverage\");\n        if (any_branch_or_cond_cov)\n          options.set_option(\"no-assertions\", true);\n        if (any_branch_or_cond_cov || any_assert_cov)\n        {\n          // Mirror set_neg_unless_pos pattern below so explicit\n          // --symex-pointer-check wins over the auto-enable.\n          if (!cmdline.isset(\"symex-pointer-check\"))\n            options.set_option(\"no-symex-pointer-check\", true);\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Expand --no-standard-checks into individual options before goto_convert,\n    // because VLA size checks are generated during goto conversion.\n    // NOTE: `no-narrowing-check` is deliberately NOT expanded here — it\n    // is only read by `goto_check` (a separate pass after goto_convert),\n    // and setting it at this point has been observed to destabilise\n    // error-trace construction in bounded-mode runs that hit a\n    // counter-example (mapping_12 regression). The second expansion\n    // block (before `goto_check`) does the right thing.\n    if (\n      cmdline.isset(\"no-standard-checks\") ||\n      options.get_bool_option(\"no-standard-checks\"))\n    {\n      // Positive opt-in flags override the umbrella for the two\n      // Solidity-relevant checks. SMTChecker idiom:\n      //   --no-standard-checks --div-by-zero-check\n      // means \"disable everything standard except div-by-zero\".\n      auto set_neg_unless_pos = [&](const char *neg, const char *pos) {\n        if (!cmdline.isset(pos))\n          options.set_option(neg, true);\n      };\n      // Couple the pointer-deref check to --bounds-check: a symbolic-size\n      // dynamic array (`new T[](n)`) lowers to a malloc'd region and its OOB\n      // access surfaces as a *dereference* failure, so --bounds-check must be\n      // able to re-enable pointer-check (otherwise no flag can detect it).\n      // Only when bounds-check is EFFECTIVELY on: a contradictory\n      // `--bounds-check --no-bounds-check` keeps pointer-check disabled too.\n      if (!cmdline.isset(\"bounds-check\") || cmdline.isset(\"no-bounds-check\"))\n        options.set_option(\"no-pointer-check\", true);\n      set_neg_unless_pos(\"no-div-by-zero-check\", \"div-by-zero-check\");\n      options.set_option(\"no-pointer-relation-check\", true);\n      options.set_option(\"no-unlimited-scanf-check\", true);\n      options.set_option(\"no-vla-size-check\", true);\n      options.set_option(\"no-align-check\", true);\n      set_neg_unless_pos(\"no-bounds-check\", \"bounds-check\");\n    }\n\n    log_progress(\"Generating GOTO Program\");\n    goto_convert(context, options, goto_functions);\n  }\n\n  catch (const char *e)\n  {\n    log_error(\"{}\", e);\n    return true;\n  }\n\n  catch (const std::string &e)\n  {\n    log_error(\"{}\", e);\n    return true;\n  }\n\n  catch (std::bad_alloc &)\n  {\n    log_error(\"Out of memory\");\n    return true;\n  }\n\n  return false;\n}\n\n// This method performs various analyses and transformations\n// on the given GOTO program. They involve all the techniques that we class\n// as \"static analyses\" - performed on the given GOTO program before it is\n// symbolically executed. Examples of such techniques include:\n//\n//  - interval analysis,\n//  - removal of unreachable code,\n//  - preprocessing the program for k-induction,\n//  - applying GOTO contractors,\n//  - ...\n//\n// \\param options - various options used by the processing methods,\n// \\param goto_functions - reference to the GOTO program to be processed.\nbool esbmc_parseoptionst::process_goto_program(\n  optionst &options,\n  goto_functionst &goto_functions)\n{\n  try\n  {\n    namespacet ns(context);\n\n    bool is_mul =\n      cmdline.isset(\"multi-property\") || cmdline.isset(\"parallel-solving\");\n    is_coverage = cmdline.isset(\"assertion-coverage\") ||\n                  cmdline.isset(\"assertion-coverage-claims\") ||\n                  cmdline.isset(\"condition-coverage\") ||\n                  cmdline.isset(\"condition-coverage-claims\") ||\n                  cmdline.isset(\"condition-coverage-rm\") ||\n                  cmdline.isset(\"condition-coverage-claims-rm\") ||\n                  cmdline.isset(\"branch-coverage\") ||\n                  cmdline.isset(\"branch-coverage-claims\") ||\n                  cmdline.isset(\"branch-function-coverage\") ||\n                  cmdline.isset(\"branch-function-coverage-claims\") ||\n                  cmdline.isset(\"k-path-coverage\") ||\n                  cmdline.isset(\"k-path-coverage-claims\") ||\n                  cmdline.isset(\"solidity-path-coverage\");\n\n    // For coverage mode, treat extra input files (cmdline.args[1:]) as include\n    // files so that the coverage location_pool covers all input sources.\n    if (is_coverage && cmdline.args.size() > 1)\n      for (size_t i = 1; i < cmdline.args.size(); i++)\n        config.ansi_c.include_files.push_back(cmdline.args[i]);\n\n    // For Solidity coverage mode: neutralize the multi-transaction harness loop.\n    // The _ESBMC_Main_* functions contain a while(nondet_bool()) loop that calls\n    // user functions repeatedly. This causes massive symex overhead in coverage\n    // mode where we only need each function executed once. Convert backward GOTOs\n    // (loop back-edges) in _ESBMC_Main* functions to SKIPs so the loop body\n    // executes exactly once.\n    //\n    // --coverage-multi-tx opts OUT of this neutralization: the loop stays live\n    // (bounded by --unwind), so a branch reachable only through a state-building\n    // call sequence (deposit(); withdraw();) becomes coverable and the Foundry\n    // generator can reconstruct the multi-call sequence. Costs symex time, hence\n    // opt-in.\n    if (is_coverage && !cmdline.isset(\"coverage-multi-tx\"))\n    {\n      bool is_sol = cmdline.isset(\"sol\");\n      if (!is_sol)\n        for (const auto &arg : cmdline.args)\n          if (arg.size() >= 4 && arg.substr(arg.size() - 4) == \".sol\")\n          {\n            is_sol = true;\n            break;\n          }\n      if (is_sol)\n      {\n        Forall_goto_functions (f_it, goto_functions)\n        {\n          std::string fname = f_it->first.as_string();\n          if (fname.find(\"_ESBMC_Main\") == std::string::npos)\n            continue;\n          Forall_goto_program_instructions (it, f_it->second.body)\n          {\n            if (it->is_backwards_goto())\n              it->make_skip();\n          }\n        }\n        goto_functions.update();\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Solidity implicit default: re-applied here for the read_goto_binary\n    // path that bypasses parse_goto_program's earlier setter.\n    {\n      bool is_solidity = cmdline.isset(\"sol\");\n      if (!is_solidity)\n        for (const auto &arg : cmdline.args)\n          if (arg.size() >= 4 && arg.substr(arg.size() - 4) == \".sol\")\n          {\n            is_solidity = true;\n            break;\n          }\n      if (is_solidity)\n        options.set_option(\"no-standard-checks\", true);\n\n      // Coverage auto-enable on the read_goto_binary path. Only the symex\n      // gate is meaningful here (no-assertions is too late: ASSERT\n      // instructions were already baked into the loaded .goto), but we\n      // set both for symmetry with the parse_goto_program branch.\n      if (is_solidity)\n      {\n        const bool any_assert_cov = cmdline.isset(\"assertion-coverage\") ||\n                                    cmdline.isset(\"assertion-coverage-claims\");\n        const bool any_branch_or_cond_cov =\n          cmdline.isset(\"branch-coverage\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"branch-coverage-claims\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"branch-function-coverage\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"branch-function-coverage-claims\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"condition-coverage\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"condition-coverage-claims\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"condition-coverage-rm\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"condition-coverage-claims-rm\") ||\n          cmdline.isset(\"solidity-path-coverage\");\n        if (any_branch_or_cond_cov)\n          options.set_option(\"no-assertions\", true);\n        if (any_branch_or_cond_cov || any_assert_cov)\n        {\n          if (!cmdline.isset(\"symex-pointer-check\"))\n            options.set_option(\"no-symex-pointer-check\", true);\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Expand --no-standard-checks before goto_check (also expanded before\n    // goto_convert in parse_goto_program; re-expanding here is idempotent\n    // and covers the read_goto_binary path).\n    if (\n      cmdline.isset(\"no-standard-checks\") ||\n      options.get_bool_option(\"no-standard-checks\"))\n    {\n      auto set_neg_unless_pos = [&](const char *neg, const char *pos) {\n        if (!cmdline.isset(pos))\n          options.set_option(neg, true);\n      };\n      // See the goto_convert-side block above: --bounds-check re-enables the\n      // pointer-deref check so symbolic-size dynamic-array OOB (a dereference\n      // failure) is detectable. A contradictory `--bounds-check\n      // --no-bounds-check` keeps pointer-check disabled too.\n      if (!cmdline.isset(\"bounds-check\") || cmdline.isset(\"no-bounds-check\"))\n        options.set_option(\"no-pointer-check\", true);\n      set_neg_unless_pos(\"no-div-by-zero-check\", \"div-by-zero-check\");\n      options.set_option(\"no-pointer-relation-check\", true);\n      options.set_option(\"no-unlimited-scanf-check\", true);\n      options.set_option(\"no-vla-size-check\", true);\n      options.set_option(\"no-align-check\", true);\n      set_neg_unless_pos(\"no-bounds-check\", \"bounds-check\");\n      set_neg_unless_pos(\"no-narrowing-check\", \"narrowing-check\");\n    }\n\n    // Start by removing all no-op instructions and unreachable code\n    if (!(cmdline.isset(\"no-remove-no-op\")))\n      remove_no_op(goto_functions);\n\n    // We should skip this 'remove-unreachable' removal in goto-cov and multi-property\n    // - multi-property wants to find all the bugs in the src code\n    // - assertion-coverage wants to find out unreached codes (asserts)\n    // - however, the optimization below will remove codes during the Goto stage\n    if (\n      !(cmdline.isset(\"no-remove-unreachable\") || is_mul || is_coverage) ||\n      cmdline.isset(\"condition-coverage-rm\") ||\n      cmdline.isset(\"condition-coverage-claims-rm\"))\n      remove_unreachable(goto_functions);\n\n    // Apply all the initialized algorithms\n    for (auto &algorithm : goto_preprocess_algorithms)\n    {\n      if (cmdline.isset(\"function\"))\n        algorithm->setTarget(cmdline.getval(\"function\"));\n      algorithm->run(goto_functions);\n    }\n\n    // do partial inlining\n    if (!cmdline.isset(\"no-inlining\"))\n    {\n      if (cmdline.isset(\"full-inlining\"))\n        goto_inline(goto_functions, options, ns);\n      else\n        goto_partial_inline(goto_functions, options, ns);\n    }\n\n    if (cmdline.isset(\"gcse\"))\n    {\n      std::shared_ptr<value_set_analysist> vsa =\n        std::make_shared<value_set_analysist>(ns);\n      try\n      {\n        log_status(\"Computing Value-Set Analysis (VSA)\");\n        (*vsa)(goto_functions);\n      }\n      catch (vsa_not_implemented_exception &)\n      {\n        log_warning(\n          \"Unable to compute VSA due to incomplete implementation. {\n              const auto &file = i_it->location.get_file();\n              const auto &line = i_it->location.get_line();\n\n              if (!line.empty())\n                loc = \" [\" + file.as_string() + \":\" + line.as_string() + \"]\";\n              else\n                loc = \" [\" + file.as_string() + \"]\";\n            }\n            log_status(\"{} -> {}({}){}\", caller, callee, args, loc);\n          }\n        }\n      }\n      std::exit(0);\n    }\n\n    // Translate the GOTO program to C and output it into the log or\n    // a specified output file\n    if (cmdline.isset(\"goto2c\"))\n    {\n      // Creating a translator here\n      goto2ct goto2c(ns, goto_functions);\n      goto2c.preprocess();\n      goto2c.check();\n      std::string res = goto2c.translate();\n\n      const std::string &filename = options.get_option(\"output\");\n      if (!filename.empty())\n      {\n        // Outputting the translated program into the output file\n        std::ofstream out(filename);\n        assert(out);\n        out << res;\n      }\n      else\n        std::cout << res;\n      return true;\n    }\n  }\n\n  catch (const char *e)\n  {\n    log_error(\"{}\", e);\n    return true;\n  }\n\n  catch (const std::string &e)\n  {\n    log_error(\"{}\", e);\n    return true;\n  }\n\n  return false;\n}\n\n// This performs the preprocessing of the input program\n// when the old C/C++ frontend (i.e., from \"ansi-c/\" or \"cpp/\") is used.\nvoid esbmc_parseoptionst::preprocessing()\n{\n  try\n  {\n    if (cmdline.args.size() != 1)\n    {\n infile(filename.c_str());\n    if (!infile)\n    {\n      log_error(\"failed to open input file\");\n      return;\n    }\n#ifdef ENABLE_OLD_FRONTEND\n    std::ostringstream oss;\n    if goto_programt &prog = func.body;\n    Forall_goto_program_instructions (p_it, prog)\n      add_monitor_exprs(p_it, prog.instructions, monitors);\n  }\n\n  // Find main function; find first function it != insn_list.end(); ++it)\n  {\n    if (it->type != RETURN)\n      continue;\n    insn_list.insert(it, new_insn);\n  }\n}\n\nstatic void collect_symbol_names(\n  const expr2tc &e,\n  const std::string &prefix,\n  std::set<std::string> &used_syms)\n{\n  if (is_symbol2t(e))\n  {\n    const symbol2t &thesym = to_symbol2t(e);\n    assert(thesym.rlevel == 0);\n    std::string sym = thesym.get_symbol_name();\n\n    used_syms.insert(sym);\n  }\n  else\n  {\n    e->foreach_operand([&prefix, &used_syms](const expr2tc &e) {\n      if (!is_nil_expr(e))\n        collect_symbol_names(e, prefix, used_syms);\n    });\n  }\n}\n\nexpr2tc esbmc_parseoptionst::calculate_a_property_monitor(\n  const std::string &name,\n  std::set<std::string> &used_syms) const\n{\n  const symbolt *fn = context.find_symbol(\"c:@F@\" + name + \"_status\");\n  assert(fn);\n\n  const codet &fn_code = to_code(fn->value);\n  assert(fn_code.get_statement() == \"block\");\n  assert(fn_code.operands().size() == 1);\n\n  const codet &fn_ret = to_code(fn_code.op0());\n  assert(fn_ret.get_statement() == \"return\");\n  assert(fn_ret.operands().size() == 1);\n\n  expr2tc new_main_expr;\n  migrate_expr(fn_ret.op0(), new_main_expr);\n\n  collect_symbol_names(new_main_expr, name, used_syms);\n\n  return new_main_expr;\n}\n\nvoid esbmc_parseoptionst::add_monitor_exprs(\n  goto_programt::targett insn,\n  goto_programt::instructionst &insn_list,\n  const std::map<std::string, std::pair<std::set<std::string>, expr2tc>>\n    &monitors)\n{\n  // We've been handed an instruction, look for assignments to the\n  // symbol we're looking for. actually an assignment that we're interested in?\n  std::string sym_name = sym.get_symbol_name();\n  std::set<std::pair<std::string, expr2tc>> triggered;\n  for (const auto &[prop, pair] : monitors)\n  {\n      log_status(\"Enforcing contracts for {} function(s)\", to_enforce.size());\n      // Pass --function entry point so the enforce wrapper allocates fresh\n      // backing storage for pointer esbmc_parseoptionst::resolve_color_option() const\n{\n  const char *raw = cmdline.getval(\"color\");\n  std::string val = (raw && *raw) ? raw : \"auto\";\n  if (val != \"auto\" && val != \"always\" && by one or more alphanumeric/hyphen characters,\n// stopping at delimiters like '.', ',', ' ', ')', '\\'', '\"', or end of string.\nstatic std::string colorize_flag_refs(const std::string &text)\n{\n  std::string result;\n  size_t i = 0;\n  while (i < text.size())\n  {\n    if (\n      i + 2 < text.size() && text[i] == '-' && text[i + 1] == '-' &&\n      (std::isalnum(text[i + 2]) || text[i + 2] == '-'))\n    {\n      size_t start = i;\n      i += 2;\n      while (i < text.size() && (std::isalnum(text[i]) || text[i] == '-'))\n        i++;\n      result += CLR_BOLD;\n      result += text.substr(start, i - start);\n      result += CLR_RESET;\n    }\n    else\n    {\n      result += text[i];\n      i++;\n    }\n  }\n  return result;\n}\n\n// This prints the ESBMC version and a list bool use_color = resolve_color_option();\n\n  // Print the \"* * *     ESBMC x.y.z     * * *\"\n  auto const esbmc_string = fmt::format(\" ESBMC {} \", ESBMC_VERSION);\n  auto const title_start = std::ostringstream oss;\n  oss << cmdline.cmdline_options;\n\n  if (!use_color)\n  {\n    log_status(\"{}\", oss.str());\n    return;\n  }\n\n  // Colorize: group headers in bold cyan, option names in bold,\n  // and --flag references in descriptions in bold\n  std::istringstream iss(oss.str());\n  std::string line;\n  while (std::getline(iss, line))\n  {\n    if (!line.empty() && line[0] != ' ' && line.back() == ':')\n      // Group header (e.g. \"Printing options:\")\n      fmt::print(messaget::state.out, CLR_BOLD_CYAN \"{}\" CLR_RESET \"\\n\", line);\n    else if (\n      line.size() >= 3 && line[0] == ' ' && line[1] == ' ' && line[2] == '-')\n    {\n      // Option line: colorize the flag portion (up to the description)\n      auto desc_pos = line.find(\"  \", 4);\n      if (desc_pos != std::string::npos)\n        fmt::print(\n          messaget::state.out,\n          CLR_BOLD \"{}\" CLR_RESET \"{}\\n\",\n          line.substr(0, desc_pos),\n          colorize_flag_refs(line.substr(desc_pos)));\n      else\n        fmt::print(messaget::state.out, CLR_BOLD \"{}\" CLR_RESET \"\\n\", line);\n    }\n    else\n      fmt::print(messaget::state.out, \"{}\\n\", colorize_flag_refs(line));\n  }\n\n  // Restore everything back to original output stream.\n  messaget::state.out = outstream;\n}\n\n// When k-induction exhausts all k-steps without a options.get_bool_option(\"no-unwinding-assertions\");\n  const bool saved_partial_loops = options.get_bool_option(\"partial-loops\");\n  const std::string saved_unwind = options.set_option(\"no-unwinding-assertions\", true);\n  options.set_option(\"partial-loops\", true);\n  options.set_option(\"unwind\", integer2string(k_step));\n  options.set_option(\"diagnose-unknown-properties\", true);\n\n  bmct bmc(goto_functions, options, context);\n\n  log_progress(\n    \"\\nDiagnosing unresolved properties (inductive step, k = {:d}):\", double_paren(R\"(\\((\\([^()]*\\))\\))\");\n  std::string prev;\n  do\n  {\n    prev = s;\n    s = std::regex_replace(s, double_paren, \"$1\");\n  } while (s != prev);\n\n  // Remove parens in array else\n      // this could be\n      // 1. the loop is too large that we cannot goto-unwind it\n      // 2. the loop is somewhat non-deterministic that we cannot run goto-unwind\n \"covered\" : \"uncovered\";\n1399\t      // k-path Phase-2 (#4335): annotate each claim as feasible (a\n1400\t      // maximal element of the subsumption lattice and thus part of the\n1401\t      // spanning set) or spanning-set-redundant (subsumed by a stronger\n1402\t      // emitted goal — covering it adds no information beyond covering\n1403\t      // its subsumer).\n1404\t      if (is_k_path_cov)\n1405\t      {\n1406\t        const auto &redundant = goto_coveraget::k_path_spanning_redundant;\n1407\t        claim_entry[\"feasibility\"] = redundant.count({claim_msg, claim_loc}) > 0\n1408\t                                       ? \"spanning-set-redundant\"\n1409\t                                       : \"feasible\";\n1410\t      }\n1411\t\n1412\t      // Solidity complete-path coverage: the CE->generalisation interface.\n1413\t      // Tri-state per complete path, plus the bound the verdict was reached\n1414\t      // under and how the path exits.\n1415\t      if (is_path_cov)\n1416\t      {\n1417\t        char v = 0;\n1418\t        {\n1419\t          std::lock_guard lock(goto_coveraget::claim_outcome_mutex);\n1420\t          auto it_o = goto_coveraget::claim_outcome.find(claim_sig);\n1421\t          if (it_o != goto_coveraget::claim_outcome.end())\n1422\t            v = it_o->second;\n1423\t        }\n1424\t        // Witnessed = refuted this run, or already refuted in an earlier\n1425\t        // escalation round (cross-run covered-set). Either way a concrete\n1426\t        // input exists for this path.\n1427\t        const bool prior =\n1428\t          goto_coveraget::path_witnessed_earlier({claim_msg, claim_loc});\n1429\t        const bool witnessed = covered || prior;\n1430\t\n1431\t        // F: feasible, CE in hand.\n1432\t        // I: PROVEN unreachable. No coverage configuration can establish this\n1433\t        //    today — see path_cov_can_prove_unreachable() — so this arm is\n1434\t        //    currently unreachable by construction, deliberately.\n1435\t        // U: everything else, INCLUDING a claim that \"holds\" at this\n1436\t        //    exploration: that means no witness within one-or-N transactions\n1437\t        //    from the post-constructor entry state, not that the path is\n1438\t        //    unreachable. It stays U and is flagged `bounded_holds`.\n1439\t        std::string tri;\n1440\t        if (witnessed)\n1441\t          tri = \"F\";\n1442\t        else if (v == 'P' && unbounded_run)\n1443\t          tri = \"I\";\n1444\t        else\n1445\t          tri = \"U\";\n1446\t        claim_entry[\"status\"] = tri;\n1447\t        if (tri == \"U\")\n1448\t        {\n1449\t          // Same single source as the stdout breakdown, so the file and the\n1450\t          // terminal can never disagree about why a path is uncovered.\n1451\t          const std::string tok =\n1452\t            goto_coveraget::path_u_reason_token({claim_msg, claim_loc});\n1453\t          claim_entry[\"u_reason\"] = tok;\n1454\t          if (tok == \"named-obstacle\")\n1455\t          {\n1456\t            auto ob =\n1457\t              goto_coveraget::named_obstacle_paths.find({claim_msg, claim_loc});\n1458\t            if (ob != goto_coveraget::named_obstacle_paths.end())\n1459\t              claim_entry[\"u_reason_detail\"] = ob->second;\n1460\t          }\n1461\t          else if (tok == \"unit-not-entered\")\n1462\t          {\n1463\t            // WHY the unit was not entered, not just that it wasn't: excluded\n1464\t            // on purpose by --focus-function is a normal per-method run, while\n1465\t            // \"the harness never entered it\" is a defect. A consumer that\n1466\t            // cannot tell them apart would treat a deliberate narrowing as a\n1467\t            // broken run, or worse, the reverse.\n1468\t            const size_t p = claim_msg.rfind(\":path:\");\n1469\t            const std::string unit =\n1470\t              p == std::string::npos ? claim_msg : claim_msg.substr(0, p);\n1471\t            auto ue = goto_coveraget::units_not_entered.find(unit);\n1472\t            if (ue != goto_coveraget::units_not_entered.end())\n1473\t              claim_entry[\"u_reason_detail\"] = ue->second;\n1474\t          }\n1475\t        }\n1476\t        // Kept alongside the token: a consumer that already reads these keys\n1477\t        // keeps working, and `bounded_holds` additionally marks the U's worth\n1478\t        // re-checking under a deeper exploration.\n1479\t        if (v == 'P' && !unbounded_run)\n1480\t          claim_entry[\"bounded_holds\"] = true;\n1481\t        if (!witnessed && v == 0)\n1482\t          // Never handed to the solver this run (sliced away, or skipped\n1483\t          // because an earlier round already covered a different path).\n1484\t          claim_entry[\"not_solved_this_run\"] = true;\n1485\t\n1486\t        claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"max_tx\"] = max_tx.empty() ? \"default\" : max_tx;\n1487\t        claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"unwind\"] =\n1488\t          unwind_s.empty() ? \"default\" : unwind_s;\n1489\t        claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"kind\"] = unbounded_run ? \"unbounded\" : \"bounded\";\n1490\t        claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"tx_exploration\"] = tx_exploration;\n1491\t        if (loops_truncated)\n1492\t          claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"loops_truncated\"] = true;\n1493\t        // Both revert shapes exit the transaction, so both are \"revert\": the\n1494\t        // custom-error one (ASSUME(false) in a #sol_error callee) and the\n1495\t        // rollback one (require/revert(\"msg\"), which restores `*this` and then\n1496\t        // reaches END_FUNCTION). Reporting the latter as \"normal\" would claim a\n1497\t        // reverting transaction succeeded.\n1498\t        const bool ck_err =\n1499\t          goto_coveraget::revert_paths.count({claim_msg, claim_loc}) > 0;\n1500\t        const bool ck_rb =\n1501\t          goto_coveraget::rollback_revert_paths.count({claim_msg, claim_loc}) >\n1502\t          0;\n1503\t        const bool ck_un =\n1504\t          goto_coveraget::undetermined_exit_paths.count({claim_msg, claim_loc}) >\n1505\t          0;\n1506\t        claim_entry[\"exit_kind\"] =\n1507\t          (ck_err || ck_rb) ? \"revert\" : (ck_un ? \"undetermined\" : \"normal\");\n1508\t        if (ck_rb)\n1509\t          // Distinguishes the two: here the rollback IS modelled, so\n1510\t          // final_state is the correctly restored post-state.\n1511\t          claim_entry[\"revert_kind\"] = \"rollback\";\n1512\t        else if (ck_err)\n1513\t          claim_entry[\"revert_kind\"] = \"custom-error\";\n1514\t        else if (ck_un)\n1515\t          claim_entry[\"exit_kind_undetermined_reason\"] =\n1516\t            \"reaches END_FUNCTION bypassing the function epilogue and carries \"\n1517\t            \"no rollback restore: a `require` failing before any state write \"\n1518\t            \"and a plain early `return` compile to the same shape, so this is \"\n1519\t            \"either a revert or a normal early exit\";\n1520\t        claim_entry[\"witnessed_in_earlier_round\"] = prior && !covered;\n1521\t\n1522\t        // path_id == enc(pi): the integer encoding the path's whole decision\n1523\t        // sequence (tr accumulator). Text before \":path:\" is the function.\n1524\t        const auto pos = claim_msg.rfind(\":path:\");\n1525\t        if (pos != std::string::npos)\n1526\t        {\n1527\t          claim_entry[\"path_id\"] = claim_msg.substr(pos + 6);\n1528\t          claim_entry[\"path_function\"] = claim_msg.substr(0, pos);\n1529\t        }\n1530\t        // The decision depth, i.e. the `cnt` half of the path's identity. A\n1531\t        // stage-2 query is `tr == enc && cnt == depth`, so a consumer that only\n1532\t        // had `path_id` could not build one; it had to be told the depth out of\n1533\t        // band, which is the opposite of an interface.\n1534\t        {\n1535\t          auto dp =\n1536\t            goto_coveraget::path_decision_depth.find({claim_msg, claim_loc});\n1537\t          if (dp != goto_coveraget::path_decision_depth.end())\n1538\t            claim_entry[\"path_depth\"] = dp->second;\n1539\t\n1540\t          // ---- THE ORDERED DECISION SEQUENCE, for F claims only ----\n1541\t          //\n1542\t          // This is what makes path coverage comparable with branch coverage at\n1543\t          // all: the two metrics share no denominator until the witnessed paths\n1544\t          // are projected onto the DECISIONS they walk. `path_id` cannot be\n1545\t          // projected — `enc` records the arms and nothing about the sites, so\n1546\t          // only the enumerator knows which instruction each bit came from.\n1547\t          //\n1548\t          // RESTRICTED TO F on purpose, and it is not merely a saving. F is the\n1549\t          // only status the projection can use (an uncovered path witnesses no\n1550\t          // decision), and F is rare — single digits per unit — while a unit can\n1551\t          // enumerate 120166 paths. Emitting for every claim would put the\n1552\t          // report's size in the same order as the path count for no gain.\n1553\t          if (tri == \"F\" && pos != std::string::npos)\n1554\t          {\n1555\t            const std::string unit = claim_msg.substr(0, pos);\n1556\t            const uint64_t penc =\n1557\t              strtoull(claim_msg.substr(pos + 6).c_str(), nullptr, 10);\n1558\t            auto ti = goto_coveraget::path_decision_table.find(unit);\n1559\t            auto xi = goto_coveraget::path_decision_index.find(unit);\n1560\t            if (\n1561\t              ti != goto_coveraget::path_decision_table.end() &&\n1562\t              xi != goto_coveraget::path_decision_index.end() &&\n1563\t              dp != goto_coveraget::path_decision_depth.end() &&\n1564\t              dp->second > 0)\n1565\t            {\n1566\t              const uint64_t pdepth = dp->second;\n1567\t              json seq = json::array();\n1568\t              size_t missing = 0;\n1569\t              for (uint64_t k = 0; k < pdepth; ++k)\n1570\t              {\n1571\t                const uint64_t key = penc >> (pdepth - 1 - k);\n1572\t                auto di = xi->second.find(key);\n1573\t                if (di == xi->second.end() || di->second >= ti->second.size())\n1574\t                {\n1575\t                  // Reported as a hole, never skipped. A shorter array would\n1576\t                  // read as \"this path walks fewer decisions\" — a claim about\n1577\t                  // the path, when the truth is a claim about the recording.\n1578\t                  json h;\n1579\t                  h[\"index\"] = k + 1;\n1580\t                  h[\"unrecorded_prefix_enc\"] = std::to_string(key);\n1581\t                  seq.push_back(h);\n1582\t                  ++missing;\n1583\t                  continue;\n1584\t                }\n1585\t                const auto &d = ti->second[di->second];\n1586\t                const bool arm_taken = (key & 1) != 0;\n1587\t                json e;\n1588\t                e[\"index\"] = k + 1;\n1589\t                json dloc = parse_claim_location(d.loc);\n1590\t                e[\"file\"] = dloc[\"file\"];\n1591\t                e[\"line\"] = dloc[\"line\"];\n1592\t                e[\"column\"] = dloc[\"column\"];\n1593\t                e[\"function\"] = dloc[\"function\"];\n1594\t                e[\"operand\"] = d.sub;\n1595\t                e[\"arm\"] = arm_taken ? \"taken\" : \"fall-through\";\n1596\t                // This arm's claim text, already inverted (assert(P) fails when\n1597\t                // P is false, so assert(guard) covers the FALL-THROUGH edge).\n1598\t                // Published rather than left to the consumer: inverting it\n1599\t                // there is a silent error that still produces a number.\n1600\t                //\n1601\t                // DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — do not join on it. Measured: a `require`\n1602\t                // lowers to a guard one `not` deeper under path coverage than\n1603\t                // under branch coverage (the revert-observation gate), so the\n1604\t                // texts differ for the same decision while a plain `if` agrees\n1605\t                // verbatim. See path_decisiont in goto_coverage.h. Join on\n1606\t                // file+line, which is the comparison metric's own unit.\n1607\t                e[\"branch_claim\"] = prettify_solidity_expr(\n1608\t                  arm_taken ? d.cond_arm_true : d.cond_arm_false);\n1609\t                if (d.synthetic_abi_gate)\n1610\t                  // No branch-coverage counterpart AND a location copied from\n1611\t                  // the unit's first body instruction, so a consumer matching on\n1612\t                  // location alone would credit a real decision on that line.\n1613\t                  e[\"synthetic_abi_gate\"] = true;\n1614\t                seq.push_back(e);\n1615\t              }\n1616\t              claim_entry[\"decisions\"] = seq;\n1617\t              if (missing > 0)\n1618\t                claim_entry[\"decisions_unrecorded\"] = missing;\n1619\t            }\n1620\t          }\n1621\t        }\n1622\t\n1623\t        // CE payload: the concrete values behind an F. Absent for I/U (there\n1624\t        // is no counterexample to report).\n1625\t        std::lock_guard lock(goto_coveraget::claim_outcome_mutex);\n1626\t        auto it_ce = goto_coveraget::path_ce.find(claim_sig);\n1627\t        if (it_ce != goto_coveraget::path_ce.end())\n1628\t        {\n1629\t          const auto &ce = it_ce->second;\n1630\t          json ins = json::object();\n1631\t          for (const auto &[n, v] : ce.inputs)\n1632\t            ins[prettify_solidity_expr(n)] = v;\n1633\t          json envj = json::object();\n1634\t          for (const auto &[n, v] : ce.env)\n1635\t            envj[prettify_solidity_expr(n)] = v;\n1636\t          json fin = json::object();\n1637\t          for (const auto &[n, v] : ce.final_state)\n1638\t            fin[prettify_solidity_expr(n)] = v;\n1639\t          claim_entry[\"inputs\"] = ins;\n1640\t          claim_entry[\"env\"] = envj;\n1641\t          // What the outside world returned on this path, in call order. Kept\n1642\t          // separate from `inputs` because a consumer can CHOOSE an input and\n1643\t          // cannot choose this: a replay has to mock the callee to return these\n1644\t          // values. An ARRAY, not a map — repeated calls reuse the same symbol\n1645\t          // name and their order is part of the answer.\n1646\t          json ext = json::array();\n1647\t          for (const auto &[n, v] : ce.extcall_returns)\n1648\t            ext.push_back({{\"symbol\", prettify_solidity_expr(n)}, {\"value\", v}});\n1649\t          claim_entry[\"extcall_returns\"] = ext;\n1650\t          if (ce.extcall_returns.empty())\n1651\t            // NOT \"there were no external calls\": say what is actually known.\n1652\t            //\n1653\t            // This list is ALWAYS empty: nothing anywhere writes to\n1654\t            // ce.extcall_returns. Below is what stands between the value and\n1655\t            // this field, measured on a four-unit contract whose units differ\n1656\t            // ONLY in the syntactic shape the call's result arrives in. There\n1657\t            // are THREE distinct reasons, not one, and a fix for any single one\n1658\t            // leaves the field empty in the other shapes -- which looks exactly\n1659\t            // like no fix at all.\n1660\t            //\n1661\t            //   (a) result bound to a named local (`bool ok = c.f();`) and the\n1662\t            //       assembly form (`success` assigned inside an approximated\n1663\t            //       block): the step DOES reach the harvest and\n1664\t            //       get_nondet_symbol DOES resolve it. It is then dropped\n1665\t            //       because the classification below has exactly three\n1666\t            //       outcomes -- parameter -> inputs, environment -> env,\n1667\t            //       otherwise -> dropped_internal -- and a call's return is a\n1668\t            //       LOCAL, so it lands in the third. There is no bucket for it.\n1669\t            //   (b) low-level `(bool ok, ) = a.call(\"\")`: get_nondet_symbol\n1670\t            //       returns nil, so the step is skipped BEFORE classification.\n1671\t            //       (This is the mechanism an earlier version of this comment\n1672\t            //       named -- correctly, but for this shape only.)\n1673\t            //   (c) used inline (`if (c.f())`): no named local is ever\n1674\t            //       assigned, so no step carries the value at all.\n1675\t            //\n1676\t            // The _ESBMC_Nondet_Extcall_* symbols that ARE in the trace are the\n1677\t            // re-entry model's method-choice bits, not the returned value\n1678\t            // (measured: identical on two paths that disagree about it), so\n1679\t            // they are deliberately not reported here.\n1680\t            claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"extcall_returns_unavailable_reason\"] =\n1681\t              \"not implemented yet, and for three different reasons depending \"\n1682\t              \"on the syntactic shape the call's result arrives in; this field \"\n1683\t              \"does NOT say which one applies to this claim. (a) bound to a \"\n1684\t              \"named local, or assigned inside an approximated assembly block: \"\n1685\t              \"the value IS harvested and resolved, then dropped because the \"\n1686\t              \"classification has buckets only for parameters and environment \"\n1687\t              \"values and a call's return is a local. (b) low-level \"\n1688\t              \"`(bool ok, ) = a.call(...)`: get_nondet_symbol returns nil, so \"\n1689\t              \"the step is skipped before classification. (c) used inline, \"\n1690\t              \"`if (c.f())`: no named local is assigned, so no trace step \"\n1691\t              \"carries it. The _ESBMC_Nondet_Extcall_* symbols that ARE in the \"\n1692\t              \"trace are the re-entry model's method-choice bits, not the \"\n1693\t              \"returned value (measured: identical on two paths that disagree \"\n1694\t              \"about it), so they are deliberately not reported here. An empty \"\n1695\t              \"list means UNKNOWN, not 'this path performs no external call'\";\n1696\t          // Contract state this path STARTED from. Without it a path guarded by\n1697\t          // state an earlier transaction established cannot be replayed from\n1698\t          // the inputs alone.\n1699\t          json entry = json::object();\n1700\t          for (const auto &[n, v] : ce.entry_storage)\n1701\t            entry[prettify_solidity_expr(n)] = v;\n1702\t          claim_entry[\"entry_storage\"] = entry;\n1703\t          if (!ce.entry_storage_known)\n1704\t            // Never let an empty entry_storage be read as \"the contract started\n1705\t            // empty\": say that the marker was not observed instead.\n1706\t            claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"entry_storage_unavailable_reason\"] =\n1707\t              \"the entry marker for this path's function was not seen in the \"\n1708\t              \"trace, so the state it started from was not captured; an empty \"\n1709\t              \"entry_storage here means UNKNOWN, not 'no state'\";\n1710\t          // A custom-error revert in a scope the revert-observation gate does\n1711\t          // NOT cover (constructor / library / free function) is still modelled\n1712\t          // by ASSUME(false) with no rollback, so the harvested values are the\n1713\t          // state AT the revert, not the post-state — on-chain the transaction\n1714\t          // is undone and the post-state is the pre-call state. Publishing\n1715\t          // those under `final_state` would be a wrong value carrying a\n1716\t          // disclaimer; publish them under their true meaning instead and leave\n1717\t          // `final_state` empty, since the post-state is genuinely unavailable.\n1718\t          if (ce.revert_pre_rollback)\n1719\t          {\n1720\t            claim_entry[\"state_at_revert_point\"] = fin;\n1721\t            claim_entry[\"final_state\"] = json::object();\n1722\t          }\n1723\t          else\n1724\t            claim_entry[\"final_state\"] = fin;\n1725\t          // State this path WROTE but whose value is not renderable (mapping /\n1726\t          // dynamic-array stores). Listed so \"absent from final_state\" is never\n1727\t          // read as \"unchanged\".\n1728\t          if (!ce.state_written_unrendered.empty())\n1729\t          {\n1730\t            json un = json::array();\n1731\t            for (const auto &n : ce.state_written_unrendered)\n1732\t              un.push_back(prettify_solidity_expr(n));\n1733\t            claim_entry[\"state_written_value_unavailable\"] = un;\n1734\t          }\n1735\t          // Not silent: say how many nondet values were classified as harness\n1736\t          // plumbing and left out of `inputs`/`env`.\n1737\t          claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"harness_nondets_dropped\"] =\n1738\t            ce.dropped_internal;\n1739\t          // How the values were harvested. REQUIRED for the reader to\n1740\t          // interpret an empty final_state: with `sliced` true the symex\n1741\t          // slicer kept only what the path claim depends on — and a path\n1742\t          // claim's guard mentions only the ghost accumulators — so state\n1743\t          // writes are legitimately absent rather than non-existent. Re-run\n1744\t          // with --no-slice to obtain the post-state.\n1745\t          claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"sliced\"] = ce.sliced;\n1746\t          claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"payload_symbols_exempt_from_slicing\"] =\n1747\t            ce.payload_symbols_protected;\n1748\t          claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"compact_trace\"] = ce.compact_trace;\n1749\t          claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"scoped_to_claim\"] = ce.scoped_to_claim;\n1750\t          if (!ce.scoped_to_claim)\n1751\t            claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"post_state_may_include_later_tx\"] =\n1752\t              \"this path's own assert was not found in the trace, so the whole \"\n1753\t              \"trace was scanned; with more than one transaction the reported \"\n1754\t              \"post-state may belong to a later transaction\";\n1755\t          // A custom-error revert is modelled by ASSUME(false) in the error\n1756\t          // callee with NO state rollback, so the harvested post-state is the\n1757\t          // state at the revert point. No coverage configuration can establish this\n        //    today — see path_cov_can_prove_unreachable() — so this arm is\n        //    currently unreachable by construction, deliberately.\n        // U: everything else, INCLUDING a claim that \"holds\" at this\n        //    exploration: that means no witness within one-or-N transactions\n        //    from the post-constructor entry state, not that the path is\n        //    unreachable. It stays U and is flagged `bounded_holds`.\n        std::string tri;\n        if (witnessed)\n          tri = \"F\";\n        else if (v == 'P' && unbounded_run)\n          tri = \"I\";\n        else\n          tri = \"U\";\n        claim_entry[\"status\"] = tri;\n        if (tri == \"U\")\n        {\n          // Same single source as the stdout breakdown, so the file and the\n          // terminal can never disagree about why a path is uncovered.\n          const std::string tok =\n            goto_coveraget::path_u_reason_token({claim_msg, claim_loc});\n          claim_entry[\"u_reason\"] = tok;\n          if (tok == \"named-obstacle\")\n          {\n            auto ob =\n              goto_coveraget::named_obstacle_paths.find({claim_msg, claim_loc});\n            if (ob != goto_coveraget::named_obstacle_paths.end())\n              claim_entry[\"u_reason_detail\"] = ob->second;\n          }\n          else if (tok == \"unit-not-entered\")\n          {\n            // WHY the unit was not entered, not just that it wasn't: excluded\n            // on purpose by --focus-function is a normal per-method run, while\n            // \"the harness never entered it\" is a defect. A consumer that\n            // cannot tell them apart would treat a deliberate narrowing as a\n            // broken run, or worse, the reverse.\n            const size_t p = claim_msg.rfind(\":path:\");\n            const std::string unit =\n              p == std::string::npos ? claim_msg : claim_msg.substr(0, p);\n            auto ue = goto_coveraget::units_not_entered.find(unit);\n            if (ue != goto_coveraget::units_not_entered.end())\n              claim_entry[\"u_reason_detail\"] = ue->second;\n          }\n        }\n        // Kept alongside the token: a consumer that already reads these keys\n        // keeps working, and `bounded_holds` additionally marks the U's worth\n        // re-checking under a deeper exploration.\n        if (v == 'P' && !unbounded_run)\n          claim_entry[\"bounded_holds\"] = true;\n        if (!witnessed && v == 0)\n          // Never handed to the solver this run (sliced away, or skipped\n          // because an earlier round already covered a different path).\n          claim_entry[\"not_solved_this_run\"] = true;\n\n        claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"max_tx\"] = max_tx.empty() ? \"default\" : max_tx;\n        claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"unwind\"] =\n          unwind_s.empty() ? \"default\" : unwind_s;\n        claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"kind\"] = unbounded_run ? \"unbounded\" : \"bounded\";\n        claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"tx_exploration\"] = tx_exploration;\n        if (loops_truncated)\n          claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"loops_truncated\"] = true;\n        // Both revert shapes exit the transaction, so both are \"revert\": the\n        // custom-error one (ASSUME(false) in a #sol_error callee) and the\n        // rollback one (require/revert(\"msg\"), which restores `*this` and then\n        // reaches END_FUNCTION). Reporting the latter as \"normal\" would claim a\n        // reverting transaction succeeded.\n        const bool ck_err =\n          goto_coveraget::revert_paths.count({claim_msg, claim_loc}) > 0;\n        const bool ck_rb =\n          goto_coveraget::rollback_revert_paths.count({claim_msg, claim_loc}) >\n          0;\n        const bool ck_un =\n          goto_coveraget::undetermined_exit_paths.count({claim_msg, claim_loc}) >\n          0;\n        claim_entry[\"exit_kind\"] =\n          (ck_err || ck_rb) ? \"revert\" : (ck_un ? \"undetermined\" : \"normal\");\n        if (ck_rb)\n          // Distinguishes the two: here the rollback IS modelled, so\n          // final_state is the correctly restored post-state.\n          claim_entry[\"revert_kind\"] = \"rollback\";\n        else if (ck_err)\n          claim_entry[\"revert_kind\"] = \"custom-error\";\n        else if (ck_un)\n          claim_entry[\"exit_kind_undetermined_reason\"] =\n            \"reaches END_FUNCTION bypassing the function epilogue and carries \"\n            \"no rollback restore: a `require` failing before any state write \"\n            \"and a plain early `return` compile to the same shape, so this is \"\n            \"either a revert or a normal early exit\";\n        claim_entry[\"witnessed_in_earlier_round\"] = prior && !covered;\n\n        // path_id == enc(pi): the integer encoding the path's whole decision\n        // sequence (tr accumulator). Text before \":path:\" is the function.\n        const auto pos = claim_msg.rfind(\":path:\");\n        if (pos != std::string::npos)\n        {\n          claim_entry[\"path_id\"] = claim_msg.substr(pos + 6);\n          claim_entry[\"path_function\"] = claim_msg.substr(0, pos);\n        }\n        // The decision depth, i.e. the `cnt` half of the path's identity. A\n        // stage-2 query is `tr == enc && cnt == depth`, so a consumer that only\n        // had `path_id` could not build one; it had to be told the depth out of\n        // band, which is the opposite of an interface.\n        {\n          auto dp =\n            goto_coveraget::path_decision_depth.find({claim_msg, claim_loc});\n          if (dp != goto_coveraget::path_decision_depth.end())\n            claim_entry[\"path_depth\"] = dp->second;\n\n          // ---- THE ORDERED DECISION SEQUENCE, for F claims only ----\n          //\n          // This is what makes path coverage comparable with branch coverage at\n          // all: the two metrics share no denominator until the witnessed paths\n          // are projected onto the DECISIONS they walk. `path_id` cannot be\n          // projected — `enc` records the arms and nothing about the sites, so\n          // only the enumerator knows which instruction each bit came from.\n          //\n          // RESTRICTED TO F on purpose, and it is not merely a saving. F is the\n          // only status the projection can use (an uncovered path witnesses no\n          // decision), and F is rare — single digits per unit — while a unit can\n          // enumerate 120166 paths. Emitting for every claim would put the\n          // report's size in the same order as the path count for no gain.\n          if (tri == \"F\" && pos != std::string::npos)\n          {\n            const std::string unit = claim_msg.substr(0, pos);\n            const uint64_t penc =\n              strtoull(claim_msg.substr(pos + 6).c_str(), nullptr, 10);\n            auto ti = goto_coveraget::path_decision_table.find(unit);\n            auto xi = goto_coveraget::path_decision_index.find(unit);\n            if (\n              ti != goto_coveraget::path_decision_table.end() &&\n              xi != goto_coveraget::path_decision_index.end() &&\n              dp != goto_coveraget::path_decision_depth.end() &&\n              dp->second > 0)\n            {\n              const uint64_t pdepth = dp->second;\n              json seq = json::array();\n              size_t missing = 0;\n              for (uint64_t k = 0; k < pdepth; ++k)\n              {\n                const uint64_t key = penc >> (pdepth - 1 - k);\n                auto di = xi->second.find(key);\n                if (di == xi->second.end() || di->second >= ti->second.size())\n                {\n                  // Reported as a hole, never skipped. A shorter array would\n                  // read as \"this path walks fewer decisions\" — a claim about\n                  // the path, when the truth is a claim about the recording.\n                  json h;\n                  h[\"index\"] = k + 1;\n                  h[\"unrecorded_prefix_enc\"] = std::to_string(key);\n                  seq.push_back(h);\n                  ++missing;\n                  continue;\n                }\n                const auto &d = ti->second[di->second];\n                const bool arm_taken = (key & 1) != 0;\n                json e;\n                e[\"index\"] = k + 1;\n                json dloc = parse_claim_location(d.loc);\n                e[\"file\"] = dloc[\"file\"];\n                e[\"line\"] = dloc[\"line\"];\n                e[\"column\"] = dloc[\"column\"];\n                e[\"function\"] = dloc[\"function\"];\n                e[\"operand\"] = d.sub;\n                e[\"arm\"] = arm_taken ? \"taken\" : \"fall-through\";\n                // This arm's claim text, already inverted (assert(P) fails when\n                // P is false, so assert(guard) covers the FALL-THROUGH edge).\n                // Published rather than left to the consumer: inverting it\n                // there is a silent error that still produces a number.\n                //\n                // DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — do not join on it. Measured: a `require`\n                // lowers to a guard one `not` deeper under path coverage than\n                // under branch coverage (the revert-observation gate), so the\n                // texts differ for the same decision while a plain `if` agrees\n                // verbatim. See path_decisiont in goto_coverage.h. Join on\n                // file+line, which is the comparison metric's own unit.\n                e[\"branch_claim\"] = prettify_solidity_expr(\n                  arm_taken ? d.cond_arm_true : d.cond_arm_false);\n                if (d.synthetic_abi_gate)\n                  // No branch-coverage counterpart AND a location copied from\n                  // the unit's first body instruction, so a consumer matching on\n                  // location alone would credit a real decision on that line.\n                  e[\"synthetic_abi_gate\"] = true;\n                seq.push_back(e);\n              }\n              claim_entry[\"decisions\"] = seq;\n              if (missing > 0)\n                claim_entry[\"decisions_unrecorded\"] = missing;\n            }\n          }\n        }\n\n        // CE payload: the concrete values behind an F. Absent for I/U (there\n        // is no counterexample to report).\n        std::lock_guard lock(goto_coveraget::claim_outcome_mutex);\n        auto it_ce = goto_coveraget::path_ce.find(claim_sig);\n        if (it_ce != goto_coveraget::path_ce.end())\n        {\n          const auto &ce = it_ce->second;\n          json ins = json::object();\n          for (const auto &[n, v] : ce.inputs)\n            ins[prettify_solidity_expr(n)] = v;\n          json envj = json::object();\n          for (const auto &[n, v] : ce.env)\n            envj[prettify_solidity_expr(n)] = v;\n          json fin = json::object();\n          for (const auto &[n, v] : ce.final_state)\n            fin[prettify_solidity_expr(n)] = v;\n          claim_entry[\"inputs\"] = ins;\n          claim_entry[\"env\"] = envj;\n          // What the outside world returned on this path, in call order. Kept\n          // separate from `inputs` because a consumer can CHOOSE an input and\n          // cannot choose this: a replay has to mock the callee to return these\n          // values. An ARRAY, not a map — repeated calls reuse the same symbol\n          // name and their order is part of the answer.\n          json ext = json::array();\n          for (const auto &[n, v] : ce.extcall_returns)\n            ext.push_back({{\"symbol\", prettify_solidity_expr(n)}, {\"value\", v}});\n          claim_entry[\"extcall_returns\"] = ext;\n          if (ce.extcall_returns.empty())\n            // NOT \"there were no external calls\": say what is actually known.\n            //\n            // This list is ALWAYS empty: nothing anywhere writes to\n            // ce.extcall_returns. Below is what stands between the value and\n            // this field, measured on a four-unit contract whose units differ\n            // ONLY in the syntactic shape the call's result arrives in. There\n            // are THREE distinct reasons, not one, and a fix for any single one\n            // leaves the field empty in the other shapes -- which looks exactly\n            // like no fix at all.\n            //\n            //   (a) result bound to a named local (`bool ok = c.f();`) and the\n            //       assembly form (`success` assigned inside an approximated\n            //       block): the step DOES reach the harvest and\n            //       get_nondet_symbol DOES resolve it. It is then dropped\n            //       because the classification below has exactly three\n            //       outcomes -- parameter -> inputs, environment -> env,\n            //       otherwise -> dropped_internal -- and a call's return is a\n            //       LOCAL, so it lands in the third. There is no bucket for it.\n            //   (b) low-level `(bool ok, ) = a.call(\"\")`: get_nondet_symbol\n            //       returns nil, so the step is skipped BEFORE classification.\n            //       (This is the mechanism an earlier version of this comment\n            //       named -- correctly, but for this shape only.)\n            //   (c) used inline (`if (c.f())`): no named local is ever\n            //       assigned, so no step carries the value at all.\n            //\n            // The _ESBMC_Nondet_Extcall_* symbols that ARE in the trace are the\n            // re-entry model's method-choice bits, not the returned value\n            // (measured: identical on two paths that disagree about it), so\n            // they are deliberately not reported here.\n            claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"extcall_returns_unavailable_reason\"] =\n              \"not implemented yet, and for three different reasons depending \"\n              \"on the syntactic shape the call's result arrives in; this field \"\n              \"does NOT say which one applies to this claim. (a) bound to a \"\n              \"named local, or assigned inside an approximated assembly block: \"\n              \"the value IS harvested and resolved, then dropped because the \"\n              \"classification has buckets only for parameters and environment \"\n              \"values and a call's return is a local. (b) low-level \"\n              \"`(bool ok, ) = a.call(...)`: get_nondet_symbol returns nil, so \"\n              \"the step is skipped before classification. (c) used inline, \"\n              \"`if (c.f())`: no named local is assigned, so no trace step \"\n              \"carries it. The _ESBMC_Nondet_Extcall_* symbols that ARE in the \"\n              \"trace are the re-entry model's method-choice bits, not the \"\n              \"returned value (measured: identical on two paths that disagree \"\n              \"about it), so they are deliberately not reported here. An empty \"\n              \"list means UNKNOWN, not 'this path performs no external call'\";\n          // Contract state this path STARTED from. Without it a path guarded by\n          // state an earlier transaction established cannot be replayed from\n          // the inputs alone.\n          json entry = json::object();\n          for (const auto &[n, v] : ce.entry_storage)\n            entry[prettify_solidity_expr(n)] = v;\n          claim_entry[\"entry_storage\"] = entry;\n          if (!ce.entry_storage_known)\n            // Never let an empty entry_storage be read as \"the contract started\n            // empty\": say that the marker was not observed instead.\n            claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"entry_storage_unavailable_reason\"] =\n              \"the entry marker for this path's function was not seen in the \"\n              \"trace, so the state it started from was not captured; an empty \"\n              \"entry_storage here means UNKNOWN, not 'no state'\";\n          // A custom-error revert in a scope the revert-observation gate does\n          // NOT cover (constructor / library / free function) is still modelled\n          // by ASSUME(false) with no rollback, so the harvested values are the\n          // state AT the revert, not the post-state — on-chain the transaction\n          // is undone and the post-state is the pre-call state. Publishing\n          // those under `final_state` would be a wrong value carrying a\n          // disclaimer; publish them under their true meaning instead and leave\n          // `final_state` empty, since the post-state is genuinely unavailable.\n          if (ce.revert_pre_rollback)\n          {\n            claim_entry[\"state_at_revert_point\"] = fin;\n            claim_entry[\"final_state\"] = json::object();\n          }\n          else\n            claim_entry[\"final_state\"] = fin;\n          // State this path WROTE but whose value is not renderable (mapping /\n          // dynamic-array stores). Listed so \"absent from final_state\" is never\n          // read as \"unchanged\".\n          if (!ce.state_written_unrendered.empty())\n          {\n            json un = json::array();\n            for (const auto &n : ce.state_written_unrendered)\n              un.push_back(prettify_solidity_expr(n));\n            claim_entry[\"state_written_value_unavailable\"] = un;\n          }\n          // Not silent: say how many nondet values were classified as harness\n          // plumbing and left out of `inputs`/`env`.\n          claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"harness_nondets_dropped\"] =\n            ce.dropped_internal;\n          // How the values were harvested. REQUIRED for the reader to\n          // interpret an empty final_state: with `sliced` true the symex\n          // slicer kept only what the path claim depends on — and a path\n          // claim's guard mentions only the ghost accumulators — so state\n          // writes are legitimately absent rather than non-existent. Re-run\n          // with --no-slice to obtain the post-state.\n          claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"sliced\"] = ce.sliced;\n          claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"payload_symbols_exempt_from_slicing\"] =\n            ce.payload_symbols_protected;\n          claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"compact_trace\"] = ce.compact_trace;\n          claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"scoped_to_claim\"] = ce.scoped_to_claim;\n          if (!ce.scoped_to_claim)\n            claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"post_state_may_include_later_tx\"] =\n              \"this path's own assert was not found in the trace, so the whole \"\n              \"trace was scanned; with more than one transaction the reported \"\n              \"post-state may belong to a later transaction\";\n          // A custom-error revert is modelled by ASSUME(false) in the error\n          // callee with NO state rollback, so the harvested post-state is the\n          // state at the revert point. On-chain the transaction reverts and\n          // every write is undone, i.e. the true post-state is the PRE-state.\n          // Say so rather than let a consumer read these values as the result.\n          if (ce.revert_pre_rollback)\n            claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"post_state_unavailable_reason\"] =\n              \"custom-error revert in a scope without rollback modelling \"\n              \"(constructor / library / free function): the harvested values \"\n              \"are published as `state_at_revert_point`, NOT as final_state. \"\n              \"The real post-state of a reverted transaction is the pre-call \"\n              \"state, which this model does not reconstruct\";\n          // Only meaningful when the payload symbols were NOT exempted: with\n          // the exemption in place an empty final_state means this path writes\n          // no state, and saying \"the writes were sliced away\" would be a\n          // wrong explanation of a correct result.\n          if (ce.sliced && !ce.payload_symbols_protected && fin.empty())\n            claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"final_state_unavailable_reason\"] =\n              \"slicing active and the payload symbols were not exempted: a \"\n              \"path claim depends only on the ghost path accumulators, so \"\n              \"contract state writes are sliced out of the counterexample. \"\n              \"Ask for --cov-report-json (which exempts them) or re-run with \"\n              \"--no-slice\";\n        }\n        else if (tri == \"F\")\n          // Witnessed, but not by THIS run: the cross-run covered-set already\n          // held it, so the path was not re-instrumented and no model was\n          // produced here. Without this the reader sees an F with no inputs and\n          // no post-state and cannot tell that from \"the CE was empty\".\n          claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"payload_absent_reason\"] =\n            \"path was already witnessed in an earlier round (covered-set) and \"\n            \"therefore not re-instrumented this run; its counterexample values \"\n            \"are in the report of the round that witnessed it\";\n      }\n      claims_json.push_back(claim_entry);\n    }\n\n    size_t total = all_claims.size();\n    size_t covered_count = 0;\n    for (const auto &c : claims_json)\n      // Path coverage reports the tri-state in `status`; \"F\" is its\n      // \"covered\" (a complete path with a counterexample in hand).\n      if (c[\"status\"] == \"covered\" || c[\"status\"] == \"F\")\n        covered_count++;\n\n    // For k-path coverage, restrict the summary to maximal goals so the\n    // JSON percentage matches the terminal spanning-set-filtered output.\n    // Individual claims keep their `feasibility` annotation so consumers\n    // that want raw counts can still derive them from the `claims` array.\n    if (is_k_path_cov)\n    {\n      total = 0;\n      covered_count = 0;\n      for (const auto &c : claims_json)\n        if (c[\"feasibility\"] == \"feasible\")\n        {\n          ++total;\n          if (c[\"status\"] == \"covered\")\n            ++covered_count;\n        }\n    }\n\n    json report;\n    report[\"coverage_type\"] = cov_type;\n    report[\"source_files\"] = json::array();\n    for (const auto &f : source_files)\n      report[\"source_files\"].push_back(f);\n    report[\"claims\"] = claims_json;\n    report[\"summary\"][\"total\"] = total;\n    report[\"summary\"][\"covered\"] = covered_count;\n    report[\"summary\"][\"uncovered\"] = total - covered_count;\n    report[\"summary\"][\"percentage\"] =\n      total > 0 ? covered_count * 100.0 / total : 0.0;\n    // For branch / branch-function modes: explicit \"no_branch\" marker when the\n    // source has zero branches. Key absent when total > 0 — consumers should\n    // read with default false. Not emitted for condition/assertion/k-path\n    // modes (their zero-claim case has different semantics).\n    if (total == 0 && (is_branch_cov || is_branch_func_cov))\n      report[\"summary\"][\"no_branch\"] = true;\n\n    // Path coverage: tri-state totals + the run's bound, so a consumer can\n    // see at a glance how many complete paths have a CE (F), how many are\n    // PROVEN unreachable (I, unbounded runs only), and how many are still\n    // open (U) — with `bounded_holds` counting the U's that held within this\n    // bound and are therefore worth re-checking unbounded.\n    if (is_path_cov)\n    {\n      size_t nF = 0, nI = 0, nU = 0, nBH = 0, nRevert = 0;\n      for (const auto &c : claims_json)\n      {\n        const std::string s = c[\"status\"];\n        if (s == \"F\")\n          ++nF;\n        else if (s == \"I\")\n          ++nI;\n        else\n          ++nU;\n        if (c.contains(\"bounded_holds\"))\n          ++nBH;\n        if (c.value(\"exit_kind\", \"\") == \"revert\")\n          ++nRevert;\n      }\n      report[\"summary\"][\"paths_total\"] = total;\n      report[\"summary\"][\"F_feasible_with_ce\"] = nF;\n      report[\"summary\"][\"I_proven_unreachable\"] = nI;\n      report[\"summary\"][\"U_undecided\"] = nU;\n      report[\"summary\"][\"U_of_which_bounded_holds\"] = nBH;\n\n      // ---- THE DECISION-SEQUENCE PUBLICATION, COUNTED ON STDOUT ----\n      //\n      // A mechanism whose only evidence is a field inside a file nobody reads\n      // has no evidence at all: this pass has already shipped one recorder that\n      // ran on every path and was consumed by nothing. Counting it here, from\n      // `claims_json` (i.e. from what was ACTUALLY emitted, not from what the\n      // producer believes it emitted), makes \"it fired\" and \"it fired on N\n      // things\" the same statement.\n      //\n      // `without` is printed even when it is zero, and it is the number that\n      // matters: an F carrying no sequence cannot be projected onto decisions,\n      // so it is a silent hole in any comparison built on this field.\n      {\n        size_t with = 0, without = 0, steps = 0, holes = 0, synth = 0;\n        for (const auto &c : claims_json)\n        {\n          if (c.value(\"status\", \"\") != \"F\")\n            continue;\n          if (!c.contains(\"decisions\"))\n          {\n            ++without;\n            continue;\n          }\n          ++with;\n          for (const auto &d : c[\"decisions\"])\n          {\n            ++steps;\n            if (d.contains(\"unrecorded_prefix_enc\"))\n              ++holes;\n            if (d.value(\"synthetic_abi_gate\", false))\n              ++synth;\n          }\n        }\n        report[\"summary\"][\"decision_sequences\"][\"paths_with\"] = with;\n        report[\"summary\"][\"decision_sequences\"][\"paths_without\"] = without;\n        report[\"summary\"][\"decision_sequences\"][\"decision_steps\"] = steps;\n        report[\"summary\"][\"decision_sequences\"][\"unrecorded_steps\"] = holes;\n        report[\"summary\"][\"decision_sequences\"][\"synthetic_abi_gate_steps\"] =\n          synth;\n        log_status(\n          \"--solidity-path-coverage: DECISION SEQUENCES published for {} of {} \"\n          \"witnessed path(s) ({} step(s), {} unrecorded, {} synthesised ABI \"\n          \"value gate). A path with no sequence cannot be projected onto \"\n          \"decisions, and the synthesised gate has no branch-coverage \"\n          \"counterpart, so both are named rather than folded in\",\n          with,\n          nF,\n          steps,\n          holes,\n          synth);\n      }\n      // Every U's reason, with all slots present including the zeros — the\n      // summary must never let a category vanish by simply not appearing.\n      {\n        json ur = json::object();\n        for (const auto &t : goto_coveraget::path_u_reason_tokens())\n          ur[t] = 0;\n        for (const auto &c : claims_json)\n          if (c.value(\"status\", \"\") == \"U\")\n          {\n            const std::string tok = c.value(\"u_reason\", \"\");\n            if (!tok.empty())\n              ur[tok] = ur[tok].get<size_t>() + 1;\n          }\n        report[\"summary\"][\"U_reasons\"] = ur;\n      }\n      report[\"summary\"][\"revert_exit_paths\"] = nRevert;\n      report[\"summary\"][\"bound\"][\"max_tx\"] = max_tx.empty() ? \"default\" : max_tx;\n      report[\"summary\"][\"bound\"][\"unwind\"] =\n        unwind_s.empty() ? \"default\" : unwind_s;\n      report[\"summary\"][\"bound\"][\"kind\"] =\n        unbounded_run ? \"unbounded\" : \"bounded\";\n      report[\"summary\"][\"bound\"][\"tx_exploration\"] = tx_exploration;\n      if (!unbounded_run)\n        report[\"summary\"][\"note\"] =\n          \"no coverage configuration can establish unreachability, so I is \"\n          \"never emitted and every path that merely held at this exploration \"\n          \"is reported as U with bounded_holds=true. In particular \"\n          \"--solidity-max-tx 0 is NOT an unbounded run: it emits the \"\n          \"`while (nondet) dispatch()` driver, whose back-edge Solidity \"\n          \"coverage then rewrites to a SKIP, leaving one guarded transaction \"\n          \"— strictly fewer than --solidity-max-tx 2. Use a larger \"\n          \"--solidity-max-tx N to explore deeper, not 0\";\n      // Known modelling limitation, stated rather than left for the reader to\n      // rediscover: the entry state of a transaction is whatever the\n      // constructor left behind. State variables are NOT havoc'd, so a path\n      // guarded by state that only a PRIOR transaction can establish (a\n      // balance, a role, an initialised flag) is unreachable at this\n      // transaction bound and lands in U — not because the path is dead, but\n      // because the run never built the state that unlocks it.
