Only the\n3071\t        // FIRST witness of a claim is recorded: one CE per complete path is\n3072\t        // what the report contracts for.\n3073\t        if (is_path_cov && witnesses.empty())\n3074\t        {\n3075\t          goto_coveraget::path_ce_t ce;\n3076\t          ce.sliced = !options.get_bool_option(\"no-slice\");\n3077\t          // Same condition the dispatch uses to set protect_ce_symbols: with\n3078\t          // the JSON requested, the payload symbols are exempt from slicing, so\n3079\t          // `sliced` alone must not be read as \"the payload was cut down\".\n3080\t          ce.payload_symbols_protected =\n3081\t            options.get_bool_option(\"cov-report-json\");\n3082\t          ce.compact_trace = is_compact_trace;\n3083\t          ce.revert_pre_rollback =\n3084\t            goto_coveraget::revert_paths.count(\n3085\t              {claim.claim_msg, claim.claim_loc}) > 0;\n3086\t          // Ordered so the emitted post-state is deterministic across runs.\n3087\t          std::map<std::string, std::string> last_state;\n3088\t          std::set<std::string> input_seen;\n3089\t          // Scope prefix this path's function parameters carry. A Solidity\n3090\t          // parameter symbol is `sol:@C@<contract>@F@<method>@<param>` (see\n3091\t          // foundry.h's parse_param_symbol), i.e. the method appears WITHOUT\n3092\t          // the `#N` disambiguator that the goto function id carries. So take\n3093\t          // claim_msg's function id (\"<function-id>:path:<enc>\") and drop the\n3094\t          // `#N` before using it as a prefix, or nothing would ever match.\n3095\t          std::string fn_scope;\n3096\t          // Contract scope prefix (`sol:@C@<Contract>@`). Mappings and dynamic\n3097\t          // arrays do NOT live inside the contract object: the frontend lowers\n3098\t          // them to CONTRACT-LEVEL global stores, whose ids carry this prefix\n3099\t          // WITHOUT the `@F@` function marker. That is what separates a state\n3100\t          // store from a function-scoped local.\n3101\t          std::string contract_scope;\n3102\t          // The goto function id, `#N` INTACT — that is the key\n3103\t          // path_entry_ghost is stored under, so it must not be truncated the\n3104\t          // way fn_scope is.\n3105\t          std::string fn_id_full;\n3106\t          {\n3107\t            const auto p = claim.claim_msg.rfind(\":path:\");\n3108\t            if (p != std::string::npos)\n3109\t            {\n3110\t              std::string fn_id = claim.claim_msg.substr(0, p);\n3111\t              fn_id_full = fn_id;\n3112\t              const auto fpos = fn_id.find(\"@F@\");\n3113\t              if (fpos != std::string::npos)\n3114\t                contract_scope = fn_id.substr(0, fpos + 1);\n3115\t              const auto hash = fn_id.find('#', fpos == std::string::npos\n3116\t                                                  ? 0\n3117\t                                                  : fpos + 3);\n3118\t              if (hash != std::string::npos)\n3119\t                fn_id.erase(hash);\n3120\t              fn_scope = fn_id + \"@\";\n3121\t            }\n3122\t          }\n3123\t          // Entry detection, using the SAME algorithm ESBMC already uses for\n3124\t          // `--show-funccall-trace` (goto_trace.cpp): every trace step carries\n3125\t          // the call stack at that point, innermost-first. Diff each step's\n3126\t          // stack against the previous one by common SUFFIX (the outermost end)\n3127\t          // and whatever remains at the front was pushed by this step. A new\n3128\t          // invocation of this path's function begins exactly when one of those\n3129\t          // newly-pushed frames is it.\n3130\t          //\n3131\t          // Two earlier attempts were wrong and are recorded so they are not\n3132\t          // retried. (1) The instrumentation's `tr = 1` is folded into the\n3133\t          // following `tr = tr*2 + guard`, so it never reaches the trace.\n3134\t          // (2) Comparing the location's BARE function name cannot tell one\n3135\t          // contract's `f` from another's, and cannot see a recursive or\n3136\t          // re-entrant call into the same function at all — it looks like\n3137\t          // execution never left. Stack frames carry the full goto function id,\n3138\t          // so both cases are exact.\n3139\t          //\n3140\t          // Steps with an EMPTY stack are skipped rather than treated as a\n3141\t          // reset: goto_trace.cpp documents that an empty stack means \"captured\n3142\t          // outside any function context\", not \"no frames on the stack\", and\n3143\t          // treating it as a reset re-emits the whole chain spuriously.\n3144\t          // Recursion makes \"the entry state\" ambiguous: with `f` nested three\n3145\t          // deep there are three different entry states, and the assert that\n3146\t          // the solver refuted belongs to exactly ONE of them. Measured on a\n3147\t          // path reachable only inside a recursive call, snapshotting on the\n3148\t          // most recent push reported the INNERMOST invocation's state, which\n3149\t          // was neither the outer nor the owning one.\n3150\t          //\n3151\t          // So key each snapshot by how many frames of this function were on\n3152\t          // the stack when it was taken, and at the end pick the depth the\n3153\t          // violated assert itself is at.\n3154\t          std::vector<stack_framet> prev_stack;\n3155\t          std::map<size_t, std::map<std::string, std::string>> entry_by_depth;\n3156\t          size_t prev_target_depth = 0;\n3157\t          size_t assert_target_depth = 0;\n3158\t          bool assert_depth_known = false;\n3159\t          auto count_target_frames =\n3160\t            [&fn_id_full](const std::vector<stack_framet> &s) {\n3161\t              size_t n = 0;\n3162\t              for (const auto &fr : s)\n3163\t                if (fr.function.as_string() == fn_id_full)\n3164\t                  ++n;\n3165\t              return n;\n3166\t            };\n3167\t          std::map<std::string, std::string> entry_snapshot;\n3168\t          // Base symbol id of a possibly-indexed lvalue (`m[k]` -> `m`).\n3169\t          auto base_sym_id = [](expr2tc e) -> std::string {\n3170\t            for (;;)\n3171\t            {\n3172\t              if (is_index2t(e))\n3173\t                e = to_index2t(e).source_value;\n3174\t              else if (is_member2t(e))\n3175\t                e = to_member2t(e).source_value;\n3176\t              else\n3177\t                break;\n3178\t            }\n3179\t            return is_symbol2t(e) ? to_symbol2t(e).thename.as_string()\n3180\t                                  : std::string();\n3181\t          };\n3182\t          std::set<std::string> unrendered_seen;\n3183\t          for (const auto &st : w.trace.steps)\n3184\t          {\n3185\t            // Stop at THIS path's own violated assert. The harness runs\n3186\t            // --solidity-max-tx transactions (default 2) and the trace spans\n3187\t            // all of them, so scanning past this point would let a LATER\n3188\t            // transaction's writes overwrite the post-state of the invocation\n3189\t            // that this path actually describes.\n3190\t            if (st.is_assert() && st.comment == claim.claim_msg)\n3191\t            {\n3192\t              ce.scoped_to_claim = true;\n3193\t              // Which invocation does the refuted assert belong to? Its own\n3194\t              // stack says so.\n3195\t              if (!st.stack_trace.empty())\n3196\t              {\n3197\t                assert_target_depth = count_target_frames(st.stack_trace);\n3198\t                assert_depth_known = assert_target_depth > 0;\n3199\t              }\n3200\t              break;\n3201\t            }\n3202\t            // Entry detection runs on EVERY step, not only assignments: the\n3203\t            // frame is pushed by the call instruction itself.\n3204\t            if (!st.stack_trace.empty())\n3205\t            {\n3206\t              const auto &cur = st.stack_trace;\n3207\t              size_t common = 0;\n3208\t              while (common < prev_stack.size() && common < cur.size() &&\n3209\t                     prev_stack[prev_stack.size() - 1 - common] ==\n3210\t                       cur[cur.size() - 1 - common])\n3211\t                ++common;\n3212\t              bool pushed_target = false;\n3213\t              for (size_t k = cur.size() - common; k-- > 0;)\n3214\t                if (cur[k].function.as_string() == fn_id_full)\n3215\t                {\n3216\t                  pushed_target = true;\n3217\t                  break;\n3218\t                }\n3219\t              const size_t d = count_target_frames(cur);\n3220\t              // Record only on an INCREASE, and only for the depth just\n3221\t              // reached: whatever state has accumulated is what that\n3222\t              // particular invocation started from.\n3223\t              if (pushed_target && d > prev_target_depth)\n3224\t                entry_by_depth[d] = last_state;\n3225\t              prev_target_depth = d;\n3226\t              prev_stack = cur;\n3227\t            }\n3228\t            if (!st.is_assignment())\n3229\t              continue;\n3230\t            if (is_nil_expr(st.lhs) || is_nil_expr(st.value))\n3231\t              continue;\n3232\t            // Diagnostic for the classification below: `--verbosity\n3233\t            // coverage:9` prints every assignment the harvest sees, with the\n3234\t            // things the classification keys on. Without it, an empty\n3235\t            // `inputs`/`entry_storage` is indistinguishable from a rule that\n3236\t            // silently never matches — which is exactly how the two bugs above\n3237\t            // (location-based extcall matching, `tr = 1` as entry marker) were\n3238\t            // found.\n3239\t            {\n3240\t              const expr2tc dnd = symex_slicet::get_nondet_symbol(st.rhs);\n3241\t              log_debug(\n3242\t                \"coverage\",\n3243\t                \"ce step: sym='{}' name='{}' fn='{}' nondet='{}'\",\n3244\t                is_symbol2t(st.lhs) ? to_symbol2t(st.lhs).thename.as_string()\n3245\t                                    : std::string(\"<not-a-symbol>\"),\n3246\t                from_expr(ns, \"\", st.lhs),\n3247\t                st.pc->location.get_function().as_string(),\n3248\t                (!is_nil_expr(dnd) && is_symbol2t(dnd))\n3249\t                  ? to_symbol2t(dnd).thename.as_string()\n3250\t                  : std::string(\"-\"));\n3251\t              std::string frames;\n3252\t              for (const auto &fr : st.stack_trace)\n3253\t                frames += (frames.empty() ? \"\" : \" < \") + fr.function.as_string();\n3254\t              log_debug(\n3255\t                \"coverage\",\n3256\t                \"   stack[{}]: {}\",\n3257\t                st.stack_trace.size(),\n3258\t                frames.empty() ? std::string(\"<empty>\") : frames);\n3259\t            }\n3260\t            const std::string name = from_expr(ns, \"\", st.lhs);\n3261\t            // NOT extcall_returns. The `_ESBMC_Nondet_Extcall_<C>` symbols are\n3262\t            // the RE-ENTRY model's own choice bits (which public method the\n3263\t            // outside world calls back into), not the value the external call\n3264\t            // returned to the contract. Measured: on the two paths of\n3265\t            // `if (ok)`, which by construction disagree about `ok`, these\n3266\t            // symbols carry the IDENTICAL tuple — so they cannot be `ok`.\n3267\t            // Publishing them under `extcall_returns` would be a wrong answer\n3268\t            // wearing the right label, so they stay counted as plumbing.\n3269\t            // See ce_extraction.extcall_returns_unavailable_reason below.\n3270\t            if (\n3271\t              is_symbol2t(st.lhs) &&\n3272\t              to_symbol2t(st.lhs).thename.as_string().find(\n3273\t                \"_ESBMC_Nondet_Extcall\") != std::string::npos)\n3274\t            {\n3275\t              ++ce.dropped_internal;\n3276\t              continue;\n3277\t            }\n3278\t            // Mapping / dynamic-array state: these do NOT live in the contract\n3279\t            // object, so the `this->` test below never sees them and they would\n3280\t            // be discarded as harness noise — leaving a reader to infer the\n3281\t            // mapping was untouched. Recognise them by their contract-level id\n3282\t            // and record them as state; when the model value is not a constant\n3283\t            // (an infinite-array store), record the NAME so the write is still\n3284\t            // visible rather than silently lost.\n3285\t            const std::string bid = base_sym_id(st.lhs);\n3286\t            if (\n3287\t              !contract_scope.empty() && bid.rfind(contract_scope, 0) == 0 &&\n3288\t              bid.find(\"@F@\") == std::string::npos)\n3289\t            {\n3290\t              // ESBMC's own contract-scope plumbing (address-binding tables,\n3291\t              // call temporaries) is not user state.\n3292\t              if (\n3293\t                name.rfind(\"$\", 0) == 0 ||\n3294\t                name.find(\"_bind_cname\") != std::string::npos ||\n3295\t                name.find(\"return_value$\") != std::string::npos)\n3296\t              {\n3297\t                ++ce.dropped_internal;\n3298\t                continue;\n3299\t              }\n3300\t              // A mapping/array element write (`m[k] = v`) yields a SCALAR\n3301\t              // model value — that is the useful post-state. The companion\n3302\t              // whole-store assignment (`m = with(m,k,v)`) yields the entire\n3303\t              // infinite array, which is the same information in a form no\n3304\t              // consumer can use and which would dwarf the report; name it as\n3305\t              // written-but-unrendered instead of dumping thousands of zeros.\n3306\t              // Only an ELEMENT write (`m[k] = v`) carries a usable post-state\n3307\t              // value. A bare whole-store assignment is the `with(...)` bulk\n3308\t              // form of the same update; recording it would print the entire\n3309\t              // infinite array — and its zero-initialised form reads as \"the\n3310\t              // mapping is empty\", contradicting the element entry beside it.\n3311\t              const bool scalar = is_index2t(st.lhs) &&\n3312\t                                  is_constant_expr(st.value) &&\n3313\t                                  !is_constant_array2t(st.value) &&\n3314\t                                  !is_constant_struct2t(st.value);\n3315\t              if (scalar)\n3316\t                last_state[name] = from_expr(ns, \"\", st.value);\n3317\t              else if (unrendered_seen.insert(name).second)\n3318\t                ce.state_written_unrendered.push_back(name);\n3319\t              continue;\n3320\t            }\n3321\t            // Never guess: a value that did not come back from the model as a\n3322\t            // constant is dropped rather than rendered symbolically.\n3323\t            if (!is_constant_expr(st.value))\n3324\t              continue;\n3325\t            // A Solidity state write `this->x = v` is lowered as a whole-object\n3326\t            // update, so the model hands back the ENTIRE contract struct.\n3327\t            // Project out the written member, otherwise every state variable\n3328\t            // would be reported as the same opaque object literal.\n3329\t            expr2tc val_expr = st.value;\n3330\t            if (is_member2t(st.lhs) && is_constant_struct2t(val_expr))\n3331\t            {\n3332\t              const irep_idt &mem = to_member2t(st.lhs).member;\n3333\t              const struct_type2t &sty = to_struct_type(val_expr->type);\n3334\t              for (size_t i = 0; i < sty.member_names.size(); ++i)\n3335\t                if (sty.member_names[i] == mem)\n3336\t                {\n3337\t                  val_expr = to_constant_struct2t(val_expr).datatype_members[i];\n3338\t                  break;\n3339\t                }\n3340\t            }\n3341\t            const std::string val = from_expr(ns, \"\", val_expr);\n3342\t            // WHOLE-OBJECT restore: require(cond) / revert(\"msg\") lower to a\n3343\t            // rollback block that assigns the entry snapshot back as ONE\n3344\t            // aggregate — `*this = _sol_save_this` — never per field. Tracking\n3345\t            // only `this->member` writes would miss it and report the\n3346\t            // pre-rollback value as the post-state, i.e. a WRONG value. Adopt\n3347\t            // every member of the restored object as the new post-state.\n3348\t            if (\n3349\t              name.rfind(\"*this\", 0) == 0 && is_constant_struct2t(st.value))\n3350\t            {\n3351\t              const struct_type2t &sty = to_struct_type(st.value->type);\n3352\t              const auto &mems = to_constant_struct2t(st.value).datatype_members;\n3353\t              for (size_t i = 0; i < sty.member_names.size() && i < mems.size();\n3354\t                   ++i)\n3355\t              {\n3356\t                const std::string mn = sty.member_names[i].as_string();\n3357\t                if (mn.empty() || mn[0] == '$' || mn.rfind(\"_ESBMC\", 0) == 0 ||\n3358\t                    mn.rfind(\"anon_pad\", 0) == 0)\n3359\t                  continue;\n3360\t                if (is_constant_expr(mems[i]))\n3361\t                  last_state[mn] = from_expr(ns, \"\", mems[i]);\n3362\t              }\n3363\t              continue;\n3364\t            }\n3365\t            if (name.find(\"this->\") != std::string::npos)\n3366\t            {\n3367\t              // Contract state variable: the LAST write on this path is the\n3368\t              // post-state this path produces. ESBMC's own bookkeeping fields\n3369\t              // on the contract object ($address/$code/$codehash/binding) are\n3370\t              // not user state and would only add noise.\n3371\t              const std::string bare = name.substr(name.rfind(\"->\") + 2);\n3372\t              if (!bare.empty() && bare[0] != '$' && bare.rfind(\"_ESBMC\", 0) != 0)\n3373\t                last_state[bare] = val;\n3374\t            }\n3375\t            else\n3376\t            {\n3377\t              // A nondet-sourced assignment is a value the harness CHOSE. But\n3378\t              // \"chosen by the harness\" is far broader than \"call argument\":\n3379\t              // it also covers the allocator tables, dispatcher choice bits and\n3380\t              // temporaries. Classify instead of dumping the whole bag, which\n3381\t              // would bury the one value a consumer needs (and bloat the report\n3382\t              // with multi-KB internal arrays).\n3383\t              const expr2tc nd = symex_slicet::get_nondet_symbol(st.rhs);\n3384\t              if (is_nil_expr(nd))\n3385\t                continue;\n3386\t              // A Solidity parameter/local carries the mangled id\n3387\t              // `sol:@C@<Contract>@F@<fn>#N@<name>`. Requiring the prefix to be\n3388\t              // THIS path's own function id keeps the call arguments of the\n3389\t              // unit under test and drops harness/dispatcher locals that merely\n3390\t              // share the shape (`_new_ts`, `addr`, `tmp`, ...).\n3391\t              std::string sym_id;\n3392\t              if (is_symbol2t(st.lhs))\n3393\t                sym_id = to_symbol2t(st.lhs).thename.as_string();\n3394\t              const bool in_fn_scope =\n3395\t                !fn_scope.empty() && sym_id.rfind(fn_scope, 0) == 0;\n3396\t              // A prefix match says \"declared inside this function\", which is\n3397\t              // true of a PARAMETER and of every local alike. Before this, an external call's return\n3400\t              // value (a local) was reported under `inputs`, i.e. as an\n3401\t              // argument a generated test could pass — it cannot.\n3402\t              bool is_param = false;\n3403\t              if (in_fn_scope && !sym_id.empty())\n3404\t              {\n3405\t                const symbolt *psym = ns.lookup(irep_idt(sym_id));\n3406\t                is_param = psym && psym->is_parameter;\n3407\t              }\n3408\t              // ⚠ This used to read \"external-call returns were already taken\n3409\t              // above, before the contract-scope-store branch could discard\n3410\t              // them\". No such code exists anywhere -- ce.extcall_returns has a\n3411\t              // declaration, three readers and ZERO writers -- so the comment\n3412\t              // asserted a step that had never been written. It cost a session:\n3413\t              // the empty field was read as \"the harvest cannot see the value\",\n3414\t              // when in fact the value arrives here resolved and falls off the\n3415\t              // end of the classification below for want of a bucket.\n3416\t              // A comment claiming a step that does not exist is worse than no\n3417\t              // comment, because it redirects the next reader away from the\n3418\t              // line that actually drops the value.\n3419\t              const bool is_env = name.rfind(\"msg_\", 0) == 0 ||\n3420\t ++ce.dropped_internal;\n3434\t            }\n3435\t          }\n3436\t          for (const auto &[n, v] : last_state)\n3437\t            ce.final_state.emplace_back(n, v);\n3438\t          // Pick the ce.entry_storage_known = true;\n3449\t            }\n3450\t          }\n3451\t          for (const auto &[n, v] : entry_snapshot)\n3452\t            ce.entry_storage.emplace_back(n, v);\n3453\t 'U' : 'F';\n      else if (solver_result == smt_convt::P_UNSATISFIABLE)\n        verdict = 'P';\n      else\n        verdict = 'U';\n      std::lock_guard lock(goto_coveraget::claim_outcome_mutex);\n      // 'F' is final: a witness stays valid, so a later phase's failure to\n      // reprove must never downgrade it.\n      auto it_o = goto_coveraget::claim_outcome.find(claim_sig);\n      if (it_o == goto_coveraget::claim_outcome.end())\n        goto_coveraget::claim_outcome.emplace(claim_sig, verdict);\n      else if (it_o->second != 'F')\n        it_o->second = verdict;\n    }\n\n    double solve_time_s = (solve_stop - solve_start);\n\n    // Atomically update summary with timing and results\n    double old_total_time_s = summary.total_time_s;\n    double new_total_time_s;\n    do\n    {\n      new_total_time_s = old_total_time_s + solve_time_s;\n    } while (!summary.total_time_s.compare_exchange_weak(\n      old_total_time_s, new_total_time_s));\n\n    if (solver_result == smt_convt::P_SATISFIABLE)\n    {\n      if (is)\n        summary.unknown_properties++;\n      else\n        summary.failed_properties++;\n    }\n    else if (solver_result == smt_convt::P_UNSATISFIABLE)\n      summary.passed_properties++;\n\n    // If an assertion instance is verified to be violated\n    if (solver_result == smt_convt::P_SATISFIABLE)\n    {\n      // Inductive step SAT means unprovable (UNKNOWN), not a real\n      // counterexample — skip trace generation and return early.\n      if (is)\n      {\n        std::lock_guard lock(result_mutex);\n        final_result = solver_result;\n        return;\n      }\n\n      bool is_compact_trace = true;\n      if (\n        options.get_bool_option(\"no-slice\") &&\n        !options.get_bool_option(\"compact-trace\"))\n        is_compact_trace = false;\n      // The path-coverage CE payload is harvested from THIS trace. A compact\n      // trace drops every step flagged `hidden`, and that is exactly where the\n      // EVM environment (msg./tx./block.) and the harness-side writes are\n      // assigned — the report's `env` block would come back empty even though\n      // the values are in the model. Building the full trace changes nothing\n      // about what is solved; it only costs trace-construction time.\n      if (is_path_cov && options.get_bool_option(\"cov-report-json\"))\n        is_compact_trace = false;\n\n      // --all-witnesses: re-solve with blocking clauses on the nondet input\n      // tuple to enumerate further violating inputs at the current k.\n      // No re-encoding: we only push extra assertions onto the live solver.\n      const bool enumerate = options.get_bool_option(\"all-witnesses\");\n      size_t max_w = 1;\n      if (enumerate)\n      {\n        const std::string mw = options.get_option(\"max-witnesses\");\n        const int mw_val = mw.empty() ? 16 : std::stoi(mw);\n        // 0 means unlimited (only meaningful with --all-witnesses).\n        max_w = (mw_val == 0) ? SIZE_MAX : (size_t)mw_val;\n      }\n\n      std::vector<witness_recordt> witnesses;\n      enumeration_stop_reasont stop_reason =\n        enumerate ? enumeration_stop_reasont::Unsat\n                  : enumeration_stop_reasont::Disabled;\n\n      // Cache option lookups so the per-witness loop body is cheap.\n      const std::string cex_output = options.get_option(\"cex-output\");\n      const std::string graphml_path =\n        options.get_option(\"witness-output-graphml\");\n      const std::string yaml_path = options.get_option(\"witness-output-yaml\");\n      const bool want_graphml = !graphml_path.empty();\n      const bool want_yaml = !yaml_path.empty();\n      const bool want_testcase = options.get_bool_option(\"generate-testcase\");\n      const bool want_html = options.get_bool_option(\"generate-html-report\");\n      const bool want_json = options.get_bool_option(\"generate-json-report\");\n      const bool want_pytest =\n        options.get_bool_option(\"generate-pytest-testcase\");\n      const bool want_ctest =\n        options.get_bool_option(\"generate-ctest-testcase\");\n      const bool want_foundry =\n        options.get_bool_option(\"generate-foundry-testcase\");\n\n      // Emit testcase metadata once per claim (not once per witness).\n      if (want_testcase)\n        generate_testcase_metadata();\n\n      // Drive enumeration with a separate variable so the original SAT\n      // outcome stays in `solver_result` for downstream bookkeeping\n      // (final_result, fail-fast counter, claim cleanup).\n      smt_convt::resultt enum_result = solver_result;\n      bool ctx_pushed = false;\n      while (enum_result == smt_convt::P_SATISFIABLE)\n      {\n        witness_recordt w;\n        build_goto_trace(local_eq, *solver_ptr, w.trace, is_compact_trace);\n        // Collecting nondet values walks every SSA step and queries the\n        // solver model per nondet symbol — non-trivial on coverage runs\n        // with many claims and large arrays. Skip it when we don't need\n        // it: the values are only consumed by `make_blocking_expr` (only\n        // when enumerating) and by the multi-witness pretty-printer\n        // (only when --all-witnesses is set, i.e. enumerate==true).\n        // The legacy single-witness renderer does not use them.\n        if (enumerate)\n          w.nondet_inputs = collect_nondet_values(local_eq, *solver_ptr);\n        w.ce_index = ce_counter++;\n\n        // Emit machine-readable artifacts NOW, while this witness's solver\n        // model is still live. After the next dec_solve(), the model is\n        // either gone (UNSAT) or replaced by the next witness's values.\n        if (!cex_output.empty())\n        {\n          std::ofstream out(fmt::format(\"{}-{}\", w.ce_index, cex_output));\n          show_goto_trace(out, ns, w.trace);\n        }\n        // For graphml/yaml the writer reads the path from `options`;\n        // override per-witness so multiple witnesses don't overwrite the\n        // same file (and so it's safe under --parallel-solving).\n        if (want_graphml)\n          violation_graphml_goto_trace(\n            options,\n            ns,\n            w.trace,\n            fmt::format(\"{}-{}\", w.ce_index, graphml_path));\n        if (want_yaml)\n          violation_yaml_goto_trace(\n            options, ns, w.trace, fmt::format(\"{}-{}\", w.ce_index, yaml_path));\n        if (want_testcase)\n          generate_testcase(\n            \"testcase-\" + std::to_string(w.ce_index) + \".xml\",\n            local_eq,\n            *solver_ptr);\n        if (want_html)\n          generate_html_report(\n            std::to_string(w.ce_index), ns, w.trace, options);\n        if (want_json)\n          generate_json_report(std::to_string(w.ce_index), ns, w.trace);\n        if (want_pytest)\n          pytest_gen.collect(local_eq, *solver_ptr);\n        if (want_ctest)\n          ctest_gen.collect(local_eq, *solver_ptr, ns);\n        if (want_foundry)\n          // Collect into the external strategy-level generator when threaded\n          // (--k-induction), else the owned member (plain BMC).\n          foundry().collect(local_eq, *solver_ptr, ns);\n\n        // Solidity complete-path coverage: harvest this path's CE payload\n        // (concrete inputs + post-state) NOW, while this witness's solver\n        // model is live — after the next dec_solve() it is gone. Only the\n        // FIRST witness of a claim is recorded: one CE per complete path is\n        // what the report contracts for.\n        if (is_path_cov && witnesses.empty())\n        {\n          goto_coveraget::path_ce_t ce;\n          ce.sliced = !options.get_bool_option(\"no-slice\");\n          // Same condition the dispatch uses to set protect_ce_symbols: with\n          // the JSON requested, the payload symbols are exempt from slicing, so\n          // `sliced` alone must not be read as \"the payload was cut down\".\n          ce.payload_symbols_protected =\n            options.get_bool_option(\"cov-report-json\");\n          ce.compact_trace = is_compact_trace;\n          ce.revert_pre_rollback =\n            goto_coveraget::revert_paths.count(\n              {claim.claim_msg, claim.claim_loc}) > 0;\n          // Ordered so the emitted post-state is deterministic across runs.\n          std::map<std::string, std::string> last_state;\n          std::set<std::string> input_seen;\n          // Scope prefix this path's function parameters carry. A Solidity\n          // parameter symbol is `sol:@C@<contract>@F@<method>@<param>` (see\n          // foundry.h's parse_param_symbol), i.e. the method appears WITHOUT\n          // the `#N` disambiguator that the goto function id carries. So take\n          // claim_msg's function id (\"<function-id>:path:<enc>\") and drop the\n          // `#N` before using it as a prefix, or nothing would ever match.\n          std::string fn_scope;\n          // Contract scope prefix (`sol:@C@<Contract>@`). Mappings and dynamic\n          // arrays do NOT live inside the contract object: the frontend lowers\n          // them to CONTRACT-LEVEL global stores, whose ids carry this prefix\n          // WITHOUT the `@F@` function marker. That is what separates a state\n          // store from a function-scoped local.\n          std::string contract_scope;\n          // The goto function id, `#N` INTACT — that is the key\n          // path_entry_ghost is stored under, so it must not be truncated the\n          // way fn_scope is.\n          std::string fn_id_full;\n          {\n            const auto p = claim.claim_msg.rfind(\":path:\");\n            if (p != std::string::npos)\n            {\n              std::string fn_id = claim.claim_msg.substr(0, p);\n              fn_id_full = fn_id;\n              const auto fpos = fn_id.find(\"@F@\");\n              if (fpos != std::string::npos)\n                contract_scope = fn_id.substr(0, fpos + 1);\n              const auto hash = fn_id.find('#', fpos == std::string::npos\n                                                  ? 0\n                                                  : fpos + 3);\n              if (hash != std::string::npos)\n                fn_id.erase(hash);\n              fn_scope = fn_id + \"@\";\n            }\n          }\n          // Entry detection, using the SAME algorithm ESBMC already uses for\n          // `--show-funccall-trace` (goto_trace.cpp): every trace step carries\n          // the call stack at that point, innermost-first. Diff each step's\n          // stack against the previous one by common SUFFIX (the outermost end)\n          // and whatever remains at the front was pushed by this step. A new\n          // invocation of this path's function begins exactly when one of those\n          // newly-pushed frames is it.\n          //\n          // Two earlier attempts were wrong and are recorded so they are not\n          // retried. (1) The instrumentation's `tr = 1` is folded into the\n          // following `tr = tr*2 + guard`, so it never reaches the trace.\n          // (2) Comparing the location's BARE function name cannot tell one\n          // contract's `f` from another's, and cannot see a recursive or\n          // re-entrant call into the same function at all — it looks like\n          // execution never left. Stack frames carry the full goto function id,\n          // so both cases are exact.\n          //\n          // Steps with an EMPTY stack are skipped rather than treated as a\n          // reset: goto_trace.cpp documents that an empty stack means \"captured\n          // outside any function context\", not \"no frames on the stack\", and\n          // treating it as a reset re-emits the whole chain spuriously.\n          // Recursion makes \"the entry state\" ambiguous: with `f` nested three\n          // deep there are three different entry states, and the assert that\n          // the solver refuted belongs to exactly ONE of them. Measured on a\n          // path reachable only inside a recursive call, snapshotting on the\n          // most recent push reported the INNERMOST invocation's state, which\n          // was neither the outer nor the owning one.\n          //\n          // So key each snapshot by how many frames of this function were on\n          // the stack when it was taken, and at the end pick the depth the\n          // violated assert itself is at.\n          std::vector<stack_framet> prev_stack;\n          std::map<size_t, std::map<std::string, std::string>> entry_by_depth;\n          size_t prev_target_depth = 0;\n          size_t assert_target_depth = 0;\n          bool assert_depth_known = false;\n          auto count_target_frames =\n            [&fn_id_full](const std::vector<stack_framet> &s) {\n              size_t n = 0;\n              for (const auto &fr : s)\n                if (fr.function.as_string() == fn_id_full)\n                  ++n;\n              return n;\n            };\n          std::map<std::string, std::string> entry_snapshot;\n          // Base symbol id of a possibly-indexed lvalue (`m[k]` -> `m`).\n          auto base_sym_id = [](expr2tc e) -> std::string {\n            for (;;)\n            {\n              if (is_index2t(e))\n                e = to_index2t(e).source_value;\n              else if (is_member2t(e))\n                e = to_member2t(e).source_value;\n              else\n                break;\n            }\n            return is_symbol2t(e) ? to_symbol2t(e).thename.as_string()\n                                  : std::string();\n          };\n          std::set<std::string> unrendered_seen;\n          for (const auto &st : w.trace.steps)\n          {\n            // Stop at THIS path's own violated assert. The harness runs\n            // --solidity-max-tx transactions (default 2) and the trace spans\n            // all of them, so scanning past this point would let a LATER\n            // transaction's writes overwrite the post-state of the invocation\n            // that this path actually describes.\n            if (st.is_assert() && st.comment == claim.claim_msg)\n            {\n              ce.scoped_to_claim = true;\n              // Which invocation does the refuted assert belong to? Its own\n              // stack says so.\n              if (!st.stack_trace.empty())\n              {\n                assert_target_depth = count_target_frames(st.stack_trace);\n                assert_depth_known = assert_target_depth > 0;\n              }\n              break;\n            }\n            // Entry detection runs on EVERY step, not only assignments: the\n            // frame is pushed by the call instruction itself.\n            if (!st.stack_trace.empty())\n            {\n              const auto &cur = st.stack_trace;\n              size_t common = 0;\n              while (common < prev_stack.size() && common < cur.size() &&\n                     prev_stack[prev_stack.size() - 1 - common] ==\n                       cur[cur.size() - 1 - common])\n                ++common;\n              bool pushed_target = false;\n              for (size_t k = cur.size() - common; k-- > 0;)\n                if (cur[k].function.as_string() == fn_id_full)\n                {\n                  pushed_target = true;\n                  break;\n                }\n              const size_t d = count_target_frames(cur);\n              // Record only on an INCREASE, and only for the depth just\n              // reached: whatever state has accumulated is what that\n              // particular invocation started from.\n              if (pushed_target && d > prev_target_depth)\n                entry_by_depth[d] = last_state;\n              prev_target_depth = d;\n              prev_stack = cur;\n            }\n            if (!st.is_assignment())\n              continue;\n            if (is_nil_expr(st.lhs) || is_nil_expr(st.value))\n              continue;\n            // Diagnostic for the classification below: `--verbosity\n            // coverage:9` prints every assignment the harvest sees, with the\n            // things the classification keys on. Without it, an empty\n            // `inputs`/`entry_storage` is indistinguishable from a rule that\n            // silently never matches — which is exactly how the two bugs above\n            // (location-based extcall matching, `tr = 1` as entry marker) were\n            // found.\n            {\n              const expr2tc dnd = symex_slicet::get_nondet_symbol(st.rhs);\n              log_debug(\n                \"coverage\",\n                \"ce step: sym='{}' name='{}' fn='{}' nondet='{}'\",\n                is_symbol2t(st.lhs) ? to_symbol2t(st.lhs).thename.as_string()\n                                    : std::string(\"<not-a-symbol>\"),\n                from_expr(ns, \"\", st.lhs),\n                st.pc->location.get_function().as_string(),\n                (!is_nil_expr(dnd) && is_symbol2t(dnd))\n                  ? to_symbol2t(dnd).thename.as_string()\n                  : std::string(\"-\"));\n              std::string frames;\n              for (const auto &fr : st.stack_trace)\n                frames += (frames.empty() ? \"\" : \" < \") + fr.function.as_string();\n              log_debug(\n                \"coverage\",\n                \"   stack[{}]: {}\",\n                st.stack_trace.size(),\n                frames.empty() ? std::string(\"<empty>\") : frames);\n            }\n            const std::string name = from_expr(ns, \"\", st.lhs);\n            // NOT extcall_returns. The `_ESBMC_Nondet_Extcall_<C>` symbols are\n            // the RE-ENTRY model's own choice bits (which public method the\n            // outside world calls back into), not the value the external call\n            // returned to the contract. Measured: on the two paths of\n            // `if (ok)`, which by construction disagree about `ok`, these\n            // symbols carry the IDENTICAL tuple — so they cannot be `ok`.\n            // Publishing them under `extcall_returns` would be a wrong answer\n            // wearing the right label, so they stay counted as plumbing.\n            // See ce_extraction.extcall_returns_unavailable_reason below.\n            if (\n              is_symbol2t(st.lhs) &&\n              to_symbol2t(st.lhs).thename.as_string().find(\n                \"_ESBMC_Nondet_Extcall\") != std::string::npos)\n            {\n              ++ce.dropped_internal;\n              continue;\n            }\n            // Mapping / dynamic-array state: these do NOT live in the contract\n            // object, so the `this->` test below never sees them and they would\n            // be discarded as harness noise — leaving a reader to infer the\n            // mapping was untouched. Recognise them by their contract-level id\n            // and record them as state; when the model value is not a constant\n            // (an infinite-array store), record the NAME so the write is still\n            // visible rather than silently lost.\n            const std::string bid = base_sym_id(st.lhs);\n            if (\n              !contract_scope.empty() && bid.rfind(contract_scope, 0) == 0 &&\n              bid.find(\"@F@\") == std::string::npos)\n            {\n              // ESBMC's own contract-scope plumbing (address-binding tables,\n              // call temporaries) is not user state.\n              if (\n                name.rfind(\"$\", 0) == 0 ||\n                name.find(\"_bind_cname\") != std::string::npos ||\n                name.find(\"return_value$\") != std::string::npos)\n              {\n                ++ce.dropped_internal;\n                continue;\n              }\n              // A mapping/array element write (`m[k] = v`) yields a SCALAR\n              // model value — that is the useful post-state. The companion\n              // whole-store assignment (`m = with(m,k,v)`) yields the entire\n              // infinite array, which is the same information in a form no\n              // consumer can use and which would dwarf the report; name it as\n              // written-but-unrendered instead of dumping thousands of zeros.\n              // Only an ELEMENT write (`m[k] = v`) carries a usable post-state\n              // value. A bare whole-store assignment is the `with(...)` bulk\n              // form of the same update; recording it would print the entire\n              // infinite array — and its zero-initialised form reads as \"the\n              // mapping is empty\", contradicting the element entry beside it.\n              const bool scalar = is_index2t(st.lhs) &&\n                                  is_constant_expr(st.value) &&\n                                  !is_constant_array2t(st.value) &&\n                                  !is_constant_struct2t(st.value);\n              if (scalar)\n                last_state[name] = from_expr(ns, \"\", st.value);\n              else if (unrendered_seen.insert(name).second)\n                ce.state_written_unrendered.push_back(name);\n              continue;\n            }\n            // Never guess: a value that did not come back from the model as a\n            // constant is dropped rather than rendered symbolically.\n            if (!is_constant_expr(st.value))\n              continue;\n            // A Solidity state write `this->x = v` is lowered as a whole-object\n            // update, so the model hands back the ENTIRE contract struct.\n            // Project out the written member, otherwise every state variable\n            // would be reported as the same opaque object literal.\n            expr2tc val_expr = st.value;\n            if (is_member2t(st.lhs) && is_constant_struct2t(val_expr))\n            {\n              const irep_idt &mem = to_member2t(st.lhs).member;\n              const struct_type2t &sty = to_struct_type(val_expr->type);\n              for (size_t i = 0; i < sty.member_names.size(); ++i)\n                if (sty.member_names[i] == mem)\n                {\n                  val_expr = to_constant_struct2t(val_expr).datatype_members[i];\n                  break;\n                }\n            }\n            const std::string val = from_expr(ns, \"\", val_expr);\n            // WHOLE-OBJECT restore: require(cond) / revert(\"msg\") lower to a\n            // rollback block that assigns the entry snapshot back as ONE\n            // aggregate — `*this = _sol_save_this` — never per field. Tracking\n            // only `this->member` writes would miss it and report the\n            // pre-rollback value as the post-state, i.e. a WRONG value. Adopt\n            // every member of the restored object as the new post-state.\n            if (\n              name.rfind(\"*this\", 0) == 0 && is_constant_struct2t(st.value))\n            {\n              const struct_type2t &sty = to_struct_type(st.value->type);\n              const auto &mems = to_constant_struct2t(st.value).datatype_members;\n              for (size_t i = 0; i < sty.member_names.size() && i < mems.size();\n                   ++i)\n              {\n                const std::string mn = sty.member_names[i].as_string();\n                if (mn.empty() || mn[0] == '$' || mn.rfind(\"_ESBMC\", 0) == 0 ||\n                    mn.rfind(\"anon_pad\", 0) == 0)\n                  continue;\n                if (is_constant_expr(mems[i]))\n                  last_state[mn] = from_expr(ns, \"\", mems[i]);\n              }\n              continue;\n            }\n            if (name.find(\"this->\") != std::string::npos)\n            {\n              // Contract state variable: the LAST write on this path is the\n              // post-state this path produces. ESBMC's own bookkeeping fields\n              // on the contract object ($address/$code/$codehash/binding) are\n              // not user state and would only add noise.\n              const std::string bare = name.substr(name.rfind(\"->\") + 2);\n              if (!bare.empty() && bare[0] != '$' && bare.rfind(\"_ESBMC\", 0) != 0)\n                last_state[bare] = val;\n            }\n            else\n            {\n              // A nondet-sourced assignment is a value the harness CHOSE. But\n              // \"chosen by the harness\" is far broader than \"call argument\":\n              // it also covers the allocator tables, dispatcher choice bits and\n              // temporaries. Classify instead of dumping the whole bag, which\n              // would bury the one value a consumer needs (and bloat the report\n              // with multi-KB internal arrays).\n              const expr2tc nd = symex_slicet::get_nondet_symbol(st.rhs);\n              if (is_nil_expr(nd))\n                continue;\n              // A Solidity parameter/local carries the mangled id\n              // `sol:@C@<Contract>@F@<fn>#N@<name>`. Requiring the prefix to be\n              // THIS path's own function id keeps the call arguments of the\n              // unit under test and drops harness/dispatcher locals that merely\n              // share the shape (`_new_ts`, `addr`, `tmp`, ...).\n              std::string sym_id;\n              if (is_symbol2t(st.lhs))\n                sym_id = to_symbol2t(st.lhs).thename.as_string();\n              const bool in_fn_scope =\n                !fn_scope.empty() && sym_id.rfind(fn_scope, 0) == 0;\n              // A prefix match says \"declared inside this function\", which is\n              // true of a PARAMETER and of every local alike. Only a parameter\n              // is something the caller supplies, so ask the symbol table\n              // instead of the name. Before this, an external call's return\n              // value (a local) was reported under `inputs`, i.e. as an\n              // argument a generated test could pass — it cannot.\n              bool is_param = false;\n              if (in_fn_scope && !sym_id.empty())\n              {\n                const symbolt *psym = ns.lookup(irep_idt(sym_id));\n                is_param = psym && psym->is_parameter;\n              }\n              // ⚠ This used to read \"external-call returns were already taken\n              // above, before the contract-scope-store branch could discard\n              // them\". No such code exists anywhere -- ce.extcall_returns has a\n              // declaration, three readers and ZERO writers -- so the comment\n              // asserted a step that had never been written. It cost a session:\n              // the empty field was read as \"the harvest cannot see the value\",\n              // when in fact the value arrives here resolved and falls off the\n              // end of the classification below for want of a bucket.\n              // A comment claiming a step that does not exist is worse than no\n              // comment, because it redirects the next reader away from the\n              // line that actually drops the value.\n              const bool is_env = name.rfind(\"msg_\", 0) == 0 ||\n                                  name.rfind(\"tx_\", 0) == 0 ||\n                                  name.rfind(\"block_\", 0) == 0;\n              if (is_param)\n              {\n                if (input_seen.insert(name).second)\n                  ce.inputs.emplace_back(name, val);\n              }\n              else if (is_env)\n              {\n                if (input_seen.insert(name).second)\n                  ce.env.emplace_back(name, val);\n              }\n              else\n                ++ce.dropped_internal;\n            }\n          }\n          for (const auto &[n, v] : last_state)\n            ce.final_state.emplace_back(n, v);\n          // Pick the snapshot for the invocation the refuted assert sits in.\n          // Anything else would be a different invocation's entry state, which\n          // for a recursive function is a different number — reporting it would\n          // be a wrong value, not an approximate one.\n          if (assert_depth_known)\n          {\n            auto ed = entry_by_depth.find(assert_target_depth);\n            if (ed != entry_by_depth.end())\n            {\n              entry_snapshot = ed->second;\n              ce.entry_storage_known = true;\n            }\n          }\n          for (const auto &[n, v] : entry_snapshot)\n            ce.entry_storage.emplace_back(n, v);\n          std::lock_guard lock(goto_coveraget::claim_outcome_mutex);\n          goto_coveraget::path_ce[claim_sig] = std::move(ce);\n        }\n\n        witnesses.push_back(std::move(w));\n\n        if (!enumerate)\n          break;\n        if (witnesses.size() >= max_w)\n nothing meaningful to block. Mark the reason so the user\n        // doesn't read \"UNSAT\" as \"exhaustive\".\n        if (witnesses.back().nondet_inputs.empty())\n        {\n          stop_reason = enumeration_stop_reasont::NoInputs;\n          break;\n        }\n\n        // Open a single SMT context frame the first time we add a blocking\n        // clause. Every subsequent blocking clause goes into the same frame;\n        // the matching pop_ctx() after the loop drops them all in one shot.\n        // This keeps the feature safe under --smt-during-symex, where\n        // solver_ptr aliases the shared runtime_solver: blocking clauses\n        // asserted while enumerating claim A cannot leak into claim B.\n        // (Push must come *after* the first model read — bitwuzla and other\n        // backends invalidate the current model on push.)\n        if (!ctx_pushed)\n        {\n          solver_ptr->push_ctx();\n          ctx_pushed = true;\n        }\n\n        // Block this input tuple and re-solve on the same instance.\n        expr2tc block = make_blocking_expr(witnesses.back().nondet_inputs);\n        solver_ptr->assert_expr(block);\n        enum_result = solver_ptr->dec_solve();\n      }\n\n      // dec_solve() can return P_ERROR / P_SMTLIB; in that case the witness\n      // set is *not* exhaustive — flag it explicitly.\n      if (\n        stop_reason == enumeration_stop_reasont::Unsat &&\n        enum_result != smt_convt::P_UNSATISFIABLE &&\n        enum_result != smt_convt::P_SATISFIABLE)\n        stop_reason = enumeration_stop_reasont::Error;\n\n      // Drop every blocking clause we asserted; the next claim's solve\n      // sees the solver in its pre-enumeration state.\n      if (ctx_pushed)\n        solver_ptr->pop_ctx();\n\n      // Store claim signature (once — multiple witnesses are still one claim)\n      if (is_assert_cov)\n      {\n        std::lock_guard lock(reached_mul_claims_mutex);\n        reached_mul_claims.emplace(claim_sig);\n      }\n      else\n      {\n        std::lock_guard lock(reached_claims_mutex);\n        if (is_goto_cov)\n          reached_claims.emplace(claim_sig);\n        else\n          reached_claims.emplace(claim.claim_cstr);\n        // Item 2e: persist this newly-witnessed branch edge immediately\n        // and atomically, so a mid-run kill (the heavy --coverage-whole-\n        // unit case dies in-solve before report_coverage) still saves\n        // partial progress and bounded re-runs accumulate monotonically.\n        // Branch coverage only; key == Item 2's (claim_msg, claim_loc);\n        // under the same mutex as reached_claims.\n        // Solidity complete-path coverage uses the SAME cross-run covered-set\n        // so an escalation round (tx=1 -> 2 -> 3) does not re-instrument a\n        // path whose CE is already in hand; its key is the same\n        // (claim_msg, claim_loc) pair, where claim_msg is the \"fn:path:enc\"\n        // comment, unique per complete path.\n        // Complete-path coverage persists through the CONTENT-ADDRESSED writer\n        // instead: its key is the stable id, and `covered_set` is empty for\n        // this metric by construction. Incremental (not just at run end) for\n        // the same reason as branch coverage — a mid-solve kill on a large\n        // contract must not throw away the paths already witnessed.\n        if (is_path_cov && !goto_coveraget::path_covered_outpath.empty())\n          goto_coveraget::write_path_covered_set_atomic();\n        if (\n          is_branch_cov && !goto_coveraget::covered_set_outpath.empty() &&\n          goto_coveraget::covered_set.emplace(claim.claim_msg, claim.claim_loc)\n            .second)\n        {\n          goto_coveraget::write_covered_set_atomic();\n          // \"data even on UNKNOWN\", covered-set-mode numerator: one\n          // more universe edge witnessed+persisted this run. Path coverage already prints per-claim progress through the\n      // PASSED/FAILED lines above.\n      if (is_vb && !is_path_cov)\n        report_coverage_verbose(\n          claim,\n          claim_sig,\n          is_assert_cov,\n          is_cond_cov,\n          is_branch_cov,\n          is_branch_func_cov,\n          reached_claims,\n          reached_mul_claims);\n      else if (!is_cov_silent)\n      {\n        report_multi_property_trace(\n          smt_convt::P_SATISFIABLE, witnesses, stop_reason, claim.claim_msg);\n      }\n\n      {\n        std::lock_guard lock(result_mutex);\n        final_result = solver_result;\n      }\n\n      // Update fail-fast-counter\n      fail_fast_cnt++;\n\n      // for kind && incr: remove verified claims\n      // whenever we find a property violation, we remove the claim\n      if (!is_keep_verified && (bs || fc || is))\n      {\n        clear_verified_claims_in_ssa(local_eq, claim, is_goto_cov);\n        clear_verified_claims_in_goto(claim, is_goto_cov);\n      }\n    }\n    else if (solver_result == smt_convt::P_UNSATISFIABLE)\n      // for kind && incr: remove verified claims\n      // when we find a property proven correct in\n      // either forward condition or inductive step\n      if (!is_keep_verified && !bs)\n      {\n        clear_verified_claims_in_ssa(local_eq, claim, is_goto_cov);\n        clear_verified_claims_in_goto(claim, is_goto_cov);\n      }\n  };\n\n  // PARALLEL\n  if (options.get_bool_option(\"parallel-solving\"))\n  {\n    /* NOTE: I would love to use std::for_each here, but it is not giving\n       * the result I would expect. \"\\033[32m\" : \"\";\n  const std::string RED = is_color ? \"\\033[31m\" : \"\";\n  const std::string RESET = is_color ? \"\\033[0m\" : \"\";\n\n  // Build the properties summary string with colors\n  std::ostringstream properties_oss;\n  properties_oss << \"Properties: \" << summary.total_properties << \" verified\";\n\n  if (summary.passed_properties > 0)\n    properties_oss << \" \" << GREEN << \"✓ \" << summary.passed_properties\n                   << \" passed\" << RESET;\n\n  if (summary.skipped_properties > 0)\n    properties_oss << \", \" << GREEN << \"✓ \" << summary.skipped_properties\n                   << \" skipped\" << RESET;\n\n  if (summary.failed_properties > 0)\n    properties_oss << \", \" << RED << \"✗ \" << summary.failed_properties\n                   << \" failed\" << RESET;\n\n  if (summary.unknown_properties > 0)\n  {\n    const std::string YELLOW = is_color ? \"\\033[33m\" : \"\";\n    properties_oss << \", \" << YELLOW << \"? \" << summary.unknown_properties\n                   << \" unknown\" << RESET;\n  }\n\n  // Build the timing summary string\n  double avg_time = summary.total_properties > 0\n                      ? summary.total_time_s / summary.total_properties\n                      : 0.0;\n\n  std::ostringstream timing_oss;\n  timing_oss << \"Solver: \" << summary.solver_name\n             << \" • Decision procedure total time: \"\n             << time2string(summary.total_time_s) << \"s\"\n             << \" • Avg: \" << std::fixed << std::setprecision(1)\n             << time2string(avg_time) << \"s/property\";\n\n  // Output the summary\n  log_result(\"{}\", properties_oss.str());\n  log_result(\"{}\", timing_oss.str());","numLines":1110,"startLine":2600,"totalLines":3710}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"c7086e96-e0aa-43fb-b3b2-b9fe3ee4d4b8","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/samson/workspace/paper_review","sessionId":"e0047351-2714-4000-919d-058ca8af97c5","version":"2.1.220","gitBranch":"VeriPUT","slug":"synchronous-wondering-flame"}

{"parentUuid":"8e6a1612-2325-4538-8792-420497584406","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"5772ac7f-0a12-45f7-b1aa-0a2240fdfc37","agentId":"a17eb698d5961ee20","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FFs5Wx8NcEDmDcSy6PZGXb","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t// Stage-2 CERTIFICATION QUERY — direction one: a box INSIDE the path's domain\n2\t// must certify.\n3\t//\n4\t// One decision, so `f` has exactly two paths:\n5\t//   enc=2, depth=1  -> the `a > 10` branch (guard value 0)\n6\t//   enc=3, depth=1  -> the fall-through    (guard value 1)\n7\t// `payable`, so no ABI value gate is synthesised and msg.value need not be\n8\t// bounded — one interval over one input is the smallest shape in which the\n9\t// query can be wrong.\n10\t//\n11\t// The query is `assume(box); assert(tr == enc && cnt == depth)`, asserted at\n12\t// EVERY exit of the unit. That placement is the whole point: an input inside\n13\t// the box that walks the OTHER path leaves through the other exit, so with the\n14\t// assert on this path's own exit alone it would never be checked and the query\n15\t// would hold vacuously — permanently green in the one place where green has to\n16\t// mean something.\n17\t//\n18\t// PASSING THIS TEST ON ITS OWN IS NOT EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING. An implementation\n19\t// that checks nothing at all also reports SUCCESSFUL here. What this half\n20\t// establishes is only that the check does not fire ALWAYS; the `_straddles`\n21\t// twin establishes that it fires at all. The test is the PAIR, and the property\n22\t// being tested is that the two verdicts are consistently OPPOSITE. Deleting\n23\t// either half leaves something that still looks like it is protecting\n24\t// something and is not.\n25\t//\n26\t// exit0 (this path's own exit) PASSES in both halves; only exit1 (the other\n27\t// path's exit) flips. So the wrong implementation — asserting on this path's\n28\t// exit alone — is precisely the run in which the pair comes out all green.\n29\t//\n30\t// This is also why neither half needs fault injection: the check comes with a\n31\t// direction that MUST flip. A detector that has no such direction (the exit\n32\t// census, the decision-set census: they never fire on a correct run) cannot\n33\t// testify for itself and has to be injected. One-directional detectors need\n34\t// injection; a detector carrying its own must-flip control does not.\n35\t//\n36\t// The certify spec `cert.json` is read-only: the tool never writes it back, so\n37\t// this fixture cannot be polluted by the run that consumes it (the discipline\n38\t// that came out of the cross-run covered-set fixture).\n39\tpragma solidity ^0.8.0;\n40\t\n41\tcontract Box {\n42\t    function f(uint256 a) external payable returns (uint256) {\n43\t        if (a > 10) {\n44\t            return 1;\n45\t        }\n46\t        return 0;\n47\t    }\n48\t}\n49\t"}]},"uuid":"2f59d7b3-9a5d-4332-a826-42b3644fab44","timestamp":"2026-07-30T17:50:30.188Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/samson/workspace/esbmc/regression/esbmc-solidity/solidity_path_cov_certify_box_inside/contract.sol","content":"// Stage-2 CERTIFICATION QUERY — direction one: a box INSIDE the path's domain\n// must certify.\n//\n// One decision, so `f` has exactly two paths:\n//   enc=2, depth=1  -> the `a > 10` branch (guard value 0)\n//   enc=3, depth=1  -> the fall-through    (guard value 1)\n// `payable`, so no ABI value gate is synthesised and msg.value need not be\n// bounded — one interval over one input is the smallest shape in which the\n// query can be wrong.\n//\n// The query is `assume(box); assert(tr == enc && cnt == depth)`, asserted at\n// EVERY exit of the unit. That placement is the whole point: an input inside\n// the box that walks the OTHER path leaves through the other exit, so with the\n// assert on this path's own exit alone it would never be checked and the query\n// would hold vacuously — permanently green in the one place where green has to\n// mean something.\n//\n// PASSING THIS TEST ON ITS OWN IS NOT EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING. An implementation\n// that checks nothing at all also reports SUCCESSFUL here. What this half\n// establishes is only that the check does not fire ALWAYS; the `_straddles`\n// twin establishes that it fires at all. The test is the PAIR, and the property\n// being tested is that the two verdicts are consistently OPPOSITE. Deleting\n// either half leaves something that still looks like it is protecting\n// something and is not.\n//\n// exit0 (this path's own exit) PASSES in both halves; only exit1 (the other\n// path's exit) flips. So the wrong implementation — asserting on this path's\n// exit alone — is precisely the run in which the pair comes out all green.\n//\n// This is also why neither half needs fault injection: the check comes with a\n// direction that MUST flip. A detector that has no such direction (the exit\n// census, the decision-set census: they never fire on a correct run) cannot\n// testify for itself and has to be injected. One-directional detectors need\n// injection; a detector carrying its own must-flip control does not.\n//\n// The certify spec `cert.json` is read-only: the tool never writes it back, so\n// this fixture cannot be polluted by the run that consumes it (the discipline\n// that came out of the cross-run covered-set fixture).\npragma solidity ^0.8.0;\n\ncontract Box {\n    function f(uint256 a) external payable returns (uint256) {\n        if (a > 10) {\n            return 1;\n        }\n        return 0;\n    }\n}\n","numLines":49,"startLine":1,"totalLines":49}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"8e6a1612-2325-4538-8792-420497584406","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/samson/workspace/paper_review","sessionId":"e0047351-2714-4000-919d-058ca8af97c5","version":"2.1.220","gitBranch":"VeriPUT","slug":"synchronous-wondering-flame"}
